title: Tshisekedi calls for cooperation between provincial institutions amid recurring governance tensions

title_en: Tshisekedi calls for cooperation between provincial institutions amid recurring governance tensions
excerpt_en: Bandundu March 25, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has urged stronger cooperation and accountability between provincial governments and provincial assemblies in the Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against institutional rivalry and political instability that continues to disrupt governance at
body_en:
Bandundu March 25, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has urged stronger cooperation and accountability between provincial governments and provincial assemblies in the Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against institutional rivalry and political instability that continues to disrupt governance at the provincial level.

Speaking at the opening of the 13th Conference of Governors held on March 24 in Bandundu (Kwilu Province), the Head of State stressed that decentralization was intended to bring governance closer to citizens, not to create competing or paralyzed institutions.

He emphasized that provincial oversight by assemblies is legitimate and necessary in a democracy, but warned it should not be used for political pressure, personal interests, or actions that undermine public service delivery.

“The provinces need institutions that cooperate, respect each other, and hold each other accountable within the framework of the law,” President Tshisekedi said, adding that institutional balance is essential for effective governance and development.

He noted that persistent conflicts between provincial executives and assemblies have repeatedly undermined policy implementation, particularly in key sectors such as agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and rural development.

According to the President, no serious development agenda can succeed in an environment marked by political instability, institutional confrontation, or unclear division of responsibilities.

The speech comes against a backdrop of recurring tensions since the 2006 Constitution established decentralization, with provinces frequently experiencing disputes over governance, oversight, and leadership accountability.

Government officials have previously attempted to curb instability, including directives from the Interior Ministry aimed at temporarily suspending motions and petitions in provincial assemblies to restore order during periods of heightened political tension.

title: CENCO warns constitutional revision is possible but risky amid DRC’s security crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has stated that while revising the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo is legally possible, it would be risky under the country’s current security and political conditions.
title_en: CENCO warns constitutional revision is possible but risky amid DRC’s security crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has stated that while revising the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo is legally possible, it would be risky under the country’s current security and political conditions.
body_en:
Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has stated that while revising the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo is legally possible, it would be risky under the country’s current security and political conditions.

Speaking during a press conference following its extraordinary plenary session held from March 23 to 25 in Kinshasa, CENCO leaders expressed concern over worsening insecurity, persistent instability, and a deepening humanitarian crisis affecting the population.

CENCO Secretary General Donatien Nshole reiterated the Church’s position that constitutional revision is allowed under existing legal procedures, but warned that opening such a process in the current climate could be dangerous due to lack of national consensus.

He stressed that the Constitution already outlines which provisions can or cannot be revised, and insisted that any reform process must be carefully managed to avoid further political tension.

The remarks come amid an ongoing national debate over possible constitutional changes, with supporters arguing that the 2006 Constitution no longer reflects current governance realities, while critics warn that reform efforts could be used for political advantage, including the removal of presidential term limits.

Opposition figures and civil society groups have raised concerns that such changes could extend the current president’s tenure beyond 2028, while the ruling camp maintains that reforms are needed to improve state efficiency.

CENCO called for caution and dialogue, emphasizing that any constitutional process must take place in a stable and consensual environment to avoid deepening existing national divisions.

title: AfDB pledges $80 million to support long-delayed national census in the DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa March 25, 2026 - The African Development Bank (AfDB) has committed $80 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-2), a major statistical exercise aimed at updating national demographic data nearly four decades after the last cen
title_en: AfDB pledges $80 million to support long-delayed national census in the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 25, 2026 - The African Development Bank (AfDB) has committed $80 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-2), a major statistical exercise aimed at updating national demographic data nearly four decades after the last cen
body_en:
Kinshasa March 25, 2026 - The African Development Bank (AfDB) has committed $80 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-2), a major statistical exercise aimed at updating national demographic data nearly four decades after the last census.

The announcement was made during a donor roundtable focused on mobilizing financing for the nationwide operation, which the government estimates will cost around $192 million in total.

According to AfDB officials, the pledged funding will be split into two components: $50 million dedicated to field operations and $30 million to strengthen national statistical institutions, including the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and other agencies involved in planning, budgeting, and monitoring.

The AfDB described the initiative as a “historic” step for the country, noting its experience in supporting large-scale statistical operations across Africa. The institution also indicated that additional funding could be considered pending internal approval.

The Congolese government is seeking to establish a “basket fund” mechanism to pool contributions from multiple development partners in order to ensure coordinated and transparent financing of the census process.

Authorities say the census is critical for improving development planning, reducing inequalities, and supporting progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are approaching the 2030 deadline.

The last full population census in the DRC dates back to 1984, leaving major gaps in demographic and socio-economic data used for national policy design.

Officials argue that the absence of reliable population data has hindered effective governance and resource allocation, making the upcoming census a key national priority and a long-standing political commitment.

title: Youssouf Ezangi extradé vers le Royaume-Uni pour purger une peine à perpétuité
excerpt: Kinshasa April 2, 2026 - British national Youssouf Ezangi, a former plumber originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo, has been extradited to the United Kingdom to serve a life sentence for his role in the May 2024 attempted coup in Kinshasa.
title_en: Youssouf Ezangi extradited to the United Kingdom to serve life sentence over 2024 DRC coup attempt
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 2, 2026 - British national Youssouf Ezangi, a former plumber originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo, has been extradited to the United Kingdom to serve a life sentence for his role in the May 2024 attempted coup in Kinshasa.
body_en:
Kinshasa April 2, 2026 - British national Youssouf Ezangi, a former plumber originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo, has been extradited to the United Kingdom to serve a life sentence for his role in the May 2024 attempted coup in Kinshasa.

Ezangi, 53 at the time of the events, was transferred from Ndolo Military Prison on March 31, 2026, under a judicial cooperation arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United Kingdom. His handover was carried out in the presence of diplomatic and military officials, including representatives of the British Embassy in Kinshasa.

He had been convicted by military courts for armed violence and terrorism-related offences linked to the failed coup attempt led by Christian Malanga on May 19, 2024. Initially sentenced to death, his punishment was later commuted to life imprisonment following a presidential pardon.

According to judicial proceedings, Ezangi was part of a group that entered key state locations in Kinshasa, including the residence of senior officials and the Palais de la Nation, during the short-lived assault on state institutions.

The extradition was formally approved as part of bilateral legal cooperation between Kinshasa and London, with authorities describing the transfer as a continuation of judicial enforcement rather than a release from accountability.

During the trial, Ezangi reportedly stated he first met Malanga in London in 2016 and later reconnected with him in several African countries before the 2024 operation. He claimed he was not fully aware of the objectives of the mission, though prosecutors linked him to the armed group that attempted to seize strategic sites in the capital.

The 2024 coup attempt, which briefly shook Kinshasa, resulted in multiple convictions of both Congolese and foreign nationals. Among those previously transferred abroad were American citizens, including Marcel Malanga, and Belgian-Congolese academic Jean-Jacques Wondo, who were also handed life sentences after being extradited to serve their terms in their home countries.

Authorities say Ezangi’s transfer leaves only a small number of foreign-linked detainees still held in the DRC in connection with the failed coup.

title: Kinshasa court sentences doctor to suspended term in assault case involving patient video
excerpt: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Kinkole High Court has sentenced Dr. David Balanganayi to two months of penal servitude, suspended for one year, in a case stemming from a widely circulated video showing him physically assaulting a patient.
title_en: Kinshasa court sentences doctor to suspended term in assault case involving patient video
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Kinkole High Court has sentenced Dr. David Balanganayi to two months of penal servitude, suspended for one year, in a case stemming from a widely circulated video showing him physically assaulting a patient.
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Kinkole High Court has sentenced Dr. David Balanganayi to two months of penal servitude, suspended for one year, in a case stemming from a widely circulated video showing him physically assaulting a patient.

The judgment, delivered on Friday, found the doctor guilty of simple assault and battery after reclassifying the initial charge of aggravated assault and battery. The court, however, dismissed accusations of torture and the publication of a criminal act, ruling that the evidence did not support those charges.

Under the suspended sentence, Dr. Balanganayi will avoid immediate imprisonment but will remain under probation for one year. Any further offense during this period would trigger enforcement of the custodial sentence.

In its civil ruling, the court ordered the state, held civilly liable, to pay compensation totaling 6 million Congolese francs to the plaintiffs, identified as Kidimba Kongolo Jean and Moya Dorcas.

The case, which has drawn significant public attention in recent days in Kinshasa, began after a video surfaced online showing a medical professional striking a patient, triggering widespread outrage on social media.

Public reaction intensified after First Lady Denise Nyakeru Tshisekedi publicly condemned the incident, calling for accountability.

During his defense, the doctor argued that his use of force was intended to compel the patient to accept treatment in a situation he described as critical, claiming it was aimed at saving her life.

title: Accord de Washington - mise en oeuvre à 27,5% malgré des progrès sécuritaires limités
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The implementation of the Washington Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda has recorded modest progress, rising from 23.3% to 27.5% by the end of March 2026, according to a recent assessment report.
title_en: Washington Agreement: Implementation Reaches 27.5% Amid Limited Security Progress
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The implementation of the Washington Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda has recorded modest progress, rising from 23.3% to 27.5% by the end of March 2026, according to a recent assessment report.
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The implementation of the Washington Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda has recorded modest progress, rising from 23.3% to 27.5% by the end of March 2026, according to a recent assessment report.

The evaluation, published on April 6 by the African Peace Agreements Barometer, marks the first notable increase after several months of stagnation observed between November 2025 and February 2026. The report attributes this improvement primarily to the activation of key security commitments, notably initial steps toward the neutralization of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR).

Overall, 21 out of the 30 tasks предусмотрed under the agreement have been launched at varying levels of implementation, representing 70% of planned actions. However, the cumulative score stands at 82.5 out of a possible 300, reflecting a relatively low overall execution rate. When considering only partially implemented tasks, the rate reaches 39.2%.

Despite this progress, the report highlights that implementation of critical security measures remains limited. Activities related to the planning, identification, and positioning of FDLR elements have achieved moderate scores, but actual military neutralization efforts remain minimal.

Humanitarian components of the agreement-including civilian protection, assistance to vulnerable populations, and the return of displaced persons and refugees-also show very low levels of implementation, underscoring ongoing challenges on the ground.

An analysis of national commitments indicates that the Democratic Republic of Congo has partially implemented 18 of the 26 tasks under its responsibility, corresponding to an overall rate of 26%. Rwanda, for its part, has partially completed 14 of its 22 assigned tasks, reaching an implementation rate of 23.8%. When focusing solely on tasks already underway, both countries show similar progress levels.

The report notes that, despite renewed diplomatic engagement and high-level backing of the agreement, including support from international partners, tangible improvements in the security situation remain limited. Mutual accusations between Kinshasa and Kigali over alleged violations continue to undermine trust and slow progress.

Parallel mediation efforts, including talks held in Doha between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 rebellion, have also seen little advancement. These discussions, intended to complement the Washington framework by addressing deeper structural causes of the conflict, remain largely stalled.

title: DRC National Assembly Advances Ratification of Strategic US Partnership and Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two key bills concerning the ratification of a strategic partnership with the United States and a peace agreement with Rwanda, marking a significant step in the country’s diplomatic and secur
title_en: DRC National Assembly Advances Ratification of Strategic US Partnership and Rwanda Peace Agreement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two key bills concerning the ratification of a strategic partnership with the United States and a peace agreement with Rwanda, marking a significant step in the country’s diplomatic and secur
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two key bills concerning the ratification of a strategic partnership with the United States and a peace agreement with Rwanda, marking a significant step in the country’s diplomatic and security agenda.

The two texts were presented on April 13 and subsequently referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee for expedited review, which has been given 24 hours to submit its report.

The agreements were defended before parliament by Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, who outlined the scope and objectives of the initiatives.

The first agreement establishes a strategic partnership between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, covering cooperation in critical minerals, energy, infrastructure development, and security coordination. According to the government, the framework includes joint monitoring mechanisms while explicitly reaffirming respect for national sovereignty.

The second agreement relates to a peace accord signed on June 27, 2025, between the DRC and Rwanda. It seeks to end hostilities, ensure respect for territorial integrity, support the disengagement of armed forces, and establish a joint security coordination mechanism aimed at promoting long-term stability in the Great Lakes region.

During parliamentary deliberations, several deputies stressed the importance of transparency and strict oversight in the implementation of both agreements, particularly regarding commitments made by all parties involved.

Debate was concluded following the adoption of an incidental motion by MP Pierre Sumeyi, who noted that key opposition figures, including Célestin Musao of the Ensemble et Alliés parliamentary group and Gratien de Saint-Nicolas Iracan, had already expressed support for the agreements, making further debate unnecessary at that stage.

The admissibility vote represents an early but important legislative step in the ratification process, with further committee scrutiny expected before final parliamentary approval.

title: Kikwit Military Court Opens Trial of Armed Gang Leader on Terrorism Charges
excerpt: Kikwit, April 8, 2026 - A military court in Kikwit has opened proceedings against an alleged armed gang leader and several of his accomplices, who are facing charges including terrorism and armed robbery.
title_en: Kikwit Military Court Opens Trial of Armed Gang Leader on Terrorism Charges
excerpt_en: Kikwit, April 8, 2026 - A military court in Kikwit has opened proceedings against an alleged armed gang leader and several of his accomplices, who are facing charges including terrorism and armed robbery.
body_en:
Kikwit, April 8, 2026 - A military court in Kikwit has opened proceedings against an alleged armed gang leader and several of his accomplices, who are facing charges including terrorism and armed robbery.

The trial began on Tuesday, April 7, before the Kikwit garrison military court in an exceptional sitting held in a newly inaugurated courtroom.

At the center of the case is Aaron Kikalula Kanda, also known as “Nija,” who prosecutors describe as the leader of a criminal group operating in the Kazamba commune. He is accused of orchestrating violent attacks against civilians during two incidents reported on March 1 and March 30.

According to the prosecution, the group carried out daytime raids that resulted in looting and left several residents injured. The defendants are being prosecuted on multiple counts, including armed robbery and acts classified as terrorism under military law.

During the opening session, the court formally identified the accused and outlined the procedural schedule. A mobile court hearing is also planned in Kazamba, near the affected area, to allow closer examination of evidence and witness testimonies.

Several victims, including elderly residents affected by the attacks, attended the hearing and indicated their willingness to testify during the proceedings.

Authorities say the case reflects ongoing efforts to strengthen accountability and respond to armed violence affecting civilian populations in the region.

title: UN Reports Detention of Over 40 Opposition Members
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The United Nations has raised concerns over the detention of dozens of political opposition members in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a report released on April 6 by its Joint Human Rights Office.
title_en: UN Reports Detention of Over 40 Opposition Members
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The United Nations has raised concerns over the detention of dozens of political opposition members in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a report released on April 6 by its Joint Human Rights Office.
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The United Nations has raised concerns over the detention of dozens of political opposition members in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a report released on April 6 by its Joint Human Rights Office.

The report indicates that at least 42 individuals, including members of opposition parties, have been arrested since January 2026 by intelligence services and the military justice system. Many are affiliated with the Ensemble pour la République party of exiled opposition figure Moïse Katumbi and the PPRD of former President Joseph Kabila.

According to the findings, several detainees are being held at Ndolo military prison in Kinshasa, while others are reportedly detained in unofficial facilities allegedly operated by the National Cyber Defense Council (CNC), an institution that has faced criticism over alleged human rights abuses.

Among those arrested in January were senior members of the PPRD, including Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, Aubin Minaku, and Dunia Kilanga. They were apprehended at their residences in operations involving both uniformed and plainclothes personnel.

The report notes that many of the detainees have been held incommunicado, without access to legal counsel or judicial proceedings, raising concerns over due process and adherence to legal standards.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa/New York, April 12, 2026 - As the race for the next United Nations Secretary-General begins to take shape, former Senegalese President Macky Sall has outlined his vision for global leadership, placing particular emphasis on strengthening Africa’s voice in international decision-making and a
body_en:
Kinshasa/New York, April 12, 2026 - As the race for the next United Nations Secretary-General begins to take shape, former Senegalese President Macky Sall has outlined his vision for global leadership, placing particular emphasis on strengthening Africa’s voice in international decision-making and addressing insecurity in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The diplomatic engagement took place during a meeting at the Permanent Mission of the DRC to the United Nations, where he was received by Ambassador Zénon Mukongo Ngay. The discussion formed part of early consultations ahead of the selection process for the next UN Secretary-General, whose mandate is set to begin on January 1, 2027, following the end of António Guterres’ tenure.

In his message, Macky Sall recalled recent discussions in Kinshasa with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, during which he sought support for his candidacy and underscored the strategic importance of the DRC in continental and global affairs.

He stressed the need for a more balanced global economic order, improved access to international financing for developing countries, and stronger multilateral cooperation at a time of rising geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

A central point of his remarks was the security situation in eastern DRC. He pledged that, if elected, he would prioritize efforts to address the crisis, which he attributed to the involvement of external actors, while calling for renewed trust between states, respect for sovereignty, and strengthened regional peace mechanisms.

The comments come as the United Nations formalizes its selection process for the next Secretary-General, which includes the submission of candidatures by member states, publication of candidate vision statements, and a series of public interactive dialogues broadcast globally.

Several high-profile candidates have already been nominated, including international figures such as Michelle Bachelet, Rafael Grossi, and Rebeca Grynspan, alongside Macky Sall.

The process, governed by UN transparency guidelines, is expected to intensify in the coming months as member states engage in consultations ahead of the 2027 leadership transition.

title: African Group at the UN Holds Strategic Retreat under Mali’s Leadership
excerpt: New York, March 29-30, 2026 - Ambassadors of the African Group to the United Nations convened in New York for a high-level strategic retreat aimed at strengthening coordination and advancing the continent’s priorities within the UN system.
title_en: African Group at the UN Holds Strategic Retreat under Mali’s Leadership
excerpt_en: New York, March 29-30, 2026 - Ambassadors of the African Group to the United Nations convened in New York for a high-level strategic retreat aimed at strengthening coordination and advancing the continent’s priorities within the UN system.
body_en:
New York, March 29-30, 2026 - Ambassadors of the African Group to the United Nations convened in New York for a high-level strategic retreat aimed at strengthening coordination and advancing the continent’s priorities within the UN system.

The meeting was chaired by Issa Konfourou, Ambassador and Permanent Representative of Mali to the United Nations, who held the presidency of the African Group for the month of March. The retreat was attended by the UN Secretary-General, António Guterres, as well as the Deputy Secretary-General, underscoring the significance of the gathering.

Held under the theme “Strengthening the Role of African Actors within the United Nations System: Challenges and Opportunities,” the discussions focused on enhancing Africa’s collective influence on key global issues and promoting a unified approach to the continent’s strategic interests.

In his opening remarks, Ambassador Konfourou stressed the importance of Africa’s active engagement in ongoing UN reform processes. He also highlighted the need to advance resolutions that secure adequate financing for African priorities, with the goal of fostering balanced and sustainable development across the continent.

Participants emphasized the importance of a coordinated and forward-looking African stance, particularly in view of upcoming milestones such as the selection of the next UN Secretary-General, critical budget negotiations, and broader institutional reforms.

The retreat concluded with a renewed commitment to unity and strategic alignment, reflecting what participants described as a consensus-driven leadership approach under Mali’s stewardship.

excerpt_en: Bamako, April 7, 2026 - Mali has expressed appreciation for its cooperation with the European Union’s civilian security mission following the end of tenure of the Head of EUCAP Sahel Mali.

Bamako, April 7, 2026 - Mali has expressed appreciation for its cooperation with the European Union’s civilian security mission following the end of tenure of the Head of EUCAP Sahel Mali.

The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, Mamoudou Kassogué, received Mr. Peter Kolding in a formal farewell audience marking the conclusion of his mandate.

The meeting provided an opportunity for the Malian authorities to review what they described as an “excellent partnership” with the EUCAP Sahel Mali, particularly in supporting the modernization of judicial infrastructure and strengthening the capacities of justice sector actors.

Officials highlighted the mission’s contribution to reinforcing the rule of law and improving the resilience of Mali’s justice system through technical and institutional support.

In recognition of his work, Minister Kassogué presented Mr. Kolding with an artistic Ciwara, a traditional Malian symbol representing courage, effort, and excellence, as a tribute to his service and commitment during his tenure.

The ceremony underscored what both sides described as a sustained partnership built on cooperation, mutual respect, and shared objectives in support of peace and justice in Mali.

excerpt: Rabat, March 31 - April 2, 2026 - Mali and Morocco have taken a further step toward strengthening bilateral relations following a diplomatic exchange mission held in Rabat, focused on capacity-building and institutional cooperation.
title_en: Mali and Morocco Deepen Diplomatic Cooperation Through Exchange Mission in Rabat
excerpt_en: Rabat, March 31 - April 2, 2026 - Mali and Morocco have taken a further step toward strengthening bilateral relations following a diplomatic exchange mission held in Rabat, focused on capacity-building and institutional cooperation.
body_en:
Rabat, March 31 - April 2, 2026 - Mali and Morocco have taken a further step toward strengthening bilateral relations following a diplomatic exchange mission held in Rabat, focused on capacity-building and institutional cooperation.

The Malian delegation, drawn from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, was led by Mahamane Amadou Maïga, Chargé d’Affaires. The visit formed part of a broader initiative to promote the exchange of expertise and best practices in diplomacy.

During the mission, Malian officials held discussions with senior representatives of Morocco’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation, and Moroccans Living Abroad. The talks were described as constructive and centered on enhancing diplomatic performance, strengthening institutional frameworks, and fostering closer collaboration.

Key Moroccan institutions participated in the exchange, including the Moroccan Institute for Diplomatic Training, Research, and Studies, the Directorate of Public Diplomacy and Non-State Actors, and the Moroccan Agency for International Cooperation. These engagements provided a platform for sharing experiences in diplomatic training, public diplomacy strategies, and international cooperation mechanisms.

The mission reflects ongoing efforts by Mali and Morocco to deepen their partnership, with a particular focus on building institutional capacity and expanding cooperation in key areas of diplomacy.

title: Dakar Forum: Mali Highlights Sovereignty and Regional Integration at High-Level Security Talks
excerpt: Dakar, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, co-chaired a key plenary session at the Dakar International Forum on Peace and Security in Africa, focusing on the evolving concept of sovereignty in a changing global landscape.

excerpt_en: Dakar, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, co-chaired a key plenary session at the Dakar International Forum on Peace and Security in Africa, focusing on the evolving concept of sovereignty in a changing global landscape.
body_en:
Dakar, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, co-chaired a key plenary session at the Dakar International Forum on Peace and Security in Africa, focusing on the evolving concept of sovereignty in a changing global landscape.

The session, held on Monday under the theme “Sovereignty and Contemporary Challenges: Africa Between Perils and Opportunities,” brought together policymakers and experts to examine how African states can navigate growing geopolitical pressures while safeguarding national interests.

In his opening remarks, Minister Diop stressed that the question of sovereignty has become central for both major powers and more vulnerable nations, particularly in a context marked by global uncertainty and shifting international dynamics.

He emphasized that national sovereignty should not be seen in opposition to collective approaches. In this regard, he pointed to the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) as an example of a framework where member states seek to reconcile national sovereignty with a broader form of collective sovereignty.

According to Diop, such regional mechanisms aim to strengthen integration through coordinated efforts in defense, diplomacy, and development, offering a strategic response to shared challenges across the Sahel.

The discussions at the forum underscored the growing importance of regional cooperation as African countries seek to balance independence with collective resilience in an increasingly complex international environment.

title: Plainte contre le Mali devant la Cour africaine pour abus présumés
excerpt: April 20, 2026 - Three international human rights organizations have filed a complaint against Mali before the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights, alleging serious violations committed during military operations in the country’s central regions.
title_en: Complaint Filed Against Mali Before African Court Over Alleged Abuses
excerpt_en: April 20, 2026 - Three international human rights organizations have filed a complaint against Mali before the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights, alleging serious violations committed during military operations in the country’s central regions.
body_en:
April 20, 2026 - Three international human rights organizations have filed a complaint against Mali before the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights, alleging serious violations committed during military operations in the country’s central regions.

The complaint was submitted by Trial International, the African Union of Lawyers, and the International Federation for Human Rights. It focuses on events that reportedly took place in 2022 in the localities of Hombori and Moura, where hundreds of civilians are alleged to have been killed.

According to the organizations, the case raises concerns over the protection of civilians during counterinsurgency operations, as well as allegations of obstruction of justice and the absence of accountability for those responsible.

The applicants argue that the proceedings aim not only to address the specific incidents but also to establish a broader legal precedent regarding state responsibility, particularly in contexts where private or allied military actors are involved in security operations.

Malian authorities have not yet publicly responded to the complaint.

The case is expected to draw significant attention at the continental level, as it touches on key issues related to human rights, accountability, and the conduct of military operations in conflict-affected environments.

excerpt: Dakar, April 15-17, 2026 - The Senegalese capital hosted a high-level international conference focused on the universalization of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), held in conjunction with discussions linked to the Hague Conference on Private International Law.
title_en: Dakar Conference on International Law: African States Push for Stronger Global Legal Cooperation
excerpt_en: Dakar, April 15-17, 2026 - The Senegalese capital hosted a high-level international conference focused on the universalization of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), held in conjunction with discussions linked to the Hague Conference on Private International Law.
body_en:
Dakar, April 15-17, 2026 - The Senegalese capital hosted a high-level international conference focused on the universalization of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), held in conjunction with discussions linked to the Hague Conference on Private International Law.

The meeting took place under the high patronage of the President of Senegal, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, and brought together representatives from 17 African states, including Mali, Morocco, Rwanda, Egypt, Mauritius, Cameroon, and the Comoros.

Regional and international organizations also took part in the proceedings, notably the African Union, ECOWAS, and OHADA, underscoring the continental dimension of the discussions on international legal cooperation.

Three Ministers of Justice from Senegal, Madagascar, and the Comoros participated directly in the sessions, alongside senior officials from international institutions, including the Secretary General of the Permanent Court of Arbitration and representatives of the Hague Conference on Private International Law, based in the Netherlands.

Mali was represented by the Secretary General of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Dr. Boubacar Sidiki Diarrah, who took part in the deliberations on behalf of the Minister of Justice.

His participation reflects Mali’s commitment to strengthening its engagement in international legal cooperation frameworks and expanding its role in global dispute resolution mechanisms.

The conference highlighted growing African interest in reinforcing legal certainty, improving access to arbitration mechanisms, and deepening cooperation between African states and international legal institutions.

title: AES Media Regulation Initiative Gains Momentum as Mali Hosts Niger Delegation

title_en: AES Media Regulation Initiative Gains Momentum as Mali Hosts Niger Delegation
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 15, 2026 - Mali’s Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on Wednesday received a high-level delegation from Niger led by Ibrahim Manzo Diallo, President of the National Communication Observatory (ONC), as regional efforts to coordinate media regulation within the Sahel intensif
body_en:
Bamako, April 15, 2026 - Mali’s Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on Wednesday received a high-level delegation from Niger led by Ibrahim Manzo Diallo, President of the National Communication Observatory (ONC), as regional efforts to coordinate media regulation within the Sahel intensify.

The visit forms part of a broader diplomatic and technical mission aimed at laying the groundwork for a joint platform dedicated to media oversight across member states of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).

At the center of discussions was the proposed establishment of a joint regulatory framework designed to harmonize communication policies and strengthen collective resilience against what officials described as a growing global information war targeting the region.

The Nigerien delegation emphasized the need for coordinated action, calling for stronger institutional collaboration among AES countries. The initiative seeks to pool resources and align strategies in order to better manage information flows and counter external influence campaigns.

As part of this effort, the ONC President appealed for the support of Mali’s transitional authorities to advance the project, noting that initial steps toward implementation are already underway. The regional tour is expected to continue in Burkina Faso, where similar consultations are planned.

Prime Minister Maïga welcomed the initiative, stating that it aligns with the broader vision underpinning the Confederation of Sahel States. He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting the project and expressed confidence in its potential to evolve into a fully operational regional mechanism.

The meeting underscores the increasing priority placed by AES member states on information governance, as they seek to reinforce sovereignty and cooperation in the face of shared communication and security challenges.

title: Djibouti, World Bank Sign $36.5 Million Deal to Boost Water Access
excerpt: Djibouti, March 31, 2026 (ADI) - The Republic of Djibouti has signed a partnership agreement with the World Bank aimed at improving access to drinking water and strengthening resilience to drought, officials said Tuesday.
title_en: Djibouti, World Bank Sign $36.5 Million Deal to Boost Water Access
excerpt_en: Djibouti, March 31, 2026 (ADI) - The Republic of Djibouti has signed a partnership agreement with the World Bank aimed at improving access to drinking water and strengthening resilience to drought, officials said Tuesday.
body_en:
Djibouti, March 31, 2026 (ADI) - The Republic of Djibouti has signed a partnership agreement with the World Bank aimed at improving access to drinking water and strengthening resilience to drought, officials said Tuesday.

The agreement, signed in Djibouti City, was attended by Minister of Economy and Finance Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh and the World Bank’s representative in the country, Fatou Fall. It marks a new phase in cooperation between Djibouti and the institution on water security challenges.

Under the deal, funding of approximately 6.5 billion Djiboutian francs (around $36.5 million) will be allocated to priority projects, with the goal of increasing national drinking water coverage to 98% by 2030. Djibouti, a country frequently affected by water scarcity, has identified access to water as a key development priority.

“This agreement reflects the commitment of the highest authorities to act swiftly in the face of water-related challenges, which constitute a national priority,” Dawaleh said, noting that the initiative aligns with the strategic vision of President Ismail Omar Guelleh.

He also praised the World Bank’s continued support for Djibouti’s development, particularly in infrastructure and essential public services.

For her part, Fatou Fall reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to supporting national efforts to expand access to water. “This partnership aims to sustainably improve living conditions and strengthen resilience to the effects of drought,” she said.

The agreement is part of the broader Djibouti ICI National Development Program, which prioritizes improvements in water services with the backing of international technical and financial partners.

title: Djibouti Inaugurates €107 Million Shipyard to Boost Maritime Industry
excerpt: Djibouti, April 4, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, on Thursday presided over the inauguration of the Djibouti Ship Repair Yard (DSRY), a major maritime infrastructure project aimed at strengthening the country’s position as a regional shipping hub.
title_en: Djibouti Inaugurates €107 Million Shipyard to Boost Maritime Industry
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 4, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, on Thursday presided over the inauguration of the Djibouti Ship Repair Yard (DSRY), a major maritime infrastructure project aimed at strengthening the country’s position as a regional shipping hub.
body_en:
Djibouti, April 4, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, on Thursday presided over the inauguration of the Djibouti Ship Repair Yard (DSRY), a major maritime infrastructure project aimed at strengthening the country’s position as a regional shipping hub.

Developed through a partnership with Damen Shipyards Group and financed by Invest International, the project represents an investment of approximately €107.5 million.

The facility, described as the largest of its kind in the Red Sea and East Africa, includes a floating dock measuring 217 meters in length and 43 meters in width, with a lifting capacity of up to 20,100 tons. It is designed to serve vessels transiting the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the busiest shipping routes in the world.

Speaking at the ceremony, President Guelleh подчеркнул the strategic importance of the new infrastructure, highlighting Djibouti’s geographic position at the entrance to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. He noted that the country has a responsibility to provide maintenance and repair services to passing vessels, positioning the project as part of a broader national strategy for maritime and industrial development.

Beyond infrastructure, the project is expected to generate around 350 direct jobs and up to 1,400 indirect jobs, while also contributing to skills development in technical fields.

Minister of Infrastructure Hassan Houmed described the shipyard as a “strategic national lever” to enhance port competitiveness and support the growth of the blue economy. Similarly, Aboubaker Omar Hadi, head of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority, подчеркнул its role in reinforcing the country’s ambition to become a leading maritime hub under its Vision 2035 framework.

For his part, Arnout Damen, Chairman of Damen Shipyards, reaffirmed the company’s commitment to ensuring the long-term success and operational excellence of the facility.

The inauguration of the DSRY marks a significant milestone in Djibouti’s efforts to expand its maritime capabilities and strengthen its role in regional and global trade.

title: International Leaders Continue to Congratulate Guelleh After Re-election
excerpt: Djibouti, April 11-13, 2026 - Diplomatic congratulations continued to pour in for the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, following his re-election in the April 10 presidential vote.
title_en: International Leaders Continue to Congratulate Guelleh After Re-election
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 11-13, 2026 - Diplomatic congratulations continued to pour in for the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, following his re-election in the April 10 presidential vote.
body_en:
Djibouti, April 11-13, 2026 - Diplomatic congratulations continued to pour in for the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, following his re-election in the April 10 presidential vote.

According to the Presidency, numerous messages have been received from heads of state and government of “brotherly and friendly countries,” extending wishes of “success and achievement” for the new mandate.

Several leaders described the result as a “resounding victory,” attributing it to what they called strong popular support for the president’s political vision. They also commended the conduct of the election, which they characterized as transparent and reflective of national unity.

Among the earliest to react were French President Emmanuel Macron and Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, who conveyed their congratulations in separate telephone conversations with President Guelleh. Discussions reportedly also touched on regional developments in the Horn of Africa.

The Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq, was also among the first world leaders to send an official message of congratulations.

Additional messages were received from regional and international figures, including Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, who praised the electoral outcome on behalf of the African Union Commission.

In separate statements, leaders including Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Déby also extended their congratulations, highlighting continued bilateral friendship and cooperation.

Officials indicated that the messages emphasize both the scale of the victory and what they described as the Djiboutian people’s commitment to a peaceful and transparent electoral process.

title: Madagascar adopts Rwanda’s electronic tax system in revenue modernization deal
excerpt: Antananarivo / Kigali, March 30, 2026 - Madagascar has signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to adopt Rwanda’s Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, a digital tax collection and invoicing platform designed to improve revenue efficiency.
title_en: Madagascar adopts Rwanda’s electronic tax system in revenue modernization deal
excerpt_en: Antananarivo / Kigali, March 30, 2026 - Madagascar has signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to adopt Rwanda’s Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, a digital tax collection and invoicing platform designed to improve revenue efficiency.
body_en:
Antananarivo / Kigali, March 30, 2026 - Madagascar has signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to adopt Rwanda’s Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, a digital tax collection and invoicing platform designed to improve revenue efficiency.

The agreement was formalized during a visit by Malagasy tax officials to Kigali, where they also received technical training on the system’s implementation and operation.

RRA Commissioner General Ronald Niwenshuti said the EBM system has significantly improved tax compliance in Rwanda, particularly in value-added tax collection.

He noted that the technology has attracted interest from several African countries seeking to modernize their tax systems and strengthen public revenue management.

Madagascar’s tax authority chief, Edmond Rafaralahy, said the country aims to replicate Rwanda’s success, describing the system as a model of effective digital governance.

Officials say Madagascar will be supported by Rwandan firm QT Global in the rollout of the technology.

Rwanda introduced EBM in 2013 as part of broader tax reforms that have since expanded to near-universal adoption among VAT-registered businesses, with authorities crediting the system for improved compliance and increased revenue collection.

The partnership highlights growing regional cooperation in digital public finance systems across Africa.

title: Rwanda justice minister calls for end to government legal losses
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, has said that government court losses must be eliminated entirely, despite improvements in the state’s legal performance.
title_en: Rwanda justice minister calls for end to government legal losses
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, has said that government court losses must be eliminated entirely, despite improvements in the state’s legal performance.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, has said that government court losses must be eliminated entirely, despite improvements in the state’s legal performance.

Speaking during a training session for government legal advisors, Ugirashebuja noted that the state had lost 27 cases between 2020 and 2023, representing about 9% of cases, resulting in financial losses estimated at nearly 1 billion Rwandan francs.

He emphasized that while the government has achieved a 91% success rate in litigation, the remaining losses remain unacceptable and must be fully addressed.

The minister attributed many of the losses to weaknesses in contract preparation and implementation, calling for stricter monitoring of public agreements and improved legal oversight.

Officials say efforts are underway to strengthen contract management systems and reduce disputes that lead to court cases involving government institutions.

Ugirashebuja also praised ongoing training programs for legal advisors, saying they are key to improving accountability and reducing future litigation risks.

excerpt_en: Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security Vincent Biruta has been received by President Denis Sassou Nguesso, to whom he delivered a message from President Paul Kagame during an official visit.

According to officials, the message from President Kagame conveyed congratulations to Sassou N’Guesso following his recent electoral victory, in which he secured another presidential term after the March 15, 2026 elections.

The talks also touched on regional diplomatic developments, including Rwanda’s support for the candidacy of Louise Mushikiwabo for leadership of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), as Kigali continues to rally support ahead of upcoming internal voting processes.

Beyond diplomatic messaging, both sides reviewed the state of bilateral relations and explored ways to deepen cooperation across multiple sectors, including security, trade, and development.

Rwanda and Congo-Brazzaville maintain longstanding diplomatic ties, strengthened over the years through agreements covering aviation, tourism, energy, security, education, environmental protection, and trade.

Officials reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cooperation as part of ongoing regional engagement efforts.

title: Rwanda and Global Partners Mark 32nd Genocide Commemoration Amid Calls to Combat Hate Speech
excerpt: Kigali, 7 April 2026 - Rwanda and international partners have begun the 32nd commemoration of the Genocide against the Tutsi, with ceremonies and messages of remembrance held across the country and abroad under the theme emphasizing reflection, unity, and vigilance against hate speech.
title_en: Rwanda and Global Partners Mark 32nd Genocide Commemoration Amid Calls to Combat Hate Speech
excerpt_en: Kigali, 7 April 2026 - Rwanda and international partners have begun the 32nd commemoration of the Genocide against the Tutsi, with ceremonies and messages of remembrance held across the country and abroad under the theme emphasizing reflection, unity, and vigilance against hate speech.
body_en:
Kigali, 7 April 2026 - Rwanda and international partners have begun the 32nd commemoration of the Genocide against the Tutsi, with ceremonies and messages of remembrance held across the country and abroad under the theme emphasizing reflection, unity, and vigilance against hate speech.

The week of mourning was formally outlined by the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement in coordination with national commemoration structures, detailing nationwide remembrance activities beginning on 7 April and extending through the official 100-day period of reflection.

The opening ceremony took place at the Kigali Genocide Memorial, followed by a nationwide “Walk to Remember” from Gasabo District to BK Arena, where an evening vigil was scheduled. Additional remembrance walks and ceremonies are planned in various districts, including Kicukiro, where participants are expected to gather at memorial sites for reflection and testimony.

Officials stated that essential services, including healthcare and hospitality, will continue operating during the period, while cultural and educational activities will integrate remembrance programming. The national flag is being flown at half-mast as part of official protocol.

Commemorations are also taking place in schools, government institutions, and embassies abroad, each organizing dedicated remembrance sessions between April and early July. Authorities emphasized that these events are intended to foster education, reflection, and intergenerational dialogue.

At the international level, survivors and representatives of organizations supporting genocide remembrance shared testimonies at events including a ceremony at the United Nations headquarters in New York, where survivors recounted personal experiences and called for continued global vigilance against genocide ideology.

Religious and civic institutions also issued statements reflecting on the tragedy, urging communities to uphold unity, reconciliation, and the rejection of denialism or revisionism. Leaders emphasized that remembrance is both a moral duty and a call to action for preventing future atrocities.

Solidarity messages were received from multiple countries and institutions, including governments and international organizations, as well as partners in sports and diplomacy, underscoring the global recognition of the genocide and the commitment to “Never Again.”

title: La France ordonne le procès d'un officier rwandais pour son rôle présumé dans le génocide de 1994
excerpt: Paris, April 9, 2026 - France’s judiciary has ordered the trial of Rwandan Lt. Col. Cyprien Kayumba over his alleged involvement in the Genocide against the Tutsi, reversing an earlier decision that had closed the case.
title_en: France Orders Trial of Rwandan Officer Over Alleged Role in 1994 Genocide
excerpt_en: Paris, April 9, 2026 - France’s judiciary has ordered the trial of Rwandan Lt. Col. Cyprien Kayumba over his alleged involvement in the Genocide against the Tutsi, reversing an earlier decision that had closed the case.
body_en:
Paris, April 9, 2026 - France’s judiciary has ordered the trial of Rwandan Lt. Col. Cyprien Kayumba over his alleged involvement in the Genocide against the Tutsi, reversing an earlier decision that had closed the case.

The ruling was issued by the investigative chamber of the Paris Court of Appeal, which determined that Kayumba should face charges of complicity in genocide and crimes against humanity. The decision follows an appeal by the French National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT), which argued that key evidence had been overlooked.

Kayumba, 71, served as a senior officer responsible for financial operations, foreign procurement, and arms distribution within Rwanda’s Ministry of Defence before and during the 1994 genocide. Investigators allege that he played a role in facilitating weapons acquisitions and supply chains linked to forces involved in the mass killings.

According to case records, Kayumba is suspected of having participated in a high-level meeting of the former Rwandan armed forces (Ex-FAR) on April 9, 1994, chaired by Théoneste Bagosora, shortly after the assassination of President Juvénal Habyarimana. He is also accused of traveling abroad later that month to negotiate arms deals, including with contacts in France.

Despite a United Nations arms embargo imposed in May 1994, prosecutors allege that Kayumba continued to facilitate weapons transfers, which were subsequently used by militias such as the Interahamwe.

Kayumba has lived in France since 1998. A complaint was first filed in 2002 by victims’ organizations, including the Collective of Civil Parties for Rwanda (CPCR). He was briefly detained in 2018 before being released under judicial supervision.

During questioning, Kayumba acknowledged involvement in arms procurement but denied knowledge that the weapons would be used in the genocide, stating he acted under orders from the Ministry of Defence. Prosecutors have challenged the credibility of this defense.

In January 2025, investigating judges initially ruled that there was insufficient evidence to proceed to trial. However, that decision was overturned on April 8, 2026, following the prosecution’s appeal.

Kigali, April 10, 2026 - The President of the Supreme Court of Rwanda, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has urged newly appointed judges and court clerks to uphold integrity and treat corruption as incompatible with judicial duty.

The remarks were delivered during a swearing-in ceremony for 10 judges and 16 court clerks, where Mukantaganzwa emphasized that ethical conduct and professionalism must guide all judicial work.

She stressed that corruption has no place in the justice system, describing it as “an abomination” and warning that any conduct leading to it undermines public trust in the courts.

“You know that corruption is an abomination. It is not acceptable and all the behaviors that lead to it are unacceptable,” she said, urging the new judicial officials to serve citizens with fairness and discipline.

Mukantaganzwa further called on the appointees to cultivate teamwork and cooperation within the judiciary, noting that collaboration among colleagues is essential to the functioning of the justice system. She encouraged them to support one another and uphold shared institutional values.

She added that the judiciary would continue to provide support to its staff while expecting them to fully discharge their responsibilities in serving the public.

Other judicial officials present echoed the same message. High Court Judge Hodari Edgar emphasized the importance of integrity and quality service delivery, while court official Uwera Mireille Marceline pledged commitment to fighting corruption and improving service to court users.

The ceremony underscored ongoing efforts within Rwanda’s judiciary to strengthen professionalism, accountability, and public confidence in the justice system.

body_en:
Kigali, April 9, 2026 - Rwanda and Chad have signed a new cooperation agreement establishing a Joint Commission aimed at enhancing bilateral relations and promoting joint development initiatives.

The agreement was signed by Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, and his Chadian counterpart, Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul.

According to officials, the Joint Commission will serve as a framework to deepen cooperation across multiple sectors and facilitate the implementation of shared projects between the two countries.

Fadoul stated that the agreement builds on existing ties and reflects a commitment to cooperation grounded in mutual respect and African solidarity. He added that the timing of the agreement is appropriate, given the already strong relationship between Rwanda and Chad.

For his part, Nduhungirehe highlighted the opportunities created by the new framework, emphasizing its role in strengthening collaboration and advancing development initiatives in both countries.

During the discussions, Nduhungirehe also conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame to Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Déby. The message included a request for Chad’s support for the re-election bid of Louise Mushikiwabo as Secretary-General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF).

Officials described the agreement as a step toward consolidating diplomatic and economic ties, while reinforcing regional cooperation efforts on the African continent.

title_en: UN Reopens Headquarters in Khartoum for First Time Since War Began
excerpt_en: Khartoum April 2, 2026; The United Nations has reopened its headquarters in Khartoum for the first time since the outbreak of war in April 2023, marking a significant step toward restoring its operations in the Sudanese capital.
body_en:
Khartoum April 2, 2026; The United Nations has reopened its headquarters in Khartoum for the first time since the outbreak of war in April 2023, marking a significant step toward restoring its operations in the Sudanese capital.

The reopening follows nearly three years of relocation to Port Sudan, where UN activities had been based due to ongoing fighting in Khartoum.

The ceremony was attended by senior Sudanese officials, including Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem and Khartoum Governor Ahmed Osman Hamza, alongside representatives from the United Nations and its affiliated agencies.

Government officials welcomed the move, describing it as an important signal of improving conditions and renewed cooperation between Sudan and international partners.

The foreign minister said the return of UN operations to Khartoum reflects a shared commitment to stabilizing the country and advancing peace efforts. He emphasized the government’s intention to work closely with UN agencies under national initiatives aimed at achieving long-term stability.

He also reiterated the government’s position on the conflict, stating that authorities remain committed to restoring order and rejecting external interference in Sudan’s internal affairs.

The minister called on regional organizations, including the African Union and IGAD, to take more active roles in supporting stability and reassessing Sudan’s standing within regional frameworks.

UN officials highlighted the gradual resumption of activities in the capital as part of broader efforts to expand humanitarian operations and coordination across the country.

title: Burhan Pledges Commitment to Democratic Transition on Anniversary of 2019 Uprising
excerpt: Sudan April 6, 2026; Sudan’s army chief and head of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has reaffirmed the military’s commitment to a democratic transition and eventual transfer of power to civilians.
title_en: Burhan Pledges Commitment to Democratic Transition on Anniversary of 2019 Uprising
excerpt_en: Sudan April 6, 2026; Sudan’s army chief and head of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has reaffirmed the military’s commitment to a democratic transition and eventual transfer of power to civilians.
body_en:
Sudan April 6, 2026; Sudan’s army chief and head of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has reaffirmed the military’s commitment to a democratic transition and eventual transfer of power to civilians.

In a recorded speech marking the seventh anniversary of the 2019 mass sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum, Burhan said the armed forces remain determined to complete the political transition process initiated after the ousting of former president Omar al-Bashir.

The address, filmed at multiple military locations, highlighted the army’s historical role in Sudan’s uprisings, referencing the 1985 revolution that removed Jaafar Nimeiri and the 2019 protests that ended Bashir’s three-decade rule.

Burhan described the military as a partner of the Sudanese people in what he termed the “battle of dignity,” referring to the ongoing conflict against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), as well as the broader political transition process.

He reiterated that the armed forces are committed to enabling a democratic process in which Sudanese citizens can freely choose their system of governance.

“This is an occasion to renew our pledge to the Sudanese people that we are their sons and partners,” he said, adding that the military would continue working toward completing the transition begun in 2019.

Burhan stated that the Sudanese population has historically stood with the military during pivotal moments, including the 1985 and 2019 uprisings, and has again aligned with it during the ongoing war that began in April 2023.

He further said Sudanese citizens would ultimately prevail and reject humiliation or tyranny.

title: Sudanese Forces Accused of Torture and Arbitrary Detention, Rights Group Says
excerpt: Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Forces affiliated with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been accused of arbitrarily detaining and torturing civilians in areas under their control, as part of a broader campaign targeting perceived opponents, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW).
title_en: Sudanese Forces Accused of Torture and Arbitrary Detention, Rights Group Says
excerpt_en: Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Forces affiliated with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been accused of arbitrarily detaining and torturing civilians in areas under their control, as part of a broader campaign targeting perceived opponents, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW).
body_en:
Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Forces affiliated with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been accused of arbitrarily detaining and torturing civilians in areas under their control, as part of a broader campaign targeting perceived opponents, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW).

The report alleges that the military and allied groups, including the General Intelligence Service and the al-Baraa Ibn Malik battalion militia, have targeted individuals based on ethnic identity, humanitarian work, and political affiliation.

Based on interviews with 28 individuals conducted between June 2025 and February 2026, the report documents alleged abuses in several regions, including Khartoum, Gezira, Gedaref, Red Sea, and Northern states. Detainees were reportedly held incommunicado in military bases or residential buildings converted into detention facilities.

HRW said testimonies from former detainees, their families, and legal representatives describe a pattern of arbitrary arrests, ill-treatment, and a climate of impunity.

In response, the Attorney General’s office rejected allegations of widespread arbitrary detention and deaths in custody. Authorities acknowledged only a single case currently under criminal investigation and maintained that all detainees are being held legally under police supervision and oversight.

The report also indicates that individuals from Darfur have been disproportionately targeted, with some accused of collaborating with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has its origins in the region. Witnesses described cases in which detainees were beaten and accused of bringing the conflict to the capital.

Humanitarian workers have also reportedly been affected. Local volunteers providing aid services, including community kitchens, were subjected to interrogation and detention. In one case, an aid worker in East Khartoum was held for more than two weeks and questioned about funding sources following the army’s recapture of the area.

Despite a January 2026 directive by military leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordering the release of hundreds of women from a prison in Omdurman, rights monitors indicated that many remain in detention without due process. The report further notes that at least 25 women have been sentenced to death on charges of collaboration.

title: Sudan Approves Economic Measures to Stabilize Currency as Pound Hits Record Low
excerpt: Sudan April 2, 2026 ; Sudan’s Higher Economic Committee has approved a set of emergency measures aimed at stabilizing the national currency and addressing worsening economic instability.
title_en: Sudan Approves Economic Measures to Stabilize Currency as Pound Hits Record Low
excerpt_en: Sudan April 2, 2026 ; Sudan’s Higher Economic Committee has approved a set of emergency measures aimed at stabilizing the national currency and addressing worsening economic instability.
body_en:
Sudan April 2, 2026 ; Sudan’s Higher Economic Committee has approved a set of emergency measures aimed at stabilizing the national currency and addressing worsening economic instability.

The decisions were taken during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Kamil Idris and attended by senior ministers responsible for economic planning, finance, and trade.

The Sudanese pound has continued its steep decline since the outbreak of war in April 2023, falling from around 600 per US dollar to approximately 3,665 per US dollar on the parallel market, reflecting severe macroeconomic pressures.

Authorities attribute the collapse to disrupted production, declining exports, and the prolonged impact of the conflict on national economic activity.

The newly approved measures include tighter regulation of luxury imports, policies to expand and diversify exports, and incentives aimed at encouraging Sudanese expatriates to channel remittances through formal banking systems.

Officials also reviewed the country’s foreign exchange reserves, the availability of essential commodities, and broader fiscal performance during the meeting.

The committee stressed the need to regulate export revenues more strictly, reduce government spending, and eliminate informal or illegal fees affecting economic activity.

In addition, state institutions have been instructed to adopt electronic revenue collection systems and complete foreign trade procedures through a centralized digital platform designed to improve transparency and reduce corruption.

title: Army Chief Al-Burhan Retires 21 Generals in Major Military Reshuffle
excerpt: Khartoum, April 11, 2026 - Sudan’s military leadership has undergone a significant restructuring after army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordered the retirement of 21 senior officers and the promotion of others, in what authorities described as a routine administrative measure.
title_en: Army Chief Al-Burhan Retires 21 Generals in Major Military Reshuffle
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 11, 2026 - Sudan’s military leadership has undergone a significant restructuring after army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordered the retirement of 21 senior officers and the promotion of others, in what authorities described as a routine administrative measure.
body_en:
Khartoum, April 11, 2026 - Sudan’s military leadership has undergone a significant restructuring after army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordered the retirement of 21 senior officers and the promotion of others, in what authorities described as a routine administrative measure.

According to a statement from the military, the reshuffle affects officers holding the rank of major general, including prominent figures such as Diab Badr Diab, Khalid al-Qadi, Qandeel Bashir, and Khalid Abdel Mutaal. The army said the decisions were taken in accordance with institutional regulations governing promotions and retirements within the armed forces.

However, the timing of the move has sparked criticism in some political and military circles. Observers noted that several of the retired officers had played key roles in the ongoing conflict against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), particularly within the framework of what the military refers to as the “Battle of Dignity.”

The reshuffle marks the second major reorganization of the military hierarchy since the outbreak of the conflict, following a similar wave of promotions and retirements in August 2025.

The changes come shortly after a series of internal disciplinary measures. Earlier in the week, Major Sir al-Khatim al-Salmabi was dismissed from the army’s media wing after publishing inaccurate information regarding a senior command appointment.

The restructuring also follows a broader overhaul of the General Staff. Under the new configuration, Yasser al-Atta was appointed Chief of Staff, while the positions of deputy and assistant commanders were abolished.

As part of the reorganization, several senior figures were reassigned to strategic roles. Shams al-Din Kabbashi was appointed assistant for construction and strategic planning, Ibrahim Jaber took on responsibilities for international relations and military cooperation, and Mirghani Idris was named assistant for military industries.

The developments highlight ongoing efforts by Sudan’s military leadership to consolidate command structures and adapt to the evolving dynamics of the conflict, now entering its third year.

title: Sudanese Civilian Groups Adopt Joint Peace Roadmap at Berlin Conference
excerpt: Berlin, April 15, 2026 - Sudanese civilian groups meeting in Berlin have adopted a unified roadmap aimed at ending the country’s war and relaunching a political transition toward peace and stability.
title_en: Sudanese Civilian Groups Adopt Joint Peace Roadmap at Berlin Conference
excerpt_en: Berlin, April 15, 2026 - Sudanese civilian groups meeting in Berlin have adopted a unified roadmap aimed at ending the country’s war and relaunching a political transition toward peace and stability.
body_en:
Berlin, April 15, 2026 - Sudanese civilian groups meeting in Berlin have adopted a unified roadmap aimed at ending the country’s war and relaunching a political transition toward peace and stability.

The agreement, signed on Wednesday during the international conference, outlines a common civilian position focused on protecting civilians and safeguarding critical infrastructure amid ongoing violence. It calls for strict respect of international humanitarian law and immediate measures to facilitate unhindered humanitarian access across conflict-affected areas.

Participants also stressed the urgency of curbing hate speech and fostering conditions conducive to dialogue and trust-building, seen as essential steps toward a comprehensive and lasting ceasefire.

Beyond immediate priorities, the document proposes a broader political process addressing the root causes of Sudan’s crisis, including governance failures, marginalization, and justice. A key component is the establishment of a transitional justice framework to ensure accountability, provide redress for victims, and support national reconciliation.

The conference, however, has drawn criticism from Sudanese authorities. In Khartoum, Prime Minister Kamil Idriss said the government had not been invited, describing the exclusion as a “serious misstep” that could undermine the initiative’s effectiveness.

Organizers defended the decision, indicating that the forum was designed as a civilian and humanitarian platform, deliberately distanced from competing claims to political legitimacy.

Prominent civilian figures welcomed the outcome. Other political leaders echoed calls for a Sudanese-led process, emphasizing the importance of international coordination in supporting reconstruction and peace efforts.

title: Une ONG soudanaise rejette la condamnation à mort d'un avocat des droits humains
excerpt: Khartoum, April 26, 2026 - A Sudanese legal advocacy group has condemned the death sentence handed to lawyer and human rights defender Abubakar Mansour, citing serious procedural violations and concerns over the fairness of the trial.
title_en: Sudan Rights Group Rejects Death Sentence for Human Rights Lawyer
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 26, 2026 - A Sudanese legal advocacy group has condemned the death sentence handed to lawyer and human rights defender Abubakar Mansour, citing serious procedural violations and concerns over the fairness of the trial.
body_en:
Khartoum, April 26, 2026 - A Sudanese legal advocacy group has condemned the death sentence handed to lawyer and human rights defender Abubakar Mansour, citing serious procedural violations and concerns over the fairness of the trial.

In a statement issued Sunday, the Emergency Lawyers group said the ruling, recently upheld by an appeals court, was marred by breaches of due process, including restrictions on defence rights and irregularities in court proceedings.

Mansour was arrested from his home in Sinjah, Sennar State, on November 25, 2024, and charged under the Sudanese Penal Code with offences including undermining the constitutional system and inciting war against the state, allegedly linked to ties with the Rapid Support Forces.

According to the group, he has been held in detention for approximately 517 days, which it described as indicative of the use of politically driven charges to prolong imprisonment.

The case has undergone multiple judicial stages. Mansour was initially convicted in April 2025, before an appeals court reviewed the case in July, dropping some charges while upholding others and recommending a harsher sentence. The case was subsequently returned to a lower court.

In October 2025, the Sinjah Criminal Court sentenced him to death. The legal group said the proceedings were flawed, alleging incomplete evidence hearings and limited access for the defence. It also claimed that the verdict was issued without notifying Mansour’s legal team or allowing them to be present.

The group further expressed concern about increasing pressure on legal professionals, citing the arrest of a member of the defence team as an example of restrictions affecting the legal community.

It argued that the handling of the case raises broader questions about judicial independence, suggesting that external influences may have affected the outcome and undermined confidence in the legal system.
