title: UN Sanctions RSF Procurement Chief and Three Colombians
excerpt: Khartoum, April 28, 2026 - A United Nations Security Council sanctions committee has added four individuals to its blacklist, including a senior official from Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and three Colombian nationals linked to a private service agency.
title_en: UN Sanctions RSF Procurement Chief and Three Colombians
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 28, 2026 - A United Nations Security Council sanctions committee has added four individuals to its blacklist, including a senior official from Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and three Colombian nationals linked to a private service agency.
body_en:
Khartoum, April 28, 2026 - A United Nations Security Council sanctions committee has added four individuals to its blacklist, including a senior official from Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and three Colombian nationals linked to a private service agency.

The committee designated Al-Goney Hamdan Dagalo, the RSF’s procurement director and a close relative of the group’s leadership. Based in Dubai, he is now subject to sanctions measures including asset freezes and travel bans.

Also sanctioned were three Colombian nationals associated with the International Services Agency (A4SI), identified as Alvaro Andres Quijano Becerra, Claudia Viviana Oliveros Forero, and Mateo Andres Duque Botero.

The sanctions fall under the framework established by the UN Security Council to address the conflict in Darfur and are part of broader efforts to enforce an arms embargo and restrict financial flows linked to armed groups.

Originally created in 2005, the sanctions committee oversees measures such as asset freezes and travel bans, supported by a panel tasked with monitoring compliance and investigating violations of international humanitarian law.

After years of limited updates, the committee has recently resumed active listings in response to the ongoing conflict that began in April 2023. The latest designations are intended to disrupt procurement networks and financing channels linked to the war.

UN officials said detailed summaries of the sanctions decisions have been made available through official channels, as part of efforts to increase transparency and accountability.

The move is part of wider international efforts to curb the flow of resources sustaining the conflict and to support prospects for a political resolution.

title: Legal Action Initiated Against Rights Lawyer Over Alleged “Misleading Information”

title_en: Legal Action Initiated Against Rights Lawyer Over Alleged “Misleading Information”
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 17, 2026 - Sudanese judicial authorities have launched legal proceedings against rights lawyer Rehab Mubarak, accusing her of disseminating information deemed harmful to national security amid the ongoing conflict.
body_en:
Khartoum, April 17, 2026 - Sudanese judicial authorities have launched legal proceedings against rights lawyer Rehab Mubarak, accusing her of disseminating information deemed harmful to national security amid the ongoing conflict.

According to judicial officials, Mubarak-who is affiliated with a network of emergency lawyers-faces charges related to the spread of what authorities describe as false reports aimed at undermining the military’s image and role. An arrest warrant has been issued as part of efforts to counter what officials characterize as a recent surge in misinformation.

Legal sources indicate that Mubarak has also been dismissed from the Sudanese Bar Association over alleged violations of professional ethics. The association maintains that she used her legal standing to promote narratives considered misleading and capable of inciting public opinion.

Mubarak, however, rejects the accusations, stating that the proceedings are linked to her work documenting human rights violations during the war. She argues that such actions are intended to suppress accountability and silence those monitoring abuses.

She further questioned the current approach to national security oversight, warning that targeting legal professionals and rights monitors risks undermining transparency and the rule of law.

The case highlights growing tensions between authorities and civil society actors in Sudan, as the conflict continues to generate competing narratives and intensify scrutiny over human rights conditions.

title: Uganda Faces Mounting Scrutiny Over Public Spending and Controversial Sovereignty Bill
excerpt: Kampala April 16, 2026 - Uganda is facing growing public and political scrutiny over its governance priorities, as controversy over parliamentary spending converges with intensifying debate around a proposed sovereignty bill currently before Parliament.
title_en: Uganda Faces Mounting Scrutiny Over Public Spending and Controversial Sovereignty Bill
excerpt_en: Kampala April 16, 2026 - Uganda is facing growing public and political scrutiny over its governance priorities, as controversy over parliamentary spending converges with intensifying debate around a proposed sovereignty bill currently before Parliament.
body_en:
Kampala April 16, 2026 - Uganda is facing growing public and political scrutiny over its governance priorities, as controversy over parliamentary spending converges with intensifying debate around a proposed sovereignty bill currently before Parliament.

Criticism has mounted following reports that Members of Parliament from the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) received allowances of up to 100 million Ugandan shillings each during a retreat in Kyankwanzi. Opposition figures argue that the payments reflect a disconnect between government spending and the realities facing public services.

David Lewis Rubongoya, Secretary General of the National Unity Platform (NUP), condemned the expenditure, saying it was unjustified at a time when sectors such as education continue to face resource shortages.

“There is no justification for allocating such sums to people who are already salaried, while essential sectors continue to face difficulties,” he said, pointing to reports of inadequate facilities in public schools.

The issue has revived broader concerns about transparency in public finance, with critics questioning disparities between political spending and service delivery, and calling for stronger oversight of resource allocation.

At the same time, parliamentary debate is intensifying over a proposed sovereignty bill, which seeks to impose strict regulations on foreign influence, including controls on external funding and harsh penalties for non-compliance.

Benjamin Katana, treasurer of the NUP, warned that the bill could significantly expand state oversight into citizens’ private and economic lives. He argued that provisions requiring government approval for certain financial transactions-such as receiving funds from abroad-could disrupt everyday activities.

“This goes beyond national security,” Katana said. “It raises questions about how far the state should go in regulating private life.”

title: Museveni Approves Financial Package for Newly Elected MPs Amid Anti-Corruption Warning
excerpt: Uganda April 16, 2026 - Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has approved a financial package of 100 million Ugandan shillings for each newly elected Member of Parliament, during a retreat for ruling party legislators in Kyankwanzi.
title_en: Museveni Approves Financial Package for Newly Elected MPs Amid Anti-Corruption Warning
excerpt_en: Uganda April 16, 2026 - Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has approved a financial package of 100 million Ugandan shillings for each newly elected Member of Parliament, during a retreat for ruling party legislators in Kyankwanzi.
body_en:
Uganda April 16, 2026 - Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has approved a financial package of 100 million Ugandan shillings for each newly elected Member of Parliament, during a retreat for ruling party legislators in Kyankwanzi.

The announcement was made during a meeting with MPs from the National Resistance Movement (NRM), where Museveni also cautioned lawmakers against corruption, warning that it undermines the effectiveness of Parliament.

According to the President, MPs who accept the package will initially receive 20 million shillings before their official swearing-in ceremony scheduled for May 2026, with the remaining amount to be disbursed later.

“I have approved 100 million shillings, but I will provide a small amount for your swearing-in first. The rest will come later. We should avoid unnecessary conduct and instead rely on institutional solutions rather than corruption,” Museveni said.

The President emphasized that corruption within Parliament weakens governance and accountability, stressing that legislators have a responsibility to oversee public institutions effectively.

“When there is corruption in Parliament, how can you control others? If those responsible for oversight are compromised, who will supervise them? It would damage the country, almost like self-destruction,” he added.

Museveni also pointed to concerns about MPs allegedly soliciting funds from public officials in exchange for shielding them from scrutiny, calling for stricter ethical conduct within parliamentary committees.

The announcement has drawn attention within Uganda’s political circles, as debates continue over governance standards, parliamentary accountability, and the role of financial incentives in public service.

title: Uganda and Rwanda to Hold 12th Round of Bilateral Cooperation Talks in Kampala
excerpt: Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda is preparing to host the 12th session of the Permanent Commission between Uganda and Rwanda, in a new round of talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation across multiple sectors.
title_en: Uganda and Rwanda to Hold 12th Round of Bilateral Cooperation Talks in Kampala
excerpt_en: Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda is preparing to host the 12th session of the Permanent Commission between Uganda and Rwanda, in a new round of talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation across multiple sectors.
body_en:
Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda is preparing to host the 12th session of the Permanent Commission between Uganda and Rwanda, in a new round of talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation across multiple sectors.

The meeting is scheduled to take place from April 20 to 22, 2026, and is being organized by Uganda’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in collaboration with its embassy in Kigali.

According to officials, the discussions will bring together representatives from more than 15 ministries, reflecting the broad scope of cooperation between the two countries.

The Ugandan delegation will be led by the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, John Mulimba, while Rwanda’s team will be headed by Dr. Usta Kaitesi, Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.

The talks are expected to be held in Kampala at the Mestil Hotel, with both open sessions and closed-door ministerial consultations planned before the adoption of joint conclusions and the signing of cooperation agreements.

Ugandan Ministry of Foreign Affairs Director for Cooperation, Ambassador Richard Kabonero, said the agenda will focus on key areas including security and defence cooperation, infrastructure development, immigration management, police coordination, and education.

He added that the two sides will also review progress made since the 11th session held in Kigali in 2023, as well as assess implementation of existing agreements.

Officials further indicated that the discussions will explore new opportunities for collaboration, particularly in trade, investment, and joint development projects, as both countries seek to strengthen regional ties and economic integration.

title: Uganda Law Society demande la suspension du procès du meurtre de la crèche de Ggaba
excerpt: Kampala April 15, 2026 - The Uganda Law Society (ULS) has petitioned the High Court Criminal Division to suspend proceedings in the ongoing Ggaba daycare murder trial, citing alleged violations of constitutional rights that it says must be addressed before the case can continue.
title_en: Uganda Law Society Seeks Suspension of Ggaba Daycare Murder Trial Over Alleged Rights Violations
excerpt_en: Kampala April 15, 2026 - The Uganda Law Society (ULS) has petitioned the High Court Criminal Division to suspend proceedings in the ongoing Ggaba daycare murder trial, citing alleged violations of constitutional rights that it says must be addressed before the case can continue.
body_en:
Kampala April 15, 2026 - The Uganda Law Society (ULS) has petitioned the High Court Criminal Division to suspend proceedings in the ongoing Ggaba daycare murder trial, citing alleged violations of constitutional rights that it says must be addressed before the case can continue.

The application relates to Criminal Court Session No. 132 of 2026, in which Christopher Okello Onyum is being tried in connection with the killing of four children at a daycare facility in Ggaba, a case that has drawn nationwide attention.

In a letter dated April 14, 2026, addressed to Justice Alice Komuhangi Khaukha, the ULS requested an urgent stay of proceedings, arguing that unresolved constitutional questions must first be determined.

Signed by ULS Vice President Anthony Asiimwe, the petition is linked to Miscellaneous Application No. 170 of 2026 - Uganda Law Society vs Attorney General - a human rights enforcement case filed through the Electronic Court Case Management Information System.

The Society argues that the proceedings raise serious constitutional issues, including alleged violations of Articles 21(1), 38, 28(3)(a), 28(3)(c), 43, 44(c), 128(1), and 128(2) of the Constitution.

It further cites Section 8(1) of the Human Rights (Enforcement) Act, 2019, which requires courts to halt proceedings where a question of rights violation arises until such issues are determined.

The Act, enacted to operationalize Article 50 of the Constitution, provides for broad enforcement mechanisms, including compensation, restitution, and other remedies where rights violations are established.

The ULS is therefore seeking both an immediate suspension of the criminal trial and the scheduling of an urgent hearing to resolve the constitutional questions raised.

title: Katumbi rejects constitutional change, calls 2006 charter “the best in the world”
excerpt: Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - Opposition leader Moïse Katumbi has strongly opposed any attempt to revise the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo, urging citizens to resist proposed reforms amid an ongoing national debate over constitutional change. In a video message sha
title_en: Katumbi rejects constitutional change, calls 2006 charter “the best in the world”
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - Opposition leader Moïse Katumbi has strongly opposed any attempt to revise the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo, urging citizens to resist proposed reforms amid an ongoing national debate over constitutional change. In a video message sha
body_en:
Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - Opposition leader Moïse Katumbi has strongly opposed any attempt to revise the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo, urging citizens to resist proposed reforms amid an ongoing national debate over constitutional change.
In a video message shared on his social media platforms, the leader of the Ensemble pour la République party warned against efforts to alter the 2006 Constitution, calling on Congolese citizens to remain vigilant and mobilize in defense of the current legal framework.
He cited Article 64, which provides for civic resistance in the event of a threat to constitutional order, and urged the population to reject any revision process he views as politically motivated.
Katumbi argued that the Constitution is not responsible for the country’s governance failures, stating that issues such as poor infrastructure, low public sector wages, unemployment, and poverty stem from leadership and policy choices rather than the constitutional framework itself.
He described the 2006 Constitution as “the best in the world” and warned that changing it would constitute a betrayal of the Congolese people.
Addressing President Félix Tshisekedi directly, Katumbi recalled past cooperation on safeguarding constitutional order and the country’s first peaceful transfer of power, urging respect for the aspirations of citizens and national stability.
The debate over constitutional revision has intensified in recent months, with the ruling party arguing that reforms are needed to improve state efficiency, while opposition figures and civil society groups warn that such changes could undermine term limits and consolidate political power beyond 2028.
The controversy continues to deepen political divisions in the country as both sides maintain sharply contrasting interpretations of the Constitution’s role in governance and development.

title: DRC lawmaker proposes reforms to limit multiple public offices and improve governance in state-owned enterprises
excerpt: Kinshasa March 29, 2026 - A member of the National Assembly from Lukunga, Dunia Mangu Mangu, has introduced a series of proposed amendments aimed at improving governance in state-owned enterprises in the Democratic Republic of Congo by restricting the accumulation of public offic
title_en: DRC lawmaker proposes reforms to limit multiple public offices and improve governance in state-owned enterprises
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 29, 2026 - A member of the National Assembly from Lukunga, Dunia Mangu Mangu, has introduced a series of proposed amendments aimed at improving governance in state-owned enterprises in the Democratic Republic of Congo by restricting the accumulation of public offic
body_en:
Kinshasa March 29, 2026 - A member of the National Assembly from Lukunga, Dunia Mangu Mangu, has introduced a series of proposed amendments aimed at improving governance in state-owned enterprises in the Democratic Republic of Congo by restricting the accumulation of public offices.
The proposals were presented during parliamentary debates on March 27 on a draft law revising the legal framework governing the organization and management of public enterprises, initiated by MP Jean-Pierre Pasi Zapamba.
At the center of the amendments is a push to prohibit individuals from simultaneously holding positions in state-owned companies and political offices, or engaging in competing commercial activities linked to those enterprises.
The lawmaker argued that such overlaps create inefficiencies, conflicts of interest, and public frustration, particularly among unemployed youth.
He also proposed stricter rules preventing individuals from holding multiple senior positions across different public institutions, citing examples such as incompatibility between ministerial roles and leadership positions in entities like the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA) or the National Insurance Company.
Dunia Mangu Mangu praised the original legislative initiative, saying it responds to public demands for greater transparency and fairness in the management of state institutions.
However, he also suggested expanding recruitment criteria for public officials beyond competitive examinations to include political considerations and national representation, arguing that this could strengthen cohesion and reduce political tensions.
He maintained that aligning appointments with both merit and political balance would help reinforce unity within state institutions.
The proposals have sparked debate in parliament, highlighting ongoing tensions in the DRC over governance standards, merit-based appointments, political inclusion, and transparency in the management of public enterprises.

title: DRC welcomes UN resolution recognizing transatlantic slave trade as “most serious crime against humanity”
excerpt: March 29, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage has welcomed a United Nations General Assembly resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and slavery of Africans as the most serious crimes against humanity. Adopted during the 8
title_en: DRC welcomes UN resolution recognizing transatlantic slave trade as “most serious crime against humanity”
excerpt_en: March 29, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage has welcomed a United Nations General Assembly resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and slavery of Africans as the most serious crimes against humanity. Adopted during the 8
body_en:
March 29, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage has welcomed a United Nations General Assembly resolution recognizing the transatlantic slave trade and slavery of Africans as the most serious crimes against humanity.
Adopted during the 80th UN General Assembly session, the resolution highlights the scale, systemic nature, and long-term consequences of slavery, stating that its legacy continues to fuel structural inequalities in the modern world.
According to the Congolese Ministry, the resolution represents an important step toward international recognition of historical injustices and strengthens calls for remembrance, justice, and reparations.
The text was adopted on March 25 with 123 votes in favor, 3 against (United States, Israel, and Argentina), and 52 abstentions, including several European countries. It was sponsored by Ghana and supported by the African Union as part of broader continental advocacy for reparative justice related to the transatlantic slave trade.
Ghanaian President John Mahama, speaking after the vote, described the resolution as “historic,” emphasizing the need for global acknowledgment of the estimated 13 million Africans forcibly displaced over centuries.
The resolution also encourages the restitution of cultural property to countries of origin, reinforcing ongoing international debates about the return of artifacts taken during colonial and slavery-era injustices.
In line with this agenda, the DRC Ministry highlighted its ongoing efforts to preserve historical memory, including a memorandum of understanding signed in January 2025 for the creation of a national memorial dedicated to Ota Benga, a Congolese man who was taken to the United States in the early 20th century and displayed at the Bronx Zoo in 1906.
Authorities in Kinshasa say the project reflects a broader commitment to historical recognition, cultural restoration, and the promotion of African heritage as part of international justice and memory initiatives.

title: DRC holds workshop on mining diplomacy to strengthen governance and global positioning of mineral sector
excerpt: March 30, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector gathered in Kinshasa for a high-level workshop focused on strengthening mining diplomacy, improving governance, and enhancing the country’s position in global critical mineral value chains. Organize
title_en: DRC holds workshop on mining diplomacy to strengthen governance and global positioning of mineral sector
excerpt_en: March 30, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector gathered in Kinshasa for a high-level workshop focused on strengthening mining diplomacy, improving governance, and enhancing the country’s position in global critical mineral value chains. Organize
body_en:
March 30, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector gathered in Kinshasa for a high-level workshop focused on strengthening mining diplomacy, improving governance, and enhancing the country’s position in global critical mineral value chains.
Organized by the Bon Regard Association (BREG) in collaboration with government institutions, technical services, development partners, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations, the two-day forum (March 30-31) aims to produce policy recommendations for national decision-makers.
Officials emphasized that the DRC’s vast mineral wealth-particularly in critical minerals essential to the global energy transition-places the country in a strategic position within the international economy, but that structural challenges continue to limit its full potential.
Speaking on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nzengu Mishinga Jules highlighted transparency, accountability, and coordinated diplomacy as key pillars for strengthening the country’s mining governance and international credibility.
He stressed the need for closer synergy between the Ministries of Mines, Planning, and Finance, along with diplomatic services, to ensure a coherent strategy that moves the country beyond the perception of being merely a raw materials exporter.
International partners also expressed support for reform efforts. The United Kingdom reaffirmed its commitment to supporting governance and transparency initiatives in the sector, including additional contributions through programs implemented by the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI).
British officials underscored the DRC’s “crucial role” in the global energy transition and encouraged reforms that could attract responsible investment and strengthen institutional stability.
NRGI representatives emphasized that improved governance, reduced illicit resource flows, and better environmental and human rights standards are essential for transforming mining wealth into sustainable national development.
Participants also highlighted persistent challenges in the sector, including conflict-linked resource extraction, weak governance structures, environmental degradation, and limited local value addition.
Organizers said the workshop is intended to move beyond discussion toward actionable recommendations that will help the government strengthen mining diplomacy and position the DRC as a strategic, rules-based actor in global mineral supply chains.

title: DRC and Brazil sign agreement on employment for dependents of diplomatic staff
excerpt: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil have signed a bilateral agreement allowing dependents of diplomatic mission staff to engage in paid employment, marking a new step in strengthening ties between the two countries. The agreement was concluded du
title_en: DRC and Brazil sign agreement on employment for dependents of diplomatic staff
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil have signed a bilateral agreement allowing dependents of diplomatic mission staff to engage in paid employment, marking a new step in strengthening ties between the two countries. The agreement was concluded du
body_en:
Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil have signed a bilateral agreement allowing dependents of diplomatic mission staff to engage in paid employment, marking a new step in strengthening ties between the two countries.
The agreement was concluded during the official visit to Kinshasa by Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira from March 29 to 30, as part of broader efforts to deepen cooperation and reinforce longstanding diplomatic relations.
According to Congolese authorities, the deal applies to dependents of staff serving in diplomatic missions, consular posts, and permanent representations, facilitating their access to local labor markets under defined legal frameworks.
Officials from both countries described the agreement as progress in legal and social cooperation, while reaffirming their shared commitment to expanding collaboration across multiple sectors.
Discussions between the two sides identified key areas of priority, including agriculture, infrastructure, defense, education, mining, culture, research, and economic development. Both governments also expressed their intention to boost trade and encourage investment flows.
The visit builds on previous engagements, notably multisectoral consultations held in Brasília and a Congolese diplomatic mission in August 2025.
As part of this ongoing partnership, the second session of the DRC-Brazil multisectoral consultations is scheduled to take place in Kinshasa in 2027.

title: Norbert Basengezi elected Second Vice-President, replacing Bahati Lukwebo
excerpt: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - Senator Norbert Basengezi Katintima has been elected Second Vice-President of the Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, securing a clear majority in Friday’s vote. According to results announced by Senate President Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Base
title_en: Norbert Basengezi elected Second Vice-President, replacing Bahati Lukwebo
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - Senator Norbert Basengezi Katintima has been elected Second Vice-President of the Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, securing a clear majority in Friday’s vote. According to results announced by Senate President Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Base
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - Senator Norbert Basengezi Katintima has been elected Second Vice-President of the Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, securing a clear majority in Friday’s vote.
According to results announced by Senate President Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Basengezi received 87 votes in favor, against 5 votes opposed and 3 invalid ballots.
A former head of the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) and senator representing South Kivu, Basengezi was designated by the ruling coalition, the Sacred Union of the Nation, to succeed Modeste Bahati Lukwebo in the Senate bureau.
His election follows a process marked by the withdrawal of other contenders. Senator Françoise Bemba Ndokwa, initially in the race, saw her candidacy withdrawn by her party, the Movement for the Liberation of Congo. Another candidate, Mariane Bakiele, also stepped down on the eve of the vote, citing alignment with the majority coalition’s choice and respect for the Head of State, Félix Tshisekedi.
With no remaining challengers, Basengezi stood as the sole candidate, a position validated by a special commission set up to review applications.
The vacancy followed the resignation of Bahati Lukwebo, which the Senate formally acknowledged during a plenary session on March 21. His departure came amid a petition seeking his removal over alleged “incompetence.” A special parliamentary commission had been tasked with examining the case but closed its proceedings after his resignation.
Basengezi’s election consolidates the Sacred Union’s hold over key positions within the upper chamber, at a time of ongoing political realignments within the country’s institutions.

title: Sankuru gubernatorial race: Legal challenge threatens April 15 election timetable
excerpt: Sankuru April 4, 2026 - A legal dispute over candidate eligibility has introduced fresh uncertainty into the electoral process for the governorship of Sankuru province, with a key court hearing scheduled for April 10. The Council of State is set to examine a case filed by guberna
title_en: Sankuru gubernatorial race: Legal challenge threatens April 15 election timetable
excerpt_en: Sankuru April 4, 2026 - A legal dispute over candidate eligibility has introduced fresh uncertainty into the electoral process for the governorship of Sankuru province, with a key court hearing scheduled for April 10. The Council of State is set to examine a case filed by guberna
body_en:
Sankuru April 4, 2026 - A legal dispute over candidate eligibility has introduced fresh uncertainty into the electoral process for the governorship of Sankuru province, with a key court hearing scheduled for April 10.
The Council of State is set to examine a case filed by gubernatorial candidate Justin Omokala Wemambolo, who is contesting the final list of candidates published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI).
Omokala is challenging the inclusion of fellow candidate Jules Lodi Emongo, arguing that his candidacy as an independent violates constitutional and electoral provisions. According to him, Emongo-elected as a senator under the banner of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress-failed to formally resign from his party before declaring an independent bid, as required by law.
He also contests the eligibility of Emongo’s running mate for vice-governor, claiming the individual, a civil servant, did not submit a resignation or official leave of absence prior to entering the race, in breach of electoral regulations.
The dispute follows a decision by the Sankuru Court of Appeal, which rejected Omokala’s appeal on procedural grounds, ruling that he lacked standing despite appearing on the provisional list of candidates. Omokala has since escalated the matter to the Council of State, the country’s highest administrative jurisdiction.
He further criticized CENI for publishing the final list before the conclusion of ongoing legal proceedings, arguing that the electoral body should have awaited the outcome of the April 10 hearing.
The controversy comes as the gubernatorial election, initially delayed due to funding constraints, is now scheduled for April 15. The final list includes 10 candidates, down from 11 following the withdrawal of one contender.
With legal proceedings still underway, the outcome of the Council of State hearing could prove decisive in determining whether the electoral calendar in Sankuru can be maintained.

The controversy comes as the gubernatorial election, initially delayed due to funding constraints, is now scheduled for April 15. The final list includes 10 candidates, down from 11 following the withdrawal of one contender.
With legal proceedings still underway, the outcome of the Council of State hearing could prove decisive in determining whether the electoral calendar in Sankuru can be maintained.

title: DRC suspends fuel transport price cap for 45 days amid global oil market tensions
excerpt: Kinshasa March 24, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has temporarily suspended the cap on transport price differentials for petroleum products for a period of 45 days, as part of measures aimed at stabilizing fuel supply and protecting consumer purchasing
title_en: DRC suspends fuel transport price cap for 45 days amid global oil market tensions
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 24, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has temporarily suspended the cap on transport price differentials for petroleum products for a period of 45 days, as part of measures aimed at stabilizing fuel supply and protecting consumer purchasing
body_en:
Kinshasa March 24, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has temporarily suspended the cap on transport price differentials for petroleum products for a period of 45 days, as part of measures aimed at stabilizing fuel supply and protecting consumer purchasing power.
The decision was taken under instructions from Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka, who directed the ministries responsible for the economy, hydrocarbons, and finance to implement the suspension in response to rising geopolitical tensions affecting global energy markets.
Authorities say the measure is intended to anticipate the economic impact of disruptions in international oil supply routes, including key maritime corridors such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Suez Canal.
While the suspension could lead to higher logistics costs in the short term, the government has announced compensatory steps, including temporary reductions or suspensions of certain border taxes and royalties to limit pressure on fuel prices.
Officials also indicated that additional measures will be implemented to ensure the steady import and distribution of petroleum products via regional supply routes through Kenya and Tanzania, while monitoring freight and insurance costs used to calculate average border pricing.
Despite global market volatility, the government has reassured the public that national fuel reserves remain sufficient to meet demand until June, with additional shipments expected in the coming weeks to reinforce supply.
The policy follows discussions in a recent Council of Ministers meeting chaired by President Félix Tshisekedi, during which officials emphasized the need for coordinated action to maintain macroeconomic stability in the face of external shocks.

title: Kinshasa Calls for Results-Oriented Security Partnership
excerpt: Paris, April 17, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has called for a more “demanding” and results-driven security partnership with France, as both countries seek to strengthen military cooperation amid ongoing instability in eastern DRC. The appeal was made during talks on A
title_en: Kinshasa Calls for Results-Oriented Security Partnership
excerpt_en: Paris, April 17, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has called for a more “demanding” and results-driven security partnership with France, as both countries seek to strengthen military cooperation amid ongoing instability in eastern DRC. The appeal was made during talks on A
body_en:
Paris, April 17, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has called for a more “demanding” and results-driven security partnership with France, as both countries seek to strengthen military cooperation amid ongoing instability in eastern DRC.
The appeal was made during talks on April 16 between Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita and French Minister of the Armed Forces Catherine Vautrin at the French Ministry of Defense.
According to Congolese authorities, the meeting focused on enhancing bilateral cooperation in defense and military training, with both sides reviewing strategic areas of collaboration alongside technical experts. Discussions also addressed ongoing reforms aimed at transforming the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) into a more professional and effective force capable of addressing current security threats.
Congolese officials emphasized the need to modernize existing cooperation frameworks, including longstanding agreements between the two countries, while adapting them to present-day security challenges.
Against the backdrop of continued violence in eastern DRC-linked to the AFC/M23 rebellion, the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), and other armed groups-Kinshasa called for a partnership centered on concrete outcomes. Authorities highlighted priorities such as specialized training, institutional reform support, doctrinal guidance, and enhanced operational capacity.
French authorities reiterated their commitment to supporting the professionalization of the FARDC and broader peace and stabilization efforts in the Great Lakes region. The discussions took place on the sidelines of a high-level forum on maritime security involving partners from the Gulf of Guinea.
As part of efforts to deepen cooperation, the Congolese government also announced plans to deploy a defense attaché to Paris in the coming days to facilitate coordination between the two countries.
France and the DRC maintain longstanding defense ties, including training programs and institutional support initiatives. French military cooperation has notably contributed to training structures in the DRC, including advanced officer education programs involving both national and international participants.

title: UN: China Urges Stronger Mining Cooperation to Tackle Conflict in Great Lakes
excerpt: New York, April 18, 2026 - China has called for enhanced cooperation in the mining sector and stronger action against illegal exploitation and smuggling of natural resources in the Great Lakes region, warning that these dynamics continue to fuel instability, particularly in easte
title_en: UN: China Urges Stronger Mining Cooperation to Tackle Conflict in Great Lakes
excerpt_en: New York, April 18, 2026 - China has called for enhanced cooperation in the mining sector and stronger action against illegal exploitation and smuggling of natural resources in the Great Lakes region, warning that these dynamics continue to fuel instability, particularly in easte
body_en:
New York, April 18, 2026 - China has called for enhanced cooperation in the mining sector and stronger action against illegal exploitation and smuggling of natural resources in the Great Lakes region, warning that these dynamics continue to fuel instability, particularly in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Speaking at a United Nations Security Council session on April 15, Ambassador Sun Lei, Chargé d’Affaires of China’s Permanent Mission to the UN, stressed that security efforts alone are insufficient to address the root causes of conflict in the region.
He noted that persistent unrest is closely linked to governance challenges and underdevelopment, with natural resources often contributing to cycles of violence rather than economic progress. According to the Chinese diplomat, illegal mining activities and their connection to armed groups remain a central driver of insecurity.
China called on the international community to support countries in the region in strengthening transparent and mutually beneficial cooperation in the exploitation of mineral resources, while dismantling illicit mining and smuggling networks.
The ambassador also emphasized the need for a long-term development-oriented approach, arguing that improving governance and economic opportunities is essential to achieving lasting stability.
Reaffirming China’s engagement in Africa, he highlighted ongoing cooperation in infrastructure, industrialization, and resource development, as well as a planned zero-tariff policy for dozens of African countries aimed at boosting trade and economic growth.
The appeal comes amid a deteriorating security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC, where clashes involving the AFC/M23 rebellion and other armed groups continue to drive mass displacement and deepen food insecurity across the region.
Tensions between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda also remain high, with both sides exchanging accusations over support to armed groups and involvement in the exploitation of natural resources, further complicating efforts toward regional stabilization.

title: “Save the DRC” Opposition Movement Holds Second Conclave, Denounces Political and Security Crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The opposition movement “Save the DRC,” led by former President Joseph Kabila, has concluded its second conclave held from April 6 to 8, 2026, focusing on the country’s political, security, economic, and social situation. In a statement issued after the
title_en: “Save the DRC” Opposition Movement Holds Second Conclave, Denounces Political and Security Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The opposition movement “Save the DRC,” led by former President Joseph Kabila, has concluded its second conclave held from April 6 to 8, 2026, focusing on the country’s political, security, economic, and social situation. In a statement issued after the
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The opposition movement “Save the DRC,” led by former President Joseph Kabila, has concluded its second conclave held from April 6 to 8, 2026, focusing on the country’s political, security, economic, and social situation.
In a statement issued after the meeting, the movement said participants reviewed ongoing national crises and various domestic and international initiatives aimed at resolving them. The group, which operates from outside the Democratic Republic of Congo, was established in October 2025 in Nairobi and brings together exiled political figures and banned political actors.
The movement strongly criticized what it described as a “deliberate slide toward dictatorship” under the current administration, led by President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, accusing it of political repression, restrictions on dissent, and refusal to engage in what it considers a credible national dialogue.
It further denounced alleged violations of fundamental rights, including attacks on political freedoms, targeted violence against dissenting voices, and the abandonment of civilian populations in parts of eastern Congo, particularly in Ituri and North Kivu, where armed groups continue to operate.
According to the movement’s communiqué, these situations constitute serious breaches of constitutional provisions and international humanitarian law, and reflect what it calls a broader crisis of governance.
“Save the DRC” also accused the government of ignoring the root causes of the ongoing crisis, including contested political legitimacy, governance failures, manipulation of judicial institutions, and the use of identity-based divisions for political control.
The group further criticized recent diplomatic agreements between Kinshasa and international partners, including arrangements with the United States concerning migration and other bilateral cooperation frameworks, arguing that such initiatives do not address underlying domestic instability.
Reaffirming its political position, the movement declared its opposition to any constitutional revision process, invoking Article 64 of the Constitution as justification for what it describes as a “defense of constitutional order.”
The conclave also reportedly examined regional and international mediation efforts, including past agreements such as the Sun City framework, arguing that current peace initiatives have failed to adequately address structural causes of conflict.
While operating in exile, the movement says it intends to continue mobilizing political support internationally, positioning itself as part of a broader opposition front challenging the current political order in Kinshasa.

title: AFDC-A Withdraws Support for Motion of No Confidence Against Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - A motion of no confidence targeting Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani, has lost momentum after the political grouping AFDC-A announced the withdrawal of support from its elected officials who had signed the
title_en: AFDC-A Withdraws Support for Motion of No Confidence Against Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - A motion of no confidence targeting Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani, has lost momentum after the political grouping AFDC-A announced the withdrawal of support from its elected officials who had signed the
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - A motion of no confidence targeting Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani, has lost momentum after the political grouping AFDC-A announced the withdrawal of support from its elected officials who had signed the initiative.
The announcement was made by AFDC-A leader Senator Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, who distanced his political platform from what he described as an “isolated” move by two of its National Assembly members. According to the statement, the MPs acted without prior consultation and in violation of internal party rules.
The two deputies, Cizungu Ntaboba Landry and Placide Wemba Mukagwa, had signed the motion alongside other legislators, triggering the parliamentary procedure that could have led to the resignation or dismissal of the Interior Minister if sufficient signatures were secured and a plenary vote held.
Bahati Lukwebo called on the lawmakers to withdraw their signatures, reaffirming that AFDC-A, which is part of the ruling Sacred Union coalition supporting President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, had not endorsed the initiative.
One of the MPs involved, Cizungu Ntaboba, later indicated his withdrawal from the parliamentary process linked to the motion. He had previously accused the Interior Ministry of serious governance failures, including interference in provincial administration, obstruction of parliamentary oversight, violations of institutional balance, and abuse of authority.
The motion itself had cited broader concerns over national security and alleged responsibility for persistent insecurity in parts of the country.
With AFDC-A’s withdrawal, the initiative appears to have been significantly weakened, raising uncertainty over whether it will gather enough parliamentary support to proceed to a vote in the National Assembly.

title: DRC Parliament Moves Forward on Rwanda Peace Deal and US Strategic Agreement
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two draft laws ratifying agreements signed with Rwanda and the United States, marking an important step in the legislative process for both diplomatic initiatives. The tex
title_en: DRC Parliament Moves Forward on Rwanda Peace Deal and US Strategic Agreement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two draft laws ratifying agreements signed with Rwanda and the United States, marking an important step in the legislative process for both diplomatic initiatives. The tex
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two draft laws ratifying agreements signed with Rwanda and the United States, marking an important step in the legislative process for both diplomatic initiatives.
The texts, presented on April 13, have been referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee for detailed examination before a possible plenary vote.
The agreements include a peace framework between Kinshasa and Kigali, as well as a strategic partnership between the DRC and the United States covering key sectors such as security, critical minerals, infrastructure, and economic cooperation.
Among the lawmakers reacting to the development, MP Hermès Itina Mayamba welcomed the parliamentary decision, describing both agreements as a potential turning point for peace and development in the country.
He stated that the peace accord with Rwanda and the strategic partnership with the United States could contribute to stabilizing the security situation in eastern Congo while also supporting long-term economic growth.
The legislator emphasized that the National Assembly was acting within its constitutional mandate by authorizing the ratification process of international treaties, which he said provides legal backing for government commitments.
He further noted that the initiatives come at a critical moment, as the country continues to face prolonged insecurity in its eastern provinces, and stressed the importance of institutional action to support peacebuilding efforts.
MP Itina also praised the diplomatic efforts of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, highlighting his role in advancing negotiations that led to the agreements. He similarly acknowledged the contribution of the government led by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka and Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner.
According to parliamentary procedure, the Foreign Affairs Committee will now conduct an in-depth review of both agreements before submitting its report to the plenary for further debate and potential ratification.
If approved, the agreements would enter into force as binding international commitments, shaping both the DRC’s regional security framework and its strategic economic partnerships.

title: First Group of US-Deported Migrants Arrives in Kinshasa Under Temporary Arrangement
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed the arrival of the first group of migrants deported from the United States, following a temporary arrangement agreed between Kinshasa and Washington. According to a statement from the Mini
title_en: First Group of US-Deported Migrants Arrives in Kinshasa Under Temporary Arrangement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed the arrival of the first group of migrants deported from the United States, following a temporary arrangement agreed between Kinshasa and Washington. According to a statement from the Mini
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed the arrival of the first group of migrants deported from the United States, following a temporary arrangement agreed between Kinshasa and Washington.
According to a statement from the Ministry of Communication and Media, 15 individuals were received in the capital on Friday, April 17, under a schedule coordinated by the competent authorities.
The government clarified that the arrivals are being admitted under short-stay permits in line with national immigration law and the country’s international commitments. Officials stressed that the arrangement does not constitute a permanent relocation or settlement program.
Authorities further indicated that the reception, accommodation, and logistical support for the individuals are being financed by the United States, under conditions that comply with security protocols and administrative procedures governing the movement of persons.
Kinshasa described the arrangement as strictly temporary, limited in duration, and managed under controlled conditions, while reaffirming its commitment to humanitarian principles, national sovereignty, and public interest.
The agreement forms part of broader diplomatic understandings between the DRC and the United States, which have recently expanded cooperation in areas including migration management and strategic partnerships.
However, the development has triggered strong reactions from opposition groups, civil society actors, and human rights organizations. Critics argue that the arrangement raises security and humanitarian concerns and have called for greater transparency regarding its implementation.
Some opposition voices have linked their concerns to historical precedents in the Great Lakes region, warning against potential security risks in sensitive border areas, particularly in eastern Congo, where displacement crises have previously had cross-border consequences.
The government, for its part, maintains that the arrangement is tightly regulated and will be implemented in full compliance with national law and international obligations.

title: Tshisekedi Calls for “Rebuilt Multilateralism” Based on Regional Integration at Antalya Diplomatic Forum
excerpt: Antalya, April 18, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has used its participation in the 5th Antalya Diplomatic Forum (ADF 2026) to advocate for a restructuring of global governance, with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo calling for a renewed model of multilateral
title_en: Tshisekedi Calls for “Rebuilt Multilateralism” Based on Regional Integration at Antalya Diplomatic Forum
excerpt_en: Antalya, April 18, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has used its participation in the 5th Antalya Diplomatic Forum (ADF 2026) to advocate for a restructuring of global governance, with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo calling for a renewed model of multilateral
body_en:
Antalya, April 18, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has used its participation in the 5th Antalya Diplomatic Forum (ADF 2026) to advocate for a restructuring of global governance, with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo calling for a renewed model of multilateralism anchored in regional cooperation.
The forum, held in Türkiye from April 17 to 19 under the auspices of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, brought together heads of state, diplomats, policymakers, and experts to discuss global instability under the theme “Mapping the Future, Managing Uncertainties.”
Speaking during a high-level panel on regional ownership in a changing world, President Tshisekedi argued that existing multilateral systems have shown structural limitations in responding to global crises, particularly in terms of speed and effectiveness.
He said multilateralism should not be abandoned but rather “rebuilt and refounded” through stronger regional frameworks that can respond more rapidly to crises while fostering economic integration and shared development.
The Congolese leader highlighted regional economic cooperation as a key driver of stability, noting that countries within the same region often share historical, cultural, and social ties that can facilitate more effective conflict resolution and coordinated development policies.
As an example, he cited the Lobito Corridor, a major infrastructure and trade route designed to connect Central African production zones to global markets. He described it as a model of regional integration that demonstrates how shared economic interests can promote peace and stability.
Tshisekedi further argued that regional mechanisms allow for a deeper understanding of local dynamics compared to distant multilateral frameworks, which he said can sometimes appear less responsive to specific crises.
The forum also served as a platform for broader discussions on global governance, trade fragmentation, geopolitical tensions, and rising uncertainty in the international system.
Participants engaged in plenary sessions, roundtables, and bilateral meetings aimed at identifying strategies for managing global risks while strengthening cooperation between regions.
Organizers said the event is intended to rebuild trust in international dialogue and promote more resilient global partnerships in the face of increasing geopolitical volatility.
For the DRC, the forum provided an opportunity to reinforce its diplomatic positioning as a proponent of regional integration as a foundation for both stability and economic transformation.

title: UK Ambassador Alyson King Ends Three-Year Diplomatic Mission in the DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The British Embassy in the Democratic Republic of Congo has held a farewell ceremony for outgoing Ambassador Alyson King, marking the conclusion of her three-year diplomatic mission in Kinshasa. The event, attended by political, diplomatic, and institut
title_en: UK Ambassador Alyson King Ends Three-Year Diplomatic Mission in the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The British Embassy in the Democratic Republic of Congo has held a farewell ceremony for outgoing Ambassador Alyson King, marking the conclusion of her three-year diplomatic mission in Kinshasa. The event, attended by political, diplomatic, and institut
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The British Embassy in the Democratic Republic of Congo has held a farewell ceremony for outgoing Ambassador Alyson King, marking the conclusion of her three-year diplomatic mission in Kinshasa.
The event, attended by political, diplomatic, and institutional figures, highlighted the ambassador’s tenure, during which she focused on strengthening bilateral relations between the United Kingdom and the DRC, with emphasis on investment promotion, climate action, and economic cooperation.
During her remarks, Alyson King said relations between London and Kinshasa had deepened significantly over the past three years, despite periods marked by humanitarian pressures and security challenges, particularly in the eastern part of the country.
She noted that the United Kingdom had supported humanitarian responses during crises while also contributing to efforts aimed at strengthening national systems and community resilience.
The outgoing ambassador also underscored ongoing cooperation in peacebuilding initiatives, stressing that sustainable peace remained a central priority of UK engagement in the region. She pointed to continued collaboration with Congolese authorities and international partners aimed at addressing insecurity and supporting stabilization efforts.
Alyson King also highlighted economic diplomacy achievements during her tenure, including the promotion of investment ties and the establishment of the UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce, which she described as part of broader efforts to expand commercial engagement between the two countries.
She further referenced high-level diplomatic exchanges as evidence of a growing strategic partnership between the two states.
Before her appointment in Kinshasa, she served as Deputy Head of Mission at the British Embassy in Lebanon. She formally began her role in the DRC after presenting her credentials to President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo on June 8, 2023.
At the end of her mission, she reaffirmed her commitment to continuing support for peace, security, and sustainable development initiatives in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Burkina Faso Reaffirms AES Commitment to Respectful Multilateralism at OACPS Summit
excerpt: Malabo, March 29, 2026 - Burkina Faso has reiterated its commitment to a form of multilateralism grounded in respect for national sovereignty and local development paths, during the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific
title_en: Burkina Faso Reaffirms AES Commitment to Respectful Multilateralism at OACPS Summit
excerpt_en: Malabo, March 29, 2026 - Burkina Faso has reiterated its commitment to a form of multilateralism grounded in respect for national sovereignty and local development paths, during the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific
body_en:
Malabo, March 29, 2026 - Burkina Faso has reiterated its commitment to a form of multilateralism grounded in respect for national sovereignty and local development paths, during the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS).
Speaking on behalf of President Ibrahim Traoré and the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, underscored the need for a renewed multilateral framework that prioritizes dignity, mutual respect, and context-specific solutions.
Burkina Faso, alongside Mali and Niger, called for stronger solidarity among member states and urged reforms to transform the OACPS into a more effective platform for international cooperation. The delegation highlighted the urgency of addressing intertwined security, humanitarian, and climate challenges, particularly in the Sahel region.
The statement also drew attention to the escalating terrorist threat, noting that the Sahel accounts for a significant share of global terrorism-related fatalities. In response, the AES reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding state sovereignty, enhancing strategic autonomy, and advocating for a more balanced and equitable global order.
Concluding its address, Burkina Faso and its AES partners expressed readiness to deepen collaboration with OACPS members, focusing on economic resilience, regional integration, and inclusive development strategies. They called for reinforced solidarity to turn current crises into opportunities for sustainable and shared growth.

title: Mali Joins African Consultations on Migration Governance in Cairo
excerpt: Cairo, April 1, 2026 - Mali took part in high-level African consultations on migration governance during a ministerial meeting held in Cairo, aimed at advancing the implementation of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. Representing Mali, the Minister of Ma
title_en: Mali Joins African Consultations on Migration Governance in Cairo
excerpt_en: Cairo, April 1, 2026 - Mali took part in high-level African consultations on migration governance during a ministerial meeting held in Cairo, aimed at advancing the implementation of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. Representing Mali, the Minister of Ma
body_en:
Cairo, April 1, 2026 - Mali took part in high-level African consultations on migration governance during a ministerial meeting held in Cairo, aimed at advancing the implementation of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration.
Representing Mali, the Minister of Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, joined counterparts from across the continent in discussions hosted by Egypt.
The meeting forms part of ongoing preparations for the 2026 International Migration Review Forum, set to take place in New York in May under the auspices of the United Nations.
Participants focused on strengthening coordination among African states and aligning regional priorities ahead of the global forum. The consultations also underscored the importance of collective action to ensure safe, orderly, and regular migration, while addressing the specific challenges faced by African countries.
The Cairo meeting highlights Africa’s growing engagement in shaping global migration governance frameworks and reinforcing a unified continental voice on migration-related issues.

title: Mali and Equatorial Guinea Strengthen Bilateral Ties Through High-Level Talks
excerpt: Malabo, March 31, 2026 - Mali and Equatorial Guinea have reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation following high-level discussions held on the sidelines of the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific
title_en: Mali and Equatorial Guinea Strengthen Bilateral Ties Through High-Level Talks
excerpt_en: Malabo, March 31, 2026 - Mali and Equatorial Guinea have reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation following high-level discussions held on the sidelines of the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific
body_en:
Malabo, March 31, 2026 - Mali and Equatorial Guinea have reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation following high-level discussions held on the sidelines of the 11th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS).
Representing Mali, the Minister of Malians Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, was received in audience by Simeón Oyono Esono Angüe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Equatorial Guinea.
During the meeting, Minister Attaher conveyed the fraternal greetings of Mali’s Head of State, Assimi Goïta, to Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, underscoring the longstanding ties between the two nations.
Both parties reaffirmed the strength of their relationship, rooted in friendship, solidarity, and mutual cooperation. Discussions focused on several areas of shared interest, including the need to enhance bilateral collaboration and address challenges faced by Malian nationals residing in Equatorial Guinea.
Key issues raised included improving consular protection, advancing a draft agreement on the free movement of people, and identifying practical solutions to difficulties encountered by members of the Malian diaspora.
Officials described the talks as constructive, highlighting their importance in reinforcing cooperation and advancing shared priorities between Bamako and Malabo.

excerpt_en: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Mali took another step in its diplomatic engagement with the European Union as the country’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the EU Ambassador-designate, Alberto Cerezo, for the presentation of copies of
body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Mali took another step in its diplomatic engagement with the European Union as the country’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the EU Ambassador-designate, Alberto Cerezo, for the presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence.
The formal ceremony marked the beginning of Ambassador Cerezo’s mission in Bamako, setting the stage for renewed dialogue between Mali and the European bloc.
During their meeting, both officials held discussions on the future of Mali-EU relations, emphasizing the importance of strengthening multilateral cooperation. Exchanges focused on fostering a pragmatic and constructive political dialogue grounded in mutual respect and aligned interests.
Regional security dynamics also featured prominently in the talks. Minister Diop highlighted the evolving geopolitical landscape in the Sahel, particularly in light of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), stressing the need for partners to adapt to these changing realities. He underscored that shared security challenges between Europe and the Sahel region require coordinated responses, given their geographic and strategic proximity.
Beyond political and security matters, Mali continues to expand its international partnerships in other sectors. In a parallel development, the country is reinforcing scientific cooperation with China, particularly in efforts to combat emerging infectious diseases-an area of growing global concern.
These engagements reflect Mali’s broader strategy to diversify its international partnerships while addressing both regional stability and global challenges through collaborative frameworks.

excerpt: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Cultural cooperation within the Sahel took center stage as Mali’s Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration received Mohamed Cissé, President of the ALACHO (Indigo) Association of Burkina Faso and Cultural Ambassador of the Confederation
title_en: Burkinabè Cultural Ambassador Meets Malian Minister to Strengthen Regional Cooperation
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Cultural cooperation within the Sahel took center stage as Mali’s Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration received Mohamed Cissé, President of the ALACHO (Indigo) Association of Burkina Faso and Cultural Ambassador of the Confederation
body_en:
Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Cultural cooperation within the Sahel took center stage as Mali’s Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration received Mohamed Cissé, President of the ALACHO (Indigo) Association of Burkina Faso and Cultural Ambassador of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).
Cissé’s visit to Bamako forms part of a broader regional cultural exchange initiative, highlighted by his participation in events linked to the handover of the mascot for the Bougouni Art and Culture Biennial, a key platform for artistic expression in southern Mali.
During the meeting, the Burkinabè cultural figure praised the Malian authorities for their continued commitment to promoting national culture, with particular emphasis on the valorization of Tuareg craftsmanship, widely regarded as a cornerstone of Sahelian heritage.
Talks between the two parties also focused on avenues for deepening sub-regional cultural collaboration. Discussions underscored the potential role of Cultural Ambassadors from AES member states in advancing shared cultural initiatives, especially in the lead-up to the second edition of the International Diaspora Forum.
The engagement reflects a growing recognition among Sahel states of culture as a strategic tool for regional integration, identity preservation, and international outreach.

title: Four New Ambassadors Present Credentials to Mali’s Head of State
excerpt: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali’s diplomatic landscape expanded on Thursday as President of the Transition and Head of State, General Assimi Goïta, received the credentials of four newly appointed resident ambassadors during an official ceremony at the Koulouba Palace. The ceremony
title_en: Four New Ambassadors Present Credentials to Mali’s Head of State
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali’s diplomatic landscape expanded on Thursday as President of the Transition and Head of State, General Assimi Goïta, received the credentials of four newly appointed resident ambassadors during an official ceremony at the Koulouba Palace. The ceremony
body_en:
Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali’s diplomatic landscape expanded on Thursday as President of the Transition and Head of State, General Assimi Goïta, received the credentials of four newly appointed resident ambassadors during an official ceremony at the Koulouba Palace.
The ceremony formalized the accreditation of several key diplomatic representatives. Among them were Viviana Hernandez, Ambassador-designate of Cuba; Alberto Cerezo, Ambassador-designate of the European Union; Umar Sanda Ahmed, Ambassador-designate of Ghana; and Ahmed Turki Al-Subaie, Ambassador-designate of the State of Qatar.
Each diplomat was received in audience by the Malian Head of State following the presentation of their credentials, marking the official start of their respective missions in the country.
During the ceremony, President Goïta highlighted the importance of maintaining strong and constructive relations with international partners. He praised the quality of existing diplomatic ties and reiterated Mali’s commitment to further strengthening both bilateral and multilateral cooperation.
The Head of State emphasized that such partnerships would continue to be guided by principles of openness, mutual respect, and shared benefit, as Mali seeks to reinforce its position on the regional and international stage.
The accreditation of these ambassadors reflects ongoing diplomatic engagement between Mali and a diverse group of global partners, underscoring the country’s efforts to broaden its international cooperation framework.

title: Mali-Guinea Cooperation: Vocational Training and Entrepreneurship at the Core of Bilateral Engagement
excerpt: Conakry, April 24, 2026 - Mali and Guinea are seeking to deepen their bilateral cooperation with a renewed focus on vocational training, entrepreneurship, and skills development. Mali’s Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Vocational Training, Oumou Sall Seck, w
title_en: Mali-Guinea Cooperation: Vocational Training and Entrepreneurship at the Core of Bilateral Engagement
excerpt_en: Conakry, April 24, 2026 - Mali and Guinea are seeking to deepen their bilateral cooperation with a renewed focus on vocational training, entrepreneurship, and skills development. Mali’s Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Vocational Training, Oumou Sall Seck, w
body_en:
Conakry, April 24, 2026 - Mali and Guinea are seeking to deepen their bilateral cooperation with a renewed focus on vocational training, entrepreneurship, and skills development.
Mali’s Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Vocational Training, Oumou Sall Seck, was received by Guinean Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah during a high-level meeting held on the sidelines of the Guinea Skills Olympics, where Mali participated as the guest of honor.
The talks underscored a shared ambition between the two countries to position skills development and youth employment as central pillars of their cooperation framework. Both sides emphasized the importance of translating this partnership into concrete and results-oriented initiatives.
Discussions focused on strengthening collaboration in vocational training systems, promoting entrepreneurship, and enhancing the employability of young people, in line with broader regional development priorities.
The meeting reflects a growing trend among West African countries to align education and employment policies in order to address youth unemployment and support sustainable economic growth.
In a related development, recent adjustments to travel procedures-particularly the suspension of the Electronic Travel Authorization to Morocco (AEVM)-are seen as part of a broader effort to reinvigorate bilateral relations and facilitate mobility, further strengthening cooperation ties in the region.

title_en: Mali-Morocco Relations: Suspension of Electronic Travel Authorization to Ease Mobility
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 23, 2026 - Morocco has announced the suspension of the Electronic Travel Authorization to Morocco (AEVM) for Malian nationals, in a move expected to facilitate travel and strengthen bilateral ties between the two countries. The decision was formally communicated to
body_en:
Bamako, April 23, 2026 - Morocco has announced the suspension of the Electronic Travel Authorization to Morocco (AEVM) for Malian nationals, in a move expected to facilitate travel and strengthen bilateral ties between the two countries.
The decision was formally communicated to Mali’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation by the Embassy of the Kingdom of Morocco in Bamako. It is set to take effect on April 27, 2026.
Authorities in Bamako have welcomed the measure, viewing it as a significant step toward enhancing cooperation and easing mobility between Mali and Morocco.
Until now, Malian travelers were required to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization prior to departure, a system designed to regulate migration flows and strengthen pre-arrival screening procedures. The removal of this requirement is expected to simplify administrative processes, reduce waiting times, and encourage greater movement of people.
The decision is also likely to boost tourism and business travel, while facilitating exchanges between economic operators and strengthening people-to-people connections.
The Electronic Travel Authorization, commonly used by several countries, is a digital pre-clearance system that allows authorities to verify travelers before entry. While not equivalent to a visa, it serves as an additional layer of border control.
Its suspension marks a new phase in Mali-Morocco relations, reflecting a shared commitment to deepening cooperation and promoting closer economic and social ties.

excerpt: Djibouti, April 2, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, has paid tribute to Ali Mohamed Daoud, widely known as Jean-Marie, a figure in Djibouti’s political landscape and president of the Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy (FRUD), who died overn
title_en: President Guelleh Pays Tribute to FRUD Leader Ali Mohamed Daoud
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 2, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, has paid tribute to Ali Mohamed Daoud, widely known as Jean-Marie, a figure in Djibouti’s political landscape and president of the Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy (FRUD), who died overn
body_en:
Djibouti, April 2, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, has paid tribute to Ali Mohamed Daoud, widely known as Jean-Marie, a figure in Djibouti’s political landscape and president of the Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy (FRUD), who died overnight from Wednesday to Thursday following a prolonged illness.
In a statement released on Thursday, President Guelleh praised the late politician’s enduring contributions to both political and social life, describing him as a figure who consistently placed “the general interest above personal interests.”
He also recalled Daoud’s role in efforts to restore peace and national cohesion during the 1990s, a period marked by episodes of unrest in the country. “Our fellow citizens will long remember the invaluable contribution he made to restoring peace and cohesion,” the president said.
According to the head of state, Daoud’s popularity stemmed from his “social intelligence and open-mindedness,” qualities that earned him broad respect across Djiboutian society.
President Guelleh extended his condolences to the family of the deceased, as well as to members and supporters of the FRUD and the broader Union for the Presidential Majority (UMP).
In response to the death, the president announced the suspension of his electoral campaign for three days, cancelling a planned tour of the regions of Obock and Tadjourah.
A former minister and a widely respected national figure, Ali Mohamed Daoud leaves behind a large family and a significant political legacy.
The head of state, accompanied by several government officials including Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, as well as senior members of the UMP and a large cross-section of the public, attended the funeral ceremony held in his honor.
