title: President Guelleh Meets International Election Observers Ahead of April 10 Vote
excerpt: Djibouti, April 8, 2026 - The President of the Republic and candidate for re-election, Ismail Omar Guelleh, held a series of meetings on Wednesday with the heads of international observer delegations deployed for the upcoming presidential election scheduled for April 10. The meet
title_en: President Guelleh Meets International Election Observers Ahead of April 10 Vote
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 8, 2026 - The President of the Republic and candidate for re-election, Ismail Omar Guelleh, held a series of meetings on Wednesday with the heads of international observer delegations deployed for the upcoming presidential election scheduled for April 10. The meet
body_en:
Djibouti, April 8, 2026 - The President of the Republic and candidate for re-election, Ismail Omar Guelleh, held a series of meetings on Wednesday with the heads of international observer delegations deployed for the upcoming presidential election scheduled for April 10.
The meetings, which took place at the Presidential Palace, brought together senior representatives from key regional and international organizations. Among them were Bertrand Makuza, representing the African Union; Mulatu Teshome, heading the delegation from the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD); and Shakir Mahmoud Bander, representing the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
According to official sources, discussions focused on several key aspects of the electoral process, including compliance with international standards, voter registration procedures, candidate validation mechanisms, and equitable access to state media during the campaign period.
The presence of high-profile figures leading the observer missions was highlighted as an indication of the importance attached to the electoral process. Both Mulatu Teshome and Bertrand Makuza bring extensive political experience, having previously served as head of state and head of government in their respective countries.
The meetings were also attended by Djiboutian officials, including Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdoulkader Houssein Omar, Secretary General of the Presidency Mohamed Abdillahi Waiss, and the President’s diplomatic adviser, Fathia Djama Oudine.

title: Mass Rally in Balbala Draws Large Crowd for President Guelleh’s Campaign
excerpt: Djibouti, April 6-7, 2026 - The campaign of incumbent President and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh continued to mobilize large crowds over the weekend, with organizers reporting more than 30,000 attendees at a major rally in the Balbala district on the outskirts of the capital. He
title_en: Mass Rally in Balbala Draws Large Crowd for President Guelleh’s Campaign
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 6-7, 2026 - The campaign of incumbent President and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh continued to mobilize large crowds over the weekend, with organizers reporting more than 30,000 attendees at a major rally in the Balbala district on the outskirts of the capital. He
body_en:
Djibouti, April 6-7, 2026 - The campaign of incumbent President and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh continued to mobilize large crowds over the weekend, with organizers reporting more than 30,000 attendees at a major rally in the Balbala district on the outskirts of the capital.
Held in Oumou Salama, the event marked one of the penultimate campaign gatherings ahead of the April 10 presidential election. Supporters, many dressed in green-the color associated with the ruling political camp-gathered from the afternoon, waving flags, posters, and portraits of the candidate in a highly energized atmosphere.
As the crowd grew into the evening, campaign songs and announcements filled the venue while security personnel managed the dense turnout. Supporters described the gathering as a demonstration of popular backing for the incumbent president, with chants and slogans echoing across the site.
Addressing the crowd, President Guelleh described the turnout as “a human tide,” saying it reflected strong public support for his program. “Balbala is sending a strong message today,” he told supporters.
The rally forms part of an intensified final phase of campaigning, with both the ruling camp and opposition efforts seeking to demonstrate their mobilization capacity in the capital and surrounding districts.
On April 7, the president also attended the final of a football tournament organized in support of his candidacy at the Hassan Gouled Stadium in Djibouti City. The event, which brought together 36 teams across multiple categories, concluded with the Republican Guard team defeating the National Gendarmerie team on penalties.
The stadium, with a capacity of around 10,000 seats, was filled to capacity according to organizers, with families and supporters attending in a festive atmosphere.
At the closing ceremony, President Guelleh presented trophies and awards, including cash prizes and vehicles for outstanding players. Senior officials in attendance included Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed and National Assembly President Dileita Mohamed Dileita.

title: Opposition Candidate Congratulates President Guelleh in Post-Election Meeting
excerpt: Djibouti, April 14, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, received the defeated presidential candidate, Mohamed Farah Samatar of the Unified Democratic Centre (CDU), at the Presidential Palace on Tuesday morning, in a post-election meeting described by offici
title_en: Opposition Candidate Congratulates President Guelleh in Post-Election Meeting
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 14, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, received the defeated presidential candidate, Mohamed Farah Samatar of the Unified Democratic Centre (CDU), at the Presidential Palace on Tuesday morning, in a post-election meeting described by offici
body_en:
Djibouti, April 14, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, received the defeated presidential candidate, Mohamed Farah Samatar of the Unified Democratic Centre (CDU), at the Presidential Palace on Tuesday morning, in a post-election meeting described by official sources as unprecedented.
The visit comes days after the April 10 presidential election and follows Samatar’s public concession of defeat. According to statements made after the meeting, the opposition candidate reiterated his congratulations to President Guelleh and wished him success in leading the country.
“Although I had already expressed my warmest congratulations to the re-elected president through the press, I still wanted to meet with him in person to wish him success in leading our country,” Samatar said.
He added that his gesture reflected “allegiance and submission to the will of the people,” following what he described as a clear expression of popular support for the incumbent leadership.
During the meeting, Samatar also indicated that he had discussed aspects of his political vision for the country, expressing hope that some of these ideas could be considered within the broader national agenda.
The encounter, held at the Presidential Palace, is being presented by officials as a sign of political maturity and a step toward reinforcing national cohesion in the post-election period.

title: Guelleh Urges Business-State Alliance Ahead of Djibouti Presidential Vote
excerpt: Djibouti, April 5, 2026 - Five days before the presidential election, incumbent president and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh called on business leaders to strengthen cooperation with the state in response to growing regional economic uncertainties. Speaking at a campaign event hel
title_en: Guelleh Urges Business-State Alliance Ahead of Djibouti Presidential Vote
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 5, 2026 - Five days before the presidential election, incumbent president and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh called on business leaders to strengthen cooperation with the state in response to growing regional economic uncertainties. Speaking at a campaign event hel
body_en:
Djibouti, April 5, 2026 - Five days before the presidential election, incumbent president and candidate Ismail Omar Guelleh called on business leaders to strengthen cooperation with the state in response to growing regional economic uncertainties.
Speaking at a campaign event held at the Ayla Hotel, the head of state addressed an audience of entrepreneurs in the presence of Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, president of the Chamber of Commerce. He defended the economic record of his current term while cautioning against external risks.
“Our economy is on solid ground,” Guelleh said, pointing to sustained growth, structural investments, and macroeconomic stability, which he described as making Djibouti a “haven of confidence.” He attributed these outcomes to government reforms as well as the contributions of the private sector.
However, the president warned that regional geopolitical tensions, including the conflict involving Iran, could disrupt supply chains, increase energy price volatility, and affect investment flows.
“Ignoring them would be a mistake. Giving in to them through resignation would be an act of surrender,” he said, urging closer coordination between public authorities and economic actors.
Guelleh advocated for a “strengthened, intelligent, and agile” public-private partnership to secure strategic supplies and safeguard the country’s productive base. He also cautioned against speculative practices, pledging to combat inflation through “targeted and equitable” measures.
Emphasizing the role of businesses in maintaining purchasing power, he underlined its importance for domestic market stability and long-term economic sustainability.
With the April 10 vote approaching, the president presented his platform as an “alliance” with the private sector rather than a set of campaign promises, calling for the consolidation of existing gains and the development of a more resilient and inclusive economy.
The meeting forms part of a broader series of engagements between the candidate and various segments of Djiboutian society in the lead-up to the election.

body_en:
Washington, D.C., United States, March 25, 2026 - Ugandan opposition figure Robert Kyagulanyi, widely known as Bobi Wine, has said he is willing to return to Uganda if his safety is guaranteed and he is not subjected to legal proceedings.
Speaking during an interview with France 24, Bobi Wine stated that his return depends on assurances that he can live freely without fear of arrest or persecution.
“I am ready to return to Uganda as long as I am a free person. I cannot return if it is like pleading for my freedom,” he said.
The opposition leader recently arrived in the United States after reportedly going into hiding in Uganda, citing concerns over alleged harassment and abuse by security forces.
Ugandan authorities, however, have maintained that he is not being prosecuted for any crime, suggesting that his time away from the country was a personal decision.
Tensions between Bobi Wine and the government of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni have escalated following the January 15, 2026 presidential election, which resulted in Museveni securing another term in office.

Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - The Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement, Dr. Jean Damascène Bizimana, is expected to address young people at the upcoming Gen-Z Comedy show scheduled for March 26 at Camp Kigali.
Organizers of the event say the invitation aims to give youth an opportunity to learn more about Rwandan history and civic values, particularly as the country approaches the Genocide Remembrance period against the Tutsi.
The event promoter, Ndaruhutse Merci, also known as Fally Merci, said the initiative is intended to combine entertainment with education, noting that many young attendees are eager to better understand national history and identity.
According to organizers, the show will feature a mix of comedians and performers from Rwanda and the region, alongside guest appearances, as part of a broader effort to engage youth through cultural events.
They added that although the platform is primarily comedic, it also serves as a space for civic education and dialogue with public figures.
The Gen-Z Comedy show, regularly hosted at Camp Kigali, has grown in popularity since its launch in 2022 and has become one of the recurring entertainment events targeting young audiences in Rwanda.

title: President Kagame signals possible review of morning prayer broadcast suspension
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has indicated that the issue surrounding the suspension of the morning mosque broadcast may be reviewed, suggesting that authorities could reconsider the current restrictions. The remarks were made during a meeting with membe
title_en: President Kagame signals possible review of morning prayer broadcast suspension
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has indicated that the issue surrounding the suspension of the morning mosque broadcast may be reviewed, suggesting that authorities could reconsider the current restrictions. The remarks were made during a meeting with membe
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has indicated that the issue surrounding the suspension of the morning mosque broadcast may be reviewed, suggesting that authorities could reconsider the current restrictions.
The remarks were made during a meeting with members of the Muslim community in Rwanda, where concerns were raised over the continued suspension of the early morning mosque call, which worshippers said has affected their daily religious routine.
In response, President Kagame stated that the matter could be examined and assessed by relevant authorities, emphasizing that it is a manageable issue requiring review rather than immediate dismissal.
He noted that the early morning period coincides with normal waking hours, adding that the situation should be evaluated in a practical manner while considering public concerns.
The suspension of amplified mosque broadcasts was introduced in previous years following concerns over noise levels in residential areas, in line with public order regulations. Authorities at the time stated that while the external broadcasts were restricted, religious observance itself was not prohibited.
The latest remarks have renewed public discussion around the balance between religious expression and noise regulation, with expectations that further consultations could take place on the matter.

excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, March 26, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has publicly stated his support for Israel in the ongoing conflict involving Israel and Iran, according to remarks shared through his public communications. He indicated that his position is ba
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, March 26, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has publicly stated his support for Israel in the ongoing conflict involving Israel and Iran, according to remarks shared through his public communications.
He indicated that his position is based on geopolitical and religious considerations, stating that Uganda would side with Israel if the conflict escalates in a way that threatens its defeat.
In his comments, Gen. Muhoozi said any outcome leading to what he described as the destruction or defeat of Israel would prompt alignment with Israel’s position, adding that he believes the world is growing weary of the ongoing hostilities in the Middle East.
He further referenced historical and religious ties in explaining his stance.
The conflict, referred to as the Israel-Iran war, reportedly began on February 28, 2026, and has continued for several weeks, with various international actors closely monitoring its escalation.
Gen. Muhoozi also made remarks suggesting strong political alignment with Israel, noting previous expressions of support, including plans to honor historical Israeli figures. Among them is Col. Yonatan Netanyahu, who led the 1976 Entebbe rescue operation in Uganda and was later killed during the same period.
The broader conflict involves Israel and Iran, with Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei remaining a central figure in Iran’s leadership during the ongoing tensions.

title: Rwandan minister warns of inherited genocide ideology among youth

title_en: Rwandan minister warns of inherited genocide ideology among youth
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement, Jean Damascène Bizimana, has raised concerns over the persistence of genocide ideology among some youth, attributing it in part to narratives passed down by parents. Speaking at a public ev
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement, Jean Damascène Bizimana, has raised concerns over the persistence of genocide ideology among some youth, attributing it in part to narratives passed down by parents.
Speaking at a public event in Kigali, the minister said some young people expressing hostility toward the country and its leadership are influenced by misinformation within their families, particularly from individuals linked to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
He warned that false accounts and denial narratives are being transmitted across generations, sometimes amplified through social media, undermining national unity and reconciliation efforts.
Bizimana emphasized that individuals who have served sentences for genocide-related crimes have a responsibility to tell the truth to their children and contribute positively to rebuilding society.
Recent studies cited by officials indicate that a portion of the population believes some former convicts continue to hold divisive views, while social media platforms abroad are also seen as contributing to the spread of harmful narratives.
Authorities say continued civic education and awareness efforts remain essential to strengthening unity and preventing the transmission of extremist ideologies.

title: Diplomatic dispute erupts over AU process for UN Secretary-General nomination
excerpt: Addis Ababa, March 30, 2026 - A procedural dispute has emerged within the African Union (AU) after 20 member states objected to the handling of Senegal’s former president Macky Sall’s proposed candidacy for UN Secretary-General. The controversy centers on whether AU Chairperson É
title_en: Diplomatic dispute erupts over AU process for UN Secretary-General nomination
excerpt_en: Addis Ababa, March 30, 2026 - A procedural dispute has emerged within the African Union (AU) after 20 member states objected to the handling of Senegal’s former president Macky Sall’s proposed candidacy for UN Secretary-General. The controversy centers on whether AU Chairperson É
body_en:
Addis Ababa, March 30, 2026 - A procedural dispute has emerged within the African Union (AU) after 20 member states objected to the handling of Senegal’s former president Macky Sall’s proposed candidacy for UN Secretary-General.
The controversy centers on whether AU Chairperson Évariste Ndayishimiye followed established rules when forwarding the nomination process.
Several countries reportedly argued that the procedure bypassed required AU mechanisms, including review by a ministerial committee responsible for vetting candidates for international positions.
Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that AU rules require nominations to pass through structured approval stages before being transmitted to the United Nations.
He said any direct submission without full committee validation would constitute a breach of established AU procedures.
The AU framework, developed from earlier OAU resolutions and later revised in 2006, outlines a multi-step process involving member states, ministerial review, and approval by the Council of Ministers.
Diplomatic observers say the disagreement highlights broader tensions over decision-making authority within the AU and the interpretation of its internal governance rules.
No official response has yet been issued by the AU Commission regarding the procedural concerns.

title: DRC World Cup Qualification Fuels Tshisekedi’s Renewed Push to Reclaim Eastern Territories
excerpt: Kinshasa, 6 April 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has expressed renewed optimism about retaking territories held by the AFC/M23 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, linking his confidence to a wave of national unity sparked by the country’s recent World Cup qualification. T
title_en: DRC World Cup Qualification Fuels Tshisekedi’s Renewed Push to Reclaim Eastern Territories
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, 6 April 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has expressed renewed optimism about retaking territories held by the AFC/M23 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, linking his confidence to a wave of national unity sparked by the country’s recent World Cup qualification. T
body_en:
Kinshasa, 6 April 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has expressed renewed optimism about retaking territories held by the AFC/M23 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, linking his confidence to a wave of national unity sparked by the country’s recent World Cup qualification.
The Congolese national football team secured its place in the tournament on 31 March with a narrow 1-0 victory over Jamaica national football team, marking the country’s first qualification in 52 years. Celebrations erupted nationwide, including in conflict-affected areas such as Goma, where residents joined in festivities despite ongoing control by rebel forces.
Speaking on 5 April during a ceremony in Kinshasa honoring the national team, Tshisekedi pointed to the celebrations in the east as a sign of enduring national cohesion. “You have seen the images. In these areas controlled by the enemy there is joy, and we will soon take them back because of this strength, because of this pride,” he said.
The president’s remarks come amid continued tensions with the AFC/M23, which maintains control over parts of North and South Kivu provinces. The group has rejected any suggestion of withdrawal, warning that it would respond forcefully to any military offensive.
Previous attempts by government forces to retake lost territories have largely been unsuccessful, with the AFC/M23 often managing to repel advances and, in some cases, expand its positions. International observers continue to emphasize the need for a political solution to the conflict.
Peace talks between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 are expected to resume later this month, with discussions set to take place in Switzerland after being relocated from Doha.
Despite these developments, both sides appear to be moving cautiously, raising concerns that without tangible political progress, hostilities could reignite and intensify in the coming weeks.

body_en:
New Delhi, 7 April 2026 - Students from several schools in India have presented artworks depicting the history of the Genocide against the Tutsi, as part of commemorations marking its 32nd anniversary.
The exhibition was held on the morning of 7 April during an official remembrance event, where the artworks were displayed and interpreted to invited guests. Organizers said the initiative aimed to educate young people and promote reflection on the consequences of genocide and the importance of remembrance.
Among those attending were Jacqueline Mukangira, as well as Darrin Farrant and members of the diplomatic and educational community. The guests were guided through the exhibition, with students explaining the themes and messages behind their work.
April 7 is observed globally as the International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda, marking the start of a period of commemoration for victims of the 1994 atrocities.
In Rwanda, the annual National Week of Mourning has officially begun, launching 100 days of remembrance activities held across the country and within the global Rwandan community.

title: Zimbabwe Opposition Raises Alarm Over Constitutional Amendments Seen as Extending Mnangagwa’s Rule
excerpt: Harare, 8 April 2026 - Zimbabwe’s political opposition has expressed concern over proposed constitutional amendments that could significantly reshape the country’s electoral system and extend the tenure of President Emmerson Mnangagwa. The proposed reforms would shift the preside
title_en: Zimbabwe Opposition Raises Alarm Over Constitutional Amendments Seen as Extending Mnangagwa’s Rule
excerpt_en: Harare, 8 April 2026 - Zimbabwe’s political opposition has expressed concern over proposed constitutional amendments that could significantly reshape the country’s electoral system and extend the tenure of President Emmerson Mnangagwa. The proposed reforms would shift the preside
body_en:
Harare, 8 April 2026 - Zimbabwe’s political opposition has expressed concern over proposed constitutional amendments that could significantly reshape the country’s electoral system and extend the tenure of President Emmerson Mnangagwa.
The proposed reforms would shift the presidential election process from direct popular vote to selection by members of parliament, a change critics argue would weaken democratic accountability. Opposition figure and former finance minister Tendai Biti described the move as a gradual erosion of constitutional order.
“This is a coup. The coup is happening slowly in Zimbabwe,” Biti said, warning that the reforms could concentrate political power further within the ruling establishment.
The ruling ZANU-PF party, which has governed the country since independence in the 1980s, has defended the proposed changes. Party officials argue that the reforms are aimed at reducing electoral costs and improving governance efficiency.
ZANU-PF spokesperson Patrick Chinamasa said there was no intention to halt the process, stating that the party is committed to adopting what it considers a more “cost-effective and less contentious” governance model.
Under the draft constitutional amendments currently under discussion, the terms of both the presidency and the National Assembly would be extended from five to seven years, potentially delaying the next elections from 2028 to 2030. The proposals would also allow the current presidential term to continue until 2030, with future presidents to be selected by a newly elected parliament.
The debate has intensified political tensions in the country, with opposition voices warning of democratic backsliding, while ruling party representatives maintain that the changes reflect institutional reform rather than political consolidation of power.

title: AFC/M23 Announces Leadership Changes in Goma Administration
excerpt: Goma, April 9, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has announced a reshuffle of local leadership in the eastern city of Goma, appointing new administrative officials as it consolidates its control over the area. According to an official statement, Bahati Musanga Erasto, governor of Nort
title_en: AFC/M23 Announces Leadership Changes in Goma Administration
excerpt_en: Goma, April 9, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has announced a reshuffle of local leadership in the eastern city of Goma, appointing new administrative officials as it consolidates its control over the area. According to an official statement, Bahati Musanga Erasto, governor of Nort
body_en:
Goma, April 9, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has announced a reshuffle of local leadership in the eastern city of Goma, appointing new administrative officials as it consolidates its control over the area.
According to an official statement, Bahati Musanga Erasto, governor of North Kivu appointed by the coalition, confirmed the nomination of Kasuba Ngabo Désiré as mayor of Goma, replacing Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who has been reassigned as mayor of the Lubero territory. Kasuba previously served as deputy mayor of the city.
In the same announcement, Nshimiyimana Juvénal, formerly responsible for mobilization and recruitment within the AFC/M23, was appointed deputy mayor of Goma.
Additional appointments include Katembo Isevisya as deputy mayor, and Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy mayor of Karisimbi commune.
The AFC/M23 coalition, which has been engaged in conflict with the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, took control of Goma on January 27, 2025. Since then, it has established parallel administrative structures aimed at managing security, public services, and infrastructure projects in the city.
The latest appointments are presented by the group as part of efforts to strengthen governance and maintain order in areas under its control.

title: France Shifts Africa Strategy Toward East as Military Cooperation with Kenya Expands
excerpt: April 10, 2026 - France is reportedly reorienting its Africa strategy toward East Africa, following a series of military withdrawals and diplomatic setbacks in West Africa. According to reports, the French government has strengthened military cooperation with Kenya, including pla
title_en: France Shifts Africa Strategy Toward East as Military Cooperation with Kenya Expands
excerpt_en: April 10, 2026 - France is reportedly reorienting its Africa strategy toward East Africa, following a series of military withdrawals and diplomatic setbacks in West Africa. According to reports, the French government has strengthened military cooperation with Kenya, including pla
body_en:
April 10, 2026 - France is reportedly reorienting its Africa strategy toward East Africa, following a series of military withdrawals and diplomatic setbacks in West Africa.
According to reports, the French government has strengthened military cooperation with Kenya, including plans for joint exercises and expanded security coordination. The move comes as several West African states have reduced or ended French military presence in recent years.
French President Emmanuel Macron has invited Kenyan President William Ruto to the upcoming G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains in June 2026, signaling closer diplomatic engagement between Paris and Nairobi.
Kenya is also expected to host the France-Africa summit on May 11-12, 2026, marking the first time the event will take place outside the traditional Francophone sphere. The summit is expected to focus on investment, trade, and security cooperation.
Reports indicate that Kenya’s parliament is reviewing a bilateral military cooperation agreement that would formalize joint training and defense collaboration between the two countries.
The shift follows the withdrawal of French forces from several West and Central African countries, including Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Chad, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, where governments have cited dissatisfaction with France’s counterterrorism role.
Analysts suggest that France’s renewed engagement with East Africa reflects a broader strategic repositioning, as other global powers-including Russia, China, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and the United States-continue to expand their influence across the African continent.

The message was delivered in Accra by Rwanda’s Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, during a visit on April 10, 2026. According to Rwanda’s Ministry of Education, Nsengimana conveyed a request from President Paul Kagame urging Ghanaian authorities to support Mushikiwabo’s candidacy for another term.
The OIF Secretary-General election is expected to take place at the organization’s Council of Ministers meeting scheduled for November 15-16 in Cambodia, with the nomination process closing in May 2026.
Mushikiwabo, who is seeking a third term, is currently among several declared candidates. Others include Romanian former prime minister Dacian Cioloș, former DRC culture minister Juliana Amato Lumumba, and Mauritanian academic and former minister Coumba Ba.
Rwanda’s diplomatic outreach reflects ongoing efforts to consolidate support within Francophone and partner countries ahead of the vote for one of the organization’s most influential leadership positions.

title: RSF Leader Urges UN to Open Aid Offices in Territories Under His Control
excerpt: Sudan April 7, 2026; The leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” has called on the United Nations to establish humanitarian offices in areas controlled by his forces to facilitate aid delivery amid Sudan’s ongoing conflict. Speaking fo
title_en: RSF Leader Urges UN to Open Aid Offices in Territories Under His Control
excerpt_en: Sudan April 7, 2026; The leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” has called on the United Nations to establish humanitarian offices in areas controlled by his forces to facilitate aid delivery amid Sudan’s ongoing conflict. Speaking fo
body_en:
Sudan April 7, 2026; The leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” has called on the United Nations to establish humanitarian offices in areas controlled by his forces to facilitate aid delivery amid Sudan’s ongoing conflict.
Speaking following a meeting in Nairobi with the UN Secretary-General’s Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, Hemetti said he had formally requested expanded UN presence in RSF-held territories to improve humanitarian coordination.
The United Nations has previously rejected the RSF’s attempt to establish a parallel government under its “Founding Alliance,” but continues to engage with the group’s leadership in a limited capacity for humanitarian access and civilian protection discussions.
The meeting between Hemetti and Haavisto took place on Monday in the Kenyan capital, following the envoy’s broader regional consultations that included visits to Sudan and Egypt.
According to statements from the alliance aligned with the RSF, Hemetti urged the UN to accelerate the establishment of offices in areas under its control, arguing that such a step would improve aid distribution to affected civilians.
He also called for an independent international investigation into the origins of the conflict, including allegations of chemical weapons use, and insisted that accountability for the outbreak of war is essential for any political settlement.
Hemetti blamed elements linked to Sudan’s Islamist movement and allied army factions for triggering the conflict, while also criticizing what he described as oversimplified international narratives that fail to account for Sudan’s long-standing political crises.
During his regional mission, Haavisto also met with Abdel Fattah al-Burhan in Port Sudan, as well as Egyptian officials, Arab League representatives, and various Sudanese political actors in Cairo.
The UN envoy reiterated the organization’s commitment to ending the conflict and said consultations are ongoing with all parties to identify pathways toward a political and humanitarian resolution.

title: UN Envoy Meets RSF Leader in Nairobi to Discuss De-escalation in Sudan
excerpt: Nairobi April 6, 2026; The United Nations Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, held talks on Monday in Nairobi with Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” as part of ongoing efforts to explore pathways toward de-escalation in Sudan’s confli
title_en: UN Envoy Meets RSF Leader in Nairobi to Discuss De-escalation in Sudan
excerpt_en: Nairobi April 6, 2026; The United Nations Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, held talks on Monday in Nairobi with Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” as part of ongoing efforts to explore pathways toward de-escalation in Sudan’s confli
body_en:
Nairobi April 6, 2026; The United Nations Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, held talks on Monday in Nairobi with Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” as part of ongoing efforts to explore pathways toward de-escalation in Sudan’s conflict.
The meeting in the Kenyan capital forms part of Haavisto’s first regional diplomatic tour aimed at advancing dialogue between Sudan’s warring parties. It follows earlier discussions in Khartoum with the head of Sudan’s Transitional Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
According to the United Nations, the talks focused on practical steps to reduce violence and improve the protection of civilians. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric described the engagement as a “constructive opportunity” to exchange views, adding that all parties consulted have expressed willingness to cooperate with the UN process.
He stressed that such commitments must quickly translate into tangible progress toward ending civilian suffering.
Prior to arriving in Kenya, Haavisto held consultations in Cairo with Egyptian officials, the Arab League, and representatives of the Sudanese diaspora. The mission comes amid a broader expansion of UN humanitarian operations in Sudan, including the return of Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator Denise Brown to Khartoum with a core UN team, marking a partial re-establishment of UN presence in the city.
The United Nations estimates that more than 1.6 million people have returned to Khartoum in recent months, despite ongoing risks from unexploded ordnance and damaged infrastructure.
Meanwhile, the humanitarian situation remains critical. A recent drone strike on Al Jabalayn Teaching Hospital in White Nile State killed 10 health workers and injured 22 others, according to UN reporting.
The UN’s 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan for Sudan seeks $2.9 billion to assist 20 million people but remains severely underfunded, with only 16% of required funding received to date.

title: Sudan’s Revolutionary Front Opposes Reactivation of Anti-Corruption Committee
excerpt: Sudan March 30, 2026; A Sudanese political coalition has criticized the decision to revive a key anti-corruption body, warning that the move risks deepening divisions amid the country’s ongoing conflict. The Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-Revolutionary Democratic Front (SPLM-
title_en: Sudan’s Revolutionary Front Opposes Reactivation of Anti-Corruption Committee
excerpt_en: Sudan March 30, 2026; A Sudanese political coalition has criticized the decision to revive a key anti-corruption body, warning that the move risks deepening divisions amid the country’s ongoing conflict. The Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-Revolutionary Democratic Front (SPLM-
body_en:
Sudan March 30, 2026; A Sudanese political coalition has criticized the decision to revive a key anti-corruption body, warning that the move risks deepening divisions amid the country’s ongoing conflict.
The Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-Revolutionary Democratic Front (SPLM-RDF), led by Yasir Arman, said the reactivation of the Empowerment Removal Committee (ERC) was carried out unilaterally and without consultation within the broader “Somoud” coalition.
In a statement issued Monday, the group argued that national priorities should focus on addressing the humanitarian crisis and protecting civilians, rather than pursuing political restructuring measures.
The SPLM-RDF has largely suspended its participation in coalition activities since July 2025, citing the need for internal reforms within the alliance led by former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok.
According to the movement, the decision to reinstate the ERC was not discussed through official coalition channels, with many leaders reportedly learning of the move through media reports.
The committee, chaired by former Sovereign Council member Mohamed al-Faki Suleiman, recently announced the resumption of its activities after being dissolved in the aftermath of the October 2021 military takeover. Its ability to operate effectively under current conflict conditions remains unclear.
While reaffirming the importance of dismantling remnants of the former regime, the SPLM-RDF said the ongoing war has shifted national priorities toward ending hostilities and addressing immediate humanitarian needs.
The group also called for broader measures aimed at de-escalation, including facilitating access to education by harmonizing national examinations across conflict zones, ensuring the delivery of humanitarian aid, and improving coordination in critical sectors such as health and currency management.
It further urged warring parties to lift sieges on cities, allow freedom of movement, and commit to halting attacks on civilians and infrastructure, including the use of drones.
The statement concluded with a call for the United Nations Security Council to adopt a binding resolution requiring both sides to implement humanitarian measures and work toward reducing the impact of the conflict on civilians.

title: New Political Alliance Launched in Khartoum to Advocate Civilian Rule
excerpt: Khartoum February 18, 2026; A new political coalition has been formed in Khartoum, marking the first such initiative in the capital since the outbreak of war in April 2023. The alliance, named the Revolutionary Forces for National Issues, brings together several political groups
title_en: New Political Alliance Launched in Khartoum to Advocate Civilian Rule
excerpt_en: Khartoum February 18, 2026; A new political coalition has been formed in Khartoum, marking the first such initiative in the capital since the outbreak of war in April 2023. The alliance, named the Revolutionary Forces for National Issues, brings together several political groups
body_en:
Khartoum February 18, 2026; A new political coalition has been formed in Khartoum, marking the first such initiative in the capital since the outbreak of war in April 2023.
The alliance, named the Revolutionary Forces for National Issues, brings together several political groups and movements, including factions of established parties and youth organizations. Its founding platform calls for national reconciliation, the establishment of a civilian-led government, and the disarmament of all militias.
Among its key objectives is the removal of the military from political life and the restoration of a constitutional system, alongside the creation of a legislative council to guide the transition.
A senior figure within the coalition said the initiative aims to present an inclusive vision that addresses the needs of all segments of Sudanese society. The alliance is also advocating for a national constitutional conference to oversee the transition process and safeguard sovereignty from external interference.
The coalition expressed strong opposition to armed groups, including the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and other militias operating alongside government forces. It called for their dissolution and disarmament, emphasizing the need for a unified national army with exclusive control over the use of force.
The group also highlighted the importance of justice and accountability, proposing transitional justice mechanisms that include compensation for victims, reparations, and institutional reforms to address past violations.
Some political parties involved in the drafting process have yet to formally endorse the alliance, pending internal consultations.
Structurally, the coalition will operate through a leadership body, a general secretariat, and a supreme coordination council, which is expected to include representatives from civil society, youth and women’s groups, professional sectors, and religious organizations.
The alliance underscored that regional and international actors should play a limited role, focusing on facilitating dialogue rather than directing outcomes.
It also confirmed plans to engage with the “Quintuple Mechanism,” a diplomatic framework involving the African Union, Intergovernmental Authority on Development, the United Nations, the Arab League, and the European Union, which is working to support political dialogue and help resolve Sudan’s ongoing crisis.

title_en: Sudan Confirms Arrival of Fuel Tankers at Port Sudan Amid Price Concerns
excerpt_en: Sudan March 31, 2026 ; Sudan’s Ministry of Energy says dozens of fuel tankers carrying petroleum products are currently waiting to unload at Port Sudan, in an effort to ease concerns over potential shortages and recent fuel price increases. The announcement comes after reports of
body_en:
Sudan March 31, 2026 ; Sudan’s Ministry of Energy says dozens of fuel tankers carrying petroleum products are currently waiting to unload at Port Sudan, in an effort to ease concerns over potential shortages and recent fuel price increases.
The announcement comes after reports of rising fuel prices across Port Sudan and several other states earlier in the week. Those increases were later reversed following government intervention, according to officials.
The ministry said more than 10 tankers are currently docked at berths in Port Sudan awaiting discharge, while around 20 additional vessels are positioned in the Red Sea pending entry.
Officials clarified that fuel pricing has not been directly managed by the ministry since 2021, when deregulation policies were introduced. Under the current system, pricing is largely determined by market mechanisms, while the ministry focuses on regulation, import oversight, and supply coordination.
Authorities added that they are working with importers to stabilize supply chains and reduce pressure on consumers, despite volatility in global oil markets.
Sudan remains heavily dependent on imported petroleum products, leaving domestic prices vulnerable to international fluctuations and supply disruptions.
Economic officials have previously warned that ongoing conflict and global energy market instability could continue to strain domestic supply chains, with ripple effects on transportation, electricity generation, and essential services.

title: UN Warns of Life-Threatening Aid Cuts for Sudanese Refugees in Chad
excerpt: Sudan April 9, 2026; More than one million Sudanese refugees in Chad are facing severe reductions in essential humanitarian services as funding shortages threaten to disrupt food, water, shelter, and healthcare assistance, United Nations agencies warned on Thursday. The UN Refuge
title_en: UN Warns of Life-Threatening Aid Cuts for Sudanese Refugees in Chad
excerpt_en: Sudan April 9, 2026; More than one million Sudanese refugees in Chad are facing severe reductions in essential humanitarian services as funding shortages threaten to disrupt food, water, shelter, and healthcare assistance, United Nations agencies warned on Thursday. The UN Refuge
body_en:
Sudan April 9, 2026; More than one million Sudanese refugees in Chad are facing severe reductions in essential humanitarian services as funding shortages threaten to disrupt food, water, shelter, and healthcare assistance, United Nations agencies warned on Thursday.
The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) and the World Food Programme (World Food Programme) said they are confronting a combined funding gap of $428 million, which could force further cuts if not urgently addressed.
The crisis comes as the conflict in neighbouring Sudan approaches its third year, driving mass displacement across borders and placing heavy pressure on host communities in eastern Chad.
According to UNHCR, current resources are sufficient to support only a fraction of the refugee population, leaving large numbers without adequate shelter and basic services. In several camps, water supplies fall far below minimum humanitarian standards, while overcrowding has severely strained education and healthcare systems.
The WFP has already been forced to reduce food rations, with women and children among the most affected. Aid agencies also report that tens of thousands of refugees remain stranded near border areas due to insufficient funding for relocation to safer settlements inland.
Humanitarian officials warn that continued shortfalls could push vulnerable families into increasingly dangerous survival strategies, including reduced meals, unsafe living conditions, and heightened exposure to disease and insecurity.
Chad is now hosting one of the largest refugee populations in the region relative to its population size, with pressure especially acute in eastern provinces where refugees make up a significant share of local communities.
The UN agencies are calling for urgent international support to prevent further deterioration of conditions and to sustain life-saving assistance in the coming months.

title: Sudan Crisis “Internationalized” as Berlin Conference Seeks Aid Mobilization and De-escalation
excerpt: Addis Ababa, April 12, 2026 - The conflict in Sudan has taken on an increasingly international dimension, according to regional and global actors preparing for the Berlin conference aimed at mobilizing humanitarian support and reducing hostilities. A five-member mechanism compris
title_en: Sudan Crisis “Internationalized” as Berlin Conference Seeks Aid Mobilization and De-escalation
excerpt_en: Addis Ababa, April 12, 2026 - The conflict in Sudan has taken on an increasingly international dimension, according to regional and global actors preparing for the Berlin conference aimed at mobilizing humanitarian support and reducing hostilities. A five-member mechanism compris
body_en:
Addis Ababa, April 12, 2026 - The conflict in Sudan has taken on an increasingly international dimension, according to regional and global actors preparing for the Berlin conference aimed at mobilizing humanitarian support and reducing hostilities.
A five-member mechanism comprising the African Union, the United Nations, the European Union, the Arab League, and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) is leading efforts to address the crisis between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Speaking ahead of the conference, Lawrence Korbandy warned that the Sudanese conflict now extends beyond national borders, with significant implications for international humanitarian law and regional stability.
He noted that the Berlin meeting is part of a broader series of diplomatic initiatives focused on addressing the worsening humanitarian situation while building political momentum for de-escalation. However, he acknowledged that global attention has been diverted by other geopolitical tensions, limiting the visibility of the Sudan crisis despite its scale.
Korbandy emphasized that while humanitarian assistance is a central priority, it cannot be entirely separated from the political dynamics of the conflict. He called for a balanced approach that reduces excessive politicization, which he said risks prolonging the war.
The envoy also highlighted the need to unify multiple international initiatives, warning that fragmented efforts could delay meaningful progress in a context where civilians continue to bear the brunt of daily violence.
Despite international engagement, he stressed that a lasting solution must ultimately come from within Sudan. He urged domestic actors to prioritize national interests, while calling on external partners to align their efforts in support of peace.
Korbandy indicated that IGAD is preparing to resume operations in Khartoum, reaffirming the organization’s role as a neutral mediator despite past tensions with Sudanese authorities.
He also cautioned that the prolonged conflict could lead to severe consequences, including the potential fragmentation or collapse of the Sudanese state if no resolution is found.
The Berlin conference is expected to focus on humanitarian access, coordination of aid, and diplomatic pathways to reduce violence, as the international community seeks to respond to one of Africa’s most pressing crises.

title: Sudan Calls for End to Foreign Interference at Antalya Diplomacy Forum
excerpt: Antalya, April 17, 2026 - Sudan’s Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, has called for an end to foreign interference and the influx of foreign fighters, warning that both are major drivers of the country’s ongoing conflict and key obstacles to peace. Speaking on the sidelines of th
title_en: Sudan Calls for End to Foreign Interference at Antalya Diplomacy Forum
excerpt_en: Antalya, April 17, 2026 - Sudan’s Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, has called for an end to foreign interference and the influx of foreign fighters, warning that both are major drivers of the country’s ongoing conflict and key obstacles to peace. Speaking on the sidelines of th
body_en:
Antalya, April 17, 2026 - Sudan’s Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, has called for an end to foreign interference and the influx of foreign fighters, warning that both are major drivers of the country’s ongoing conflict and key obstacles to peace.
Speaking on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkey, Salem outlined the government’s vision for resolving the crisis, centered on a comprehensive peace initiative submitted to the United Nations Security Council. The plan emphasizes a ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and the restoration of state institutions, while reaffirming Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In discussions with the European Union envoy for the Horn of Africa, Anita Weber, Salem stressed the importance of addressing the root causes of the conflict as a prerequisite for long-term stability. The EU representative reiterated support for de-escalation efforts and highlighted the need for coordinated international action to achieve a humanitarian truce as a step toward a permanent ceasefire.
Salem also held talks with senior officials from the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), focusing on regional security risks linked to the spread of mercenaries and the broader implications of the Sudanese crisis for the Horn of Africa.
The Foreign Minister emphasized that improving the humanitarian situation remains a top priority, calling for armed groups to withdraw from civilian areas in Darfur and Kordofan to facilitate aid delivery and enable the safe return of displaced populations. He also welcomed plans by IGAD to deploy a high-level delegation to Khartoum and reopen its office in the capital.
Addressing a high-level panel on Africa’s future, Salem noted that while the continent is rich in natural resources, these assets can also fuel conflict and external competition. He pointed to Sudan’s ongoing war as a stark illustration of how resource wealth can attract foreign involvement and intensify instability.

title: Sudanese Leader, Saudi Crown Prince Discuss Regional Security in Jeddah
excerpt: Jeddah, April 20, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan held talks with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah on Monday, focusing on regional stability and security in the Red Sea region. The unannounced visit came amid reports that Pakistan
title_en: Sudanese Leader, Saudi Crown Prince Discuss Regional Security in Jeddah
excerpt_en: Jeddah, April 20, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan held talks with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah on Monday, focusing on regional stability and security in the Red Sea region. The unannounced visit came amid reports that Pakistan
body_en:
Jeddah, April 20, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan held talks with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah on Monday, focusing on regional stability and security in the Red Sea region.
The unannounced visit came amid reports that Pakistan suspended a $1.5 billion arms deal with the Sudanese army after Saudi Arabia declined to provide financial backing for the agreement.
In a statement, the Sudanese Sovereign Council said the two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and explored ways to strengthen cooperation during discussions held at the Royal Palace.
Al-Burhan expressed appreciation for Saudi Arabia’s support and reaffirmed Sudan’s solidarity with the Kingdom in the face of security threats, while strongly condemning Iranian interference in regional affairs. He also stressed that Saudi Arabia’s security is closely linked to Sudan’s own stability, praising King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for their leadership.
Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for his part, welcomed the Sudanese delegation and highlighted the longstanding historical ties between the two countries, expressing appreciation for Sudan’s positions on regional issues.
Both sides agreed to maintain close coordination and continued consultation on matters affecting regional security and broader Middle East stability. Al-Burhan was accompanied by senior officials, including Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem, General Intelligence Service Director Ahmed Ibrahim Mufadal, and Sudan’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Daffallah Al-Haj Ali.
Ahead of the meeting, diplomatic and security sources cited by Reuters said Pakistan had halted a planned arms and aircraft supply deal to Sudan after Saudi Arabia withdrew its intended financing and requested the agreement be terminated. According to one Pakistani security source, Riyadh had signaled that it should not proceed with funding the procurement, amid wider Western advice discouraging involvement in African proxy conflicts.
Neither the Saudi government media office, the Sudanese Armed Forces, nor Pakistani military officials immediately commented on the reports.

title: Sudan Empowerment Removal Committee Targets Islamic Movement-Linked Assets Abroad
excerpt: Khartoum, April 24, 2026 - Sudan’s Empowerment Removal Committee has announced plans to pursue companies, organizations, and individuals linked to the Islamic Movement through international legal and financial institutions, following the group’s designation as a terrorist entity.
title_en: Sudan Empowerment Removal Committee Targets Islamic Movement-Linked Assets Abroad
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 24, 2026 - Sudan’s Empowerment Removal Committee has announced plans to pursue companies, organizations, and individuals linked to the Islamic Movement through international legal and financial institutions, following the group’s designation as a terrorist entity.
body_en:
Khartoum, April 24, 2026 - Sudan’s Empowerment Removal Committee has announced plans to pursue companies, organizations, and individuals linked to the Islamic Movement through international legal and financial institutions, following the group’s designation as a terrorist entity.
The committee, formally known as the Committee for Dismantling the June 30, 1989 Regime, said it resumed operations on March 17 after a period of suspension. The move follows recent international decisions classifying the Muslim Brotherhood-linked Islamic Movement as a terrorist organization.
Committee officials said the body had been restructured to enable it to operate partly from outside Sudan and to strengthen cooperation with international partners in tracking alleged illicit financial flows and assets. They added that efforts are ongoing to identify networks and individuals linked to the former ruling system within state institutions and abroad.
The committee’s head, Mohamed al-Faki Suleiman, said that assets allegedly transferred overseas by figures of the former regime are under investigation. He also stated that data collection and analysis continued during the suspension period, resulting in a large archive of individuals associated with the dissolved National Congress Party.
Committee rapporteur Salah Manna said the group aims to cut financial channels linked to the Islamic Movement and its affiliated charitable organizations. He warned that individuals and entities engaging in transactions with the group could face legal consequences under its new designation.
Manna further stated that the committee will work with international institutions to monitor financial holdings, alleging that corruption levels during the war and post-coup period are comparable to those recorded during the previous three decades of rule under Omar al-Bashir. He also called on foreign banks to avoid transactions linked to entities under investigation.
Committee spokesman Wagdi Salih urged caution in dealing with assets formerly owned by members of the previous regime, warning that some companies are attempting to rebrand and operate under new identities abroad. He said the committee is tracking such cases closely.
Salih also noted that 109 diplomats previously dismissed by the committee were reinstated following the 2021 coup. He added that authorities have identified 127 diplomats believed to be linked to the Islamic Movement and are engaging with host countries regarding their status.

They added that efforts are ongoing to identify networks and individuals linked to the former ruling system within state institutions and abroad.
The committee’s head, Mohamed al-Faki Suleiman, said that assets allegedly transferred overseas by figures of the former regime are under investigation. He also stated that data collection and analysis continued during the suspension period, resulting in a large archive of individuals associated with the dissolved National Congress Party.
Committee rapporteur Salah Manna said the group aims to cut financial channels linked to the Islamic Movement and its affiliated charitable organizations. He warned that individuals and entities engaging in transactions with the group could face legal consequences under its new designation.
Manna further stated that the committee will work with international institutions to monitor financial holdings, alleging that corruption levels during the war and post-coup period are comparable to those recorded during the previous three decades of rule under Omar al-Bashir. He also called on foreign banks to avoid transactions linked to entities under investigation.
Committee spokesman Wagdi Salih urged caution in dealing with assets formerly owned by members of the previous regime, warning that some companies are attempting to rebrand and operate under new identities abroad. He said the committee is tracking such cases closely.
Salih also noted that 109 diplomats previously dismissed by the committee were reinstated following the 2021 coup. He added that authorities have identified 127 diplomats believed to be linked to the Islamic Movement and are engaging with host countries regarding their status.

title: Sudan’s Agar Urges Expansion of Pro-Army Democratic Block Alliance
excerpt: Port Sudan, April 26, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Deputy Chairman Malik Agar has called for the expansion of the pro-government Democratic Block alliance, urging the inclusion of additional political parties and armed groups to broaden its national representation. Speaking a
title_en: Sudan’s Agar Urges Expansion of Pro-Army Democratic Block Alliance
excerpt_en: Port Sudan, April 26, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Deputy Chairman Malik Agar has called for the expansion of the pro-government Democratic Block alliance, urging the inclusion of additional political parties and armed groups to broaden its national representation. Speaking a
body_en:
Port Sudan, April 26, 2026 - Sudan’s Sovereign Council Deputy Chairman Malik Agar has called for the expansion of the pro-government Democratic Block alliance, urging the inclusion of additional political parties and armed groups to broaden its national representation.
Speaking at the third organizational meeting of the Forces for Freedom and Change - Democratic Block in Port Sudan, Agar said the alliance should significantly increase its membership base, aiming to represent up to half or even two-thirds of Sudan’s political forces.
He stated that strengthening the bloc’s political reach would help demonstrate, both domestically and internationally, that the current political trajectory supported by the government and its allies represents the most viable path forward for the country.
Agar noted that the Democratic Block currently includes 19 parties and armed movements out of a total of 117 registered political and armed entities in Sudan. He emphasized that while these groups may differ in their agendas, they are united by a shared commitment to national unity.
The alliance brings together several pro-government factions, including armed movements that have aligned with the army in its conflict against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), among them the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement, the Sudan Liberation Movement, and the Justice and Equality Movement.
The Sovereign Council deputy chairman reaffirmed support for democratic governance but criticized the adoption of foreign political models, arguing that systems such as those based on Western parliamentary frameworks are not suitable for Sudan’s social and economic realities.
He pointed to the needs of rural populations, including pastoralists requiring veterinary services and farmers relying on traditional agricultural tools, arguing that democracy should be measured by its ability to improve living conditions rather than by imported institutional models.
Agar also accused some political actors of exploiting democratic rhetoric for personal gain, claiming that political principles are often invoked selectively once individuals gain positions of power.
He reiterated his opposition to continued reliance on armed conflict, stating that weapons cannot serve as a foundation for democratic governance. While acknowledging past peace agreements as mechanisms for resolving national crises, he warned that the increasing proliferation of arms across the country requires urgent attention and regulation.

title: Inflation Eases to 40.22% in March Amid Declining Purchasing Power
excerpt: Khartoum, April 16, 2026 - Sudan’s annual inflation rate slowed to 40.22% in March, marking a sharp decline from 56.39% recorded in February, according to official data released by the national statistics authority. Despite the drop, the easing reflects a slower pace of price inc
title_en: Inflation Eases to 40.22% in March Amid Declining Purchasing Power
excerpt_en: Khartoum, April 16, 2026 - Sudan’s annual inflation rate slowed to 40.22% in March, marking a sharp decline from 56.39% recorded in February, according to official data released by the national statistics authority. Despite the drop, the easing reflects a slower pace of price inc
body_en:
Khartoum, April 16, 2026 - Sudan’s annual inflation rate slowed to 40.22% in March, marking a sharp decline from 56.39% recorded in February, according to official data released by the national statistics authority.
Despite the drop, the easing reflects a slower pace of price increases rather than a reduction in the cost of living. Economists point to weakening purchasing power as the primary driver, as households struggle with rising prices and a depreciating national currency.
The slowdown was observed across both urban and rural areas. Inflation in cities fell to 41.33% from 66.98% the previous month, while rural inflation declined to 39.53%, down from 50.86%.
The country’s inflation rate has been on a downward trajectory since reaching a peak of 422% in July 2021. However, the broader economic environment remains strained, with conflict continuing to disrupt production, trade, and income generation.
Data collection challenges persist in conflict-affected regions. Price figures for some states, including North and Central Darfur, were estimated due to limited field access caused by ongoing insecurity.
Inflation trends varied across the country, declining in most states while remaining stable or rising in others. The highest increase was recorded in Blue Nile state, while the most significant declines were observed in North Darfur, Al-Jazirah, and Khartoum.
Food and beverages remain the largest component of household spending, accounting for more than half of total consumption. Housing-related costs and transport also represent significant shares of expenditure.
For many Sudanese, the economic reality remains difficult. With livelihoods disrupted and job opportunities limited, households continue to face mounting pressure as the cost of essential goods and services rises in a fragile economic context shaped by prolonged conflict.

title: MP-Elect Fungaroo Urges Opposition Unity Ahead of 12th Parliament
excerpt: Kampala April 6, 2026 - Obongi County Member of Parliament-elect Hassan Kaps Fungaroo has called for greater unity among opposition parties and urged Ugandans to remain optimistic about the incoming 12th Parliament, set to take shape in May 2026. Speaking during the NBS Morning B
title_en: MP-Elect Fungaroo Urges Opposition Unity Ahead of 12th Parliament
excerpt_en: Kampala April 6, 2026 - Obongi County Member of Parliament-elect Hassan Kaps Fungaroo has called for greater unity among opposition parties and urged Ugandans to remain optimistic about the incoming 12th Parliament, set to take shape in May 2026. Speaking during the NBS Morning B
body_en:
Kampala April 6, 2026 - Obongi County Member of Parliament-elect Hassan Kaps Fungaroo has called for greater unity among opposition parties and urged Ugandans to remain optimistic about the incoming 12th Parliament, set to take shape in May 2026.
Speaking during the NBS Morning Breeze program on Monday, the Forum for Democratic Change (FDC) politician expressed confidence that the new legislature would improve on the performance of its predecessor.
“I want to assure Ugandans that the 12th Parliament will be better. My optimism is that as human beings, we always seek to improve. People should have hope in the 12th Parliament and not dismiss it,” Fungaroo said.
He emphasized the importance of the relationship between the Executive and Parliament, describing it as central to effective governance. Fungaroo pointed to the role of the presidency under Yoweri Kaguta Museveni in shaping how Parliament operates.
“How does the Executive look at Parliament? How will the President see Parliament? That’s the big picture,” he noted.
Fungaroo also highlighted internal divisions within the opposition during the 11th Parliament, which he said weakened its ability to hold the government accountable. He cited tensions among opposition parties, particularly toward the National Unity Platform (NUP), as a key challenge.
“What I saw in the 11th Parliament was some form of resentment from some Opposition parties towards NUP. That was a mistake. We never accepted certain realities and this led to a weaker opposition,” he said.
The MP-elect reaffirmed his commitment to remaining in the opposition, stressing the need to strengthen oversight and accountability mechanisms.
“I have chosen to be in the Opposition offering checks and balances,” he added.
Fungaroo further called for a collaborative approach within the new Parliament, urging citizens to support lawmakers in their legislative work.
“In the 12th Parliament, we are going to work as a team, and we need the support of the citizens of Uganda,” he said.
Uganda’s 12th Parliament is expected to comprise 556 Members of Parliament, including representatives of special interest groups. The legislature will be dominated by the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM), alongside independents and members from parties such as NUP, the Uganda People’s Congress (UPC), FDC, the Democratic Party (DP), the People’s Front for Freedom (PFF), and the Alliance for National Transformation (ANT).
The size of the House has sparked renewed debate over its sustainability, with critics warning that maintaining more than 550 MPs could strain public finances. Others have questioned whether such numbers are necessary for effective representation.
Analysts have also raised concerns about the capacity of the incoming Parliament, noting that nearly 80 percent of its members are newcomers. Some observers warn that the high turnover could affect the quality of debate and legislative scrutiny if not supported by strong institutional frameworks and a clear commitment to public service.

title: South Sudan Speaker Calls Emergency Sitting as Pressure Mounts Over Her Removal
excerpt: Juba April 7, 2026 - South Sudan’s Speaker of Parliament, Jemma Nunu Kumba, has summoned Members of Parliament and government ministers to an extraordinary sitting, as political pressure intensifies following a ruling party move to remove her from office. The emergency session, s
title_en: South Sudan Speaker Calls Emergency Sitting as Pressure Mounts Over Her Removal
excerpt_en: Juba April 7, 2026 - South Sudan’s Speaker of Parliament, Jemma Nunu Kumba, has summoned Members of Parliament and government ministers to an extraordinary sitting, as political pressure intensifies following a ruling party move to remove her from office. The emergency session, s
body_en:
Juba April 7, 2026 - South Sudan’s Speaker of Parliament, Jemma Nunu Kumba, has summoned Members of Parliament and government ministers to an extraordinary sitting, as political pressure intensifies following a ruling party move to remove her from office.
The emergency session, scheduled for April 8, comes days after the ruling Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM) voted to withdraw confidence in her leadership and recommended her dismissal to President Salva Kiir.
Parliamentary spokesperson Oliver Mori Benjamin confirmed the summons, describing the session as unprecedented and instructing all lawmakers and ministers to attend.
“We are in the operations room in Parliament, although it is a holiday. All Members of Parliament and ministers are required to attend this sitting without fail. The agenda will be communicated, but as you are aware, there have been political developments,” he said.
The developments stem from an internal dispute within the SPLM, where a caucus meeting chaired by President Kiir on March 31 reportedly resulted in a unanimous vote of no confidence against Kumba. Lawmakers subsequently recommended her removal, forwarding the decision to the president, who also serves as party chairman.
Reports suggest that a leadership change in Parliament could occur within days, with potential successors already under discussion within party ranks.
In response, the Speaker’s office has challenged the process, stating that Kumba was not given an opportunity to respond to the allegations during the caucus meeting and that no formal parliamentary procedure was followed.
“The Office of the Speaker has taken note of the concerns raised and stands ready to address these matters through appropriate institutional processes,” the statement said.
The emergency sitting places Kumba in the unusual position of convening a session that could ultimately determine her political future.
At the center of the dispute are allegations of financial misconduct raised in a petition by a group of SPLM lawmakers. The claims include funds linked to regional parliamentary games, procurement expenditures, and alleged irregular payments for services. The allegations have not been independently verified, and Kumba has not publicly addressed them in detail.
The controversy has intensified divisions within the ruling party and raised broader concerns about governance and accountability in South Sudan’s legislature.
Analysts say the situation reflects deeper fractures within the SPLM as the country approaches planned elections later in 2026, pointing to a possible realignment of political power within the unity government.
Kumba, who became South Sudan’s first female Speaker in 2021, now faces one of the most significant challenges of her political career, with the outcome of the emergency sitting expected to shape both parliamentary leadership and the wider balance of power in the country.

title: MP-Elect Nkeretanyi Sparks Debate Over Remarks on Parliamentary Role
excerpt: Kampala April 15, 2026 - Kalungu East Member of Parliament-elect Yusuf Nkeretanyi has drawn criticism after stating that he does not intend to actively participate in parliamentary proceedings, arguing that his full service to constituents depends on a change in national leadersh
title_en: MP-Elect Nkeretanyi Sparks Debate Over Remarks on Parliamentary Role
excerpt_en: Kampala April 15, 2026 - Kalungu East Member of Parliament-elect Yusuf Nkeretanyi has drawn criticism after stating that he does not intend to actively participate in parliamentary proceedings, arguing that his full service to constituents depends on a change in national leadersh
body_en:
Kampala April 15, 2026 - Kalungu East Member of Parliament-elect Yusuf Nkeretanyi has drawn criticism after stating that he does not intend to actively participate in parliamentary proceedings, arguing that his full service to constituents depends on a change in national leadership.
Nkeretanyi, a member of the National Unity Platform (NUP), made the remarks during an appearance on Sanyuka Morning Xpress, where he suggested his role in Parliament would be limited under the current administration.
“People from Kalungu don’t really have an MP; I’m just a representative. I’m not going to do anything in Parliament,” he said.
He accused the government of shifting blame onto legislators for its shortcomings. “The government blames Members of Parliament every time it fails the people,” he added.
Nkeretanyi linked his commitment to fulfilling campaign promises to a potential political transition, expressing support for Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, widely known as Bobi Wine.
“If we enter a new Uganda, my people of Kalungu should be rest assured that I will do what I promised and speak for them,” he said.
Reflecting on governance, the MP-elect emphasized the importance of responsiveness in leadership. “Listening and hearing are different-when you listen, you understand. But the government does not listen,” he said.
He also noted that while opposition plays a critical role in a democratic system, it should not be absolute. “We shouldn’t oppose everything, but we also cannot allow everything that is happening,” he added.
In the January 15, 2026 parliamentary elections, Nkeretanyi won the Kalungu East seat with 15,473 votes, defeating former Defence Minister Vincent Ssempijja, who secured 13,219 votes.
His remarks have since sparked debate over the responsibilities of elected representatives and the role of opposition lawmakers in Uganda’s parliamentary system.
body_fr:
