title: Study in Uganda Documents Rare Intergroup Violence Among Chimpanzees in Kibale National Park
excerpt: Uganda April 10, 2026 - Primatologists studying long-term chimpanzee behavior in Kibale National Park have reported a rare and prolonged episode of lethal conflict between two chimpanzee communities that had previously coexisted peacefully for years. The findings, published by re
title_en: Study in Uganda Documents Rare Intergroup Violence Among Chimpanzees in Kibale National Park
excerpt_en: Uganda April 10, 2026 - Primatologists studying long-term chimpanzee behavior in Kibale National Park have reported a rare and prolonged episode of lethal conflict between two chimpanzee communities that had previously coexisted peacefully for years. The findings, published by re
body_en:
Uganda April 10, 2026 - Primatologists studying long-term chimpanzee behavior in Kibale National Park have reported a rare and prolonged episode of lethal conflict between two chimpanzee communities that had previously coexisted peacefully for years.
The findings, published by researchers including University of Michigan anthropologist John Mitani and University of Texas researcher Aaron Sandel, document a breakdown in social relations that escalated into sustained intergroup violence beginning around 2015.
According to the study, the two chimpanzee communities gradually shifted from cooperative coexistence to hostility, with repeated violent encounters leading to a significant number of deaths over several years. Researchers estimate that dozens of individuals were killed during the conflict, including juveniles.
Mitani, who has studied the groups for more than two decades, described the transformation as unexpected, noting that long-standing social tolerance between the communities deteriorated rapidly. Sandel similarly observed that the groups had effectively separated by 2018 following years of escalating aggression.
The researchers report that the conflict involved coordinated group attacks and highly aggressive behavior, including assaults on vulnerable individuals, which contributed to a marked population decline in one of the communities and growth in the other.
They emphasize that such intergroup violence, while rare, has been documented in chimpanzees and may reflect deep evolutionary roots of territoriality and competition among social primates.
The study is being cited in broader scientific discussions about primate behavior, cooperation, and conflict, with researchers noting that it may offer insight into the evolutionary origins of organized group violence.
While drawing comparisons to human conflict is scientifically sensitive, the authors stress that the findings highlight both the complexity of chimpanzee societies and the risks of intergroup competition in species with structured social organization.

title: Uganda Reassures Public Amid Rising Global Fuel Prices
excerpt: April 15, 2026 - The Ugandan government has moved to reassure citizens over concerns about rising fuel prices, stating that sufficient national reserves are in place to cushion the impact of global market fluctuations. In a statement issued on April 14, 2026, authorities indicate
title_en: Uganda Reassures Public Amid Rising Global Fuel Prices
excerpt_en: April 15, 2026 - The Ugandan government has moved to reassure citizens over concerns about rising fuel prices, stating that sufficient national reserves are in place to cushion the impact of global market fluctuations. In a statement issued on April 14, 2026, authorities indicate
body_en:
April 15, 2026 - The Ugandan government has moved to reassure citizens over concerns about rising fuel prices, stating that sufficient national reserves are in place to cushion the impact of global market fluctuations.
In a statement issued on April 14, 2026, authorities indicated that fuel supply remains stable, with an additional 119 million liters expected to arrive via the Port of Mombasa on April 15.
According to the Uganda National Oil Company, the country continues to closely monitor developments in international oil markets, while maintaining that domestic prices are unlikely to experience significant increases in the short term.
Officials attributed the recent rise in global fuel prices to multiple external factors, including currency fluctuations-particularly the strength of the US dollar-as well as ongoing geopolitical tensions involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.
“These global developments continue to influence oil prices worldwide,” the statement noted, while emphasizing that measures are being taken to limit the impact on consumers.
The government added that it is actively managing pricing mechanisms to ensure fuel remains accessible and affordable for the population.
The reassurances come amid heightened volatility in global energy markets, particularly following disruptions linked to tensions affecting the Strait of Hormuz-a critical route through which a significant share of the world’s oil supply passes.
Recent reports indicate that oil prices have surpassed $100 per barrel after ceasefire negotiations involving the United States and Iran failed to yield an agreement, further intensifying uncertainty in global supply chains.
Ugandan authorities say they will continue to monitor the situation closely and adjust policies as needed to maintain supply stability and protect consumers.

title: Uganda Launches National Internet Exchange to Cut Costs and Boost Connectivity
excerpt: Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda has unveiled a national internet exchange platform aimed at reducing bandwidth costs, improving connection speeds, and strengthening the country’s digital infrastructure by keeping local data traffic within its borders. The initiative, launched by
title_en: Uganda Launches National Internet Exchange to Cut Costs and Boost Connectivity
excerpt_en: Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda has unveiled a national internet exchange platform aimed at reducing bandwidth costs, improving connection speeds, and strengthening the country’s digital infrastructure by keeping local data traffic within its borders. The initiative, launched by
body_en:
Kampala April 19, 2026 - Uganda has unveiled a national internet exchange platform aimed at reducing bandwidth costs, improving connection speeds, and strengthening the country’s digital infrastructure by keeping local data traffic within its borders.
The initiative, launched by the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda, introduces the National IP Peering Exchange (NIPX), a system designed to enable internet service providers, telecom operators, and other institutions to exchange data locally rather than relying on international routing.
Officials say the move addresses longstanding inefficiencies in Uganda’s internet ecosystem, where even locally hosted content has often been accessed via servers outside the country-resulting in higher costs and slower performance.
Richard Obita, Director of Technical Services at NITA-U, described the platform as a critical piece of infrastructure that connects local networks on a unified system.
“The National IP… Internet Protocol… exchange is a facility or infrastructure that will interconnect our local ISPs within the country,” Obita said during the launch in Kampala.
He added that the new system will ensure that domestic internet traffic remains within Uganda, reducing reliance on costly international bandwidth.
“This is to keep our traffic local, to keep our data local here,” he said, noting that the initiative is expected to “improve connectivity… [and] lower the cost of bandwidth.”
According to NITA-U, a significant portion of Uganda’s digital content-including locally generated and cultural material-is already hosted within the country but has historically been accessed through international routes. The NIPX platform is intended to eliminate these inefficiencies, enabling faster and more affordable access.
The development marks a significant step in Uganda’s efforts to expand its digital economy and enhance the performance and resilience of its internet infrastructure.

title: DRC moves toward strategic lithium framework balancing investment and local development
excerpt: Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s emerging lithium sector have called for a shared national strategy aimed at balancing foreign investment attractiveness with inclusive local development and stronger governance of natural resources. The
title_en: DRC moves toward strategic lithium framework balancing investment and local development
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s emerging lithium sector have called for a shared national strategy aimed at balancing foreign investment attractiveness with inclusive local development and stronger governance of natural resources. The
body_en:
Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s emerging lithium sector have called for a shared national strategy aimed at balancing foreign investment attractiveness with inclusive local development and stronger governance of natural resources.
The discussions were held over two days in Kinshasa at the Hilton Hotel, bringing together government representatives, industry actors, and civil society under the facilitation of the NGO Resource Matters.
The initiative aims to shape a coordinated vision for the country’s lithium industry as the DRC prepares to begin its first lithium production in 2026, positioning itself as a potential key player in the global energy transition value chain.
Opening the conference, Resource Matters Country Director Jimmy Munguriek emphasized the need to avoid repeating governance challenges experienced in other extractive sectors such as copper and cobalt, calling for stronger local value creation and accountability mechanisms.
Participants stressed that lithium exploitation-particularly in the Manono region and broader Tanganyika province-should be structured to maximize benefits for local communities while ensuring investor confidence.
Officials from the Ministry of Mines highlighted lithium’s growing strategic importance in global markets, particularly for battery production, electric vehicles, and renewable energy storage systems. They stated that the government intends to develop a regulated and traceable supply chain aligned with national and international standards.
The planned framework discussions also drew comparisons with other producing countries, including Zimbabwe, which has adopted policies restricting raw lithium exports in favor of local processing.
The conference sessions covered economic opportunities, governance challenges, industrialization prospects, and local development impacts. Organizers indicated that the outcome of the meetings would be used to formulate recommendations for structuring the sector.
Held behind closed doors, the discussions were intended to encourage open exchange among participants and support the development of a long-term strategic roadmap for lithium exploitation in the DRC.

title: DRC and China sign mineral cooperation agreement in Beijing to strengthen geology and mining sector
excerpt: DRC - China March 26, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and the People’s Republic of China have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at expanding cooperation in geology and mineral resources, marking a new phase in bilateral mining relations. The agreement was signed
title_en: DRC and China sign mineral cooperation agreement in Beijing to strengthen geology and mining sector
excerpt_en: DRC - China March 26, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and the People’s Republic of China have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at expanding cooperation in geology and mineral resources, marking a new phase in bilateral mining relations. The agreement was signed
body_en:
DRC - China March 26, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and the People’s Republic of China have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at expanding cooperation in geology and mineral resources, marking a new phase in bilateral mining relations.
The agreement was signed in Beijing by DRC Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba and Chinese Minister of Natural Resources Guan Zhi’ou, in the presence of senior officials from both countries.
The accord follows high-level discussions between President Félix Tshisekedi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in 2023, and is intended to establish a structured framework for long-term cooperation based on investment, resource governance, and industrial development.
Officials say the agreement emphasizes compliance with Congolese mining regulations, ongoing bilateral consultations, investment protection mechanisms, and increased local processing of raw materials within the DRC.
A key provision of the arrangement includes duty-free access for Congolese exports to China starting May 1, 2026, a measure expected to enhance the competitiveness of the country’s mining sector and support broader economic growth.
The partnership also introduces a monitoring and dialogue mechanism designed to oversee project implementation and ensure transparency in resource development initiatives.
Among the flagship projects outlined is the proposed Greater Orientale Iron Ore Mines (MIFOR), which envisions the development of a major industrial corridor linking the Indian and Atlantic Oceans. The project targets initial production of 50 million tons of iron ore annually, with potential expansion to 300 million tons, backed by an estimated investment of $28.9 billion.
The agreement further encourages Chinese participation in local processing initiatives and the deployment of large-scale industrial infrastructure within Congolese territory.
Congolese officials described the deal as part of a broader strategy to modernize the mining sector, strengthen economic sovereignty, and increase value addition within the country’s extractive industries.

title: DRC Competition Commission strengthens capacity to regulate markets and curb anti-competitive practices
excerpt: Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Competition Commission (COMCO) has held a two-day training workshop aimed at strengthening institutional capacity to enforce competition law and improve market regulation. The session, held at the Novotel Kinshasa under
title_en: DRC Competition Commission strengthens capacity to regulate markets and curb anti-competitive practices
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Competition Commission (COMCO) has held a two-day training workshop aimed at strengthening institutional capacity to enforce competition law and improve market regulation. The session, held at the Novotel Kinshasa under
body_en:
Kinshasa March 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Competition Commission (COMCO) has held a two-day training workshop aimed at strengthening institutional capacity to enforce competition law and improve market regulation.
The session, held at the Novotel Kinshasa under the high patronage of Deputy Prime Minister for National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba, was organized with technical support from European Union experts.
It brought together COMCO staff and other stakeholders involved in the enforcement of competition policy in the country, where regulatory frameworks remain in a consolidation phase.
Participants were trained on key aspects of competition law, including the identification of monopolies, cartels, barriers to market entry, abuse of dominant positions, and illicit exchange of sensitive corporate information.
The workshop also focused on ex-ante regulatory mechanisms designed to prevent market distortions before they occur, particularly in sectors affected by mergers and acquisitions.
Officials said the training combined theoretical instruction with practical case studies to strengthen analytical and enforcement skills, while encouraging exchanges of best practices among participants.
Authorities emphasized that the initiative is part of broader efforts to promote a transparent and competitive economic environment in the Democratic Republic of Congo by reinforcing institutional oversight and improving the application of competition law.

title: Mercuria and EGC sign MOU to develop responsible cobalt supply chain in DRC
excerpt: Shanghai/Kinshasa March 28, 2026 - The Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Mercuria Energy Trading have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and formalizing an artisanal cobalt supply chain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a focus on the Kasulo m
title_en: Mercuria and EGC sign MOU to develop responsible cobalt supply chain in DRC
excerpt_en: Shanghai/Kinshasa March 28, 2026 - The Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Mercuria Energy Trading have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and formalizing an artisanal cobalt supply chain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a focus on the Kasulo m
body_en:
Shanghai/Kinshasa March 28, 2026 - The Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Mercuria Energy Trading have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and formalizing an artisanal cobalt supply chain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a focus on the Kasulo mining site in Kolwezi.
Announced in Shanghai, the agreement seeks to establish what both parties describe as a “gold standard” model for artisanal and small-scale mining, emphasizing transparency, sustainability, and responsible sourcing in cobalt production.
The initiative will involve cooperation with artisanal miners, local cooperatives, the state mining company Gécamines, as well as national and provincial authorities to address key challenges in the sector, including health and safety standards, human rights compliance, environmental protection, and end-to-end traceability.
The framework is expected to align with international guidelines such as the OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Supply Chains and the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, alongside national regulatory standards.
EGC, which oversees artisanal cobalt production in the DRC, and Mercuria, a global commodities trading firm, say the partnership aims to professionalize artisanal mining by improving regulation and ensuring safer working conditions while maintaining supply chain reliability.
The Kasulo project is intended to serve as a pilot model for structured artisanal mining, with ambitions of becoming an international reference point for responsible cobalt sourcing.
Company representatives stated that the collaboration reflects growing global demand for ethically sourced critical minerals used in batteries and energy technologies, and underscores efforts to integrate artisanal mining into formal supply systems.

title: DRC signs $100 million telecom infrastructure deal with Helios Towers to expand national connectivity
excerpt: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has signed an investment agreement worth more than 100 million US dollars aimed at expanding telecommunications infrastructure across several provinces. The agreement was concluded between the National Agency for Investme
title_en: DRC signs $100 million telecom infrastructure deal with Helios Towers to expand national connectivity
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has signed an investment agreement worth more than 100 million US dollars aimed at expanding telecommunications infrastructure across several provinces. The agreement was concluded between the National Agency for Investme
body_en:
Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has signed an investment agreement worth more than 100 million US dollars aimed at expanding telecommunications infrastructure across several provinces.
The agreement was concluded between the National Agency for Investment Promotion (ANAPI) and Helios Towers DRC, a company specializing in the construction and management of shared telecommunications infrastructure.
The project is intended to support the government’s broader digital transformation agenda, aligned with the National Digital and Inclusion Plan 2025 and the “DRC Digital 2030” strategy, which seeks to position the country as a regional digital hub in Central Africa.
According to Helios Towers DRC management, the investment will focus on the expansion of mobile network infrastructure, including the installation of telecommunications towers in both urban and rural areas to improve coverage and service quality.
The company reported that more than 4,000 jobs have already been created through its operations in the country, with expectations of additional employment opportunities as infrastructure deployment expands.
Officials from ANAPI described the agreement as a signal of growing investor confidence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, attributing it to ongoing reforms aimed at improving the business environment and strengthening economic governance.
The initiative is expected to contribute to national development priorities, particularly in improving digital access, fostering economic inclusion, and supporting the structural transformation of the economy through expanded connectivity.

title: DRC and Angola push for deeper economic integration at Kinshasa forum
excerpt: Kinshasa April 1, 2026 - The third edition of the Democratic Republic of Congo-Angola Economic Forum opened in Kinshasa with calls for concrete commitments to accelerate cross-border trade and strengthen regional economic integration. Held under the theme “Sub-regional Integratio
title_en: DRC and Angola push for deeper economic integration at Kinshasa forum
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 1, 2026 - The third edition of the Democratic Republic of Congo-Angola Economic Forum opened in Kinshasa with calls for concrete commitments to accelerate cross-border trade and strengthen regional economic integration. Held under the theme “Sub-regional Integratio
body_en:
Kinshasa April 1, 2026 - The third edition of the Democratic Republic of Congo-Angola Economic Forum opened in Kinshasa with calls for concrete commitments to accelerate cross-border trade and strengthen regional economic integration.
Held under the theme “Sub-regional Integration and the Development of Cross-Border Trade,” the forum brought together government officials, private sector leaders, and economic experts from both countries to build on earlier editions held in Kinshasa and Luanda in 2023.
Opening the discussions, Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba stressed the importance of aligning bilateral cooperation with the broader objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which seeks to boost trade across the continent.
He outlined three key priorities for the discussions: reducing informal cross-border trade, improving payment systems between the two countries, and promoting joint infrastructure and industrial projects to support long-term economic cooperation.
Officials from both sides expressed expectations for tangible outcomes, including new investments, joint ventures, and sectoral agreements in strategic areas such as energy, hydrocarbons, fisheries, and cross-border electricity supply.
Government representatives emphasized that while states are responsible for creating a conducive regulatory environment, the private sector plays a central role in driving investment, innovation, and job creation.
The forum is expected to serve as a platform for strengthening economic ties between Kinshasa and Luanda, while advancing broader regional integration objectives across Central and Southern Africa.

title: South Kivu governor says AFC/M23 control cuts provincial revenue by 84% amid ongoing conflict
excerpt: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, has warned that the province is losing the vast majority of its revenues due to territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, which he says has established a parallel administration in parts of eastern
title_en: South Kivu governor says AFC/M23 control cuts provincial revenue by 84% amid ongoing conflict
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, has warned that the province is losing the vast majority of its revenues due to territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, which he says has established a parallel administration in parts of eastern
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, has warned that the province is losing the vast majority of its revenues due to territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, which he says has established a parallel administration in parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Speaking at a press briefing in Kinshasa on April 2, the governor stated that the occupation of key areas including Bukavu, Walungu, Kabare, and parts of Kalehe has resulted in an estimated 84% loss of provincial revenue.
He explained that South Kivu’s budget, which was projected at around USD 66 million, had effectively collapsed after government authorities relocated from Bukavu to Uvira, leaving major economic zones outside state control.
Purusi further alleged that the AFC/M23 administration generates between USD 17 million and USD 20 million per month through taxation in the occupied areas, claiming that these funds are transferred across the border into Rwanda.
According to him, the group has implemented a structured taxation system over local populations under difficult living conditions, while benefiting from the region’s economic activities.
In response to the fiscal collapse, the governor said he had obtained authorization from Kinshasa to reorganize revenue collection in remaining government-controlled areas, particularly at border points. He suggested that improved digitization, banking access, and streamlined customs systems could help restore up to USD 3-4 million in monthly revenue.
However, he acknowledged that the province’s economic base has been severely weakened due to looting, destruction of infrastructure, bank closures, and the broader disruption of local commerce.
Meanwhile, despite ongoing international diplomatic efforts-including the Washington process and talks mediated in Doha by Qatar-progress toward stabilizing the security situation in eastern Congo remains limited. Both Kinshasa and Kigali continue to trade accusations over violations of existing agreements, while negotiations aimed at restoring state authority and reintegrating armed groups have stalled.

title: DRC stakeholders push for reforms to improve conditions for artisanal miners amid governance concerns
excerpt: Kinshasa April 5, 2026 - A political discussion held in Kinshasa has highlighted the precarious conditions faced by artisanal miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo, calling for urgent reforms to improve governance, safety, and transparency in the sector. Organized on April 2
title_en: DRC stakeholders push for reforms to improve conditions for artisanal miners amid governance concerns
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 5, 2026 - A political discussion held in Kinshasa has highlighted the precarious conditions faced by artisanal miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo, calling for urgent reforms to improve governance, safety, and transparency in the sector. Organized on April 2
body_en:
Kinshasa April 5, 2026 - A political discussion held in Kinshasa has highlighted the precarious conditions faced by artisanal miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo, calling for urgent reforms to improve governance, safety, and transparency in the sector.
Organized on April 2 by the DRC Political Scientists’ Network (Dypol) in partnership with the Friedrich Ebert Foundation (FES), the meeting brought together policymakers, civil society actors, and mining sector experts to examine challenges affecting artisanal mining communities.
Participants noted that despite its major contribution to the national economy and livelihoods of millions, the artisanal mining sector remains characterized by informal operations, weak regulation, unsafe working conditions, child labor risks, and gender inequality.
Speaking after the discussions, Dypol national coordinator Christian Moleka stressed the need for a revised mining code that clearly defines the role of artisanal mining and strengthens oversight mechanisms to improve safety and transparency across supply chains.
He emphasized that artisanal miners are often the most vulnerable actors in a value chain that generates significant revenues, yet they remain marginalized and exposed to frequent accidents and poor working conditions.
Representatives of the Friedrich Ebert Foundation highlighted the importance of promoting more inclusive and sustainable mining governance, where artisanal mining can contribute to long-term development rather than persistent precarity.
Journalist Flore Kayala, who specializes in mining issues, drew attention to the economic role of women in the sector, noting that they remain underrepresented and face limited access to financing and cooperative leadership structures dominated by men.
She called for inclusive policies and better financial support mechanisms to enable women to participate more actively in mining activities and benefit from sector revenues.
The meeting is expected to produce a roadmap aimed at improving coordination between government institutions, civil society, mining companies, and artisanal miners to promote safer, more transparent, and more equitable mining practices in the DRC.
Social and Health

title: DRC-US Migration Arrangement Sparks Debate as First Deportees Arrive in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The implementation of a new migration cooperation agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States has entered its first operational phase, following the arrival of an initial group of deported migrants in the Congolese capital.
title_en: DRC-US Migration Arrangement Sparks Debate as First Deportees Arrive in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The implementation of a new migration cooperation agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States has entered its first operational phase, following the arrival of an initial group of deported migrants in the Congolese capital.
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - The implementation of a new migration cooperation agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States has entered its first operational phase, following the arrival of an initial group of deported migrants in the Congolese capital.
According to government authorities, 15 individuals arrived in Kinshasa on April 17 under what officials describe as a strictly temporary arrangement involving short-stay permits and controlled reception procedures.
The program has drawn political reactions, including from National Deputy and President of the DRC-USA Friendship Group Joseph Bangakya, who defended the agreement and sought to reassure public opinion over concerns about security risks.
Speaking in an interview, Bangakya stated that the Congolese authorities conduct case-by-case verification before approving any entry, insisting that individuals with criminal backgrounds would not be admitted under the arrangement.
He emphasized that the program is designed as a temporary mechanism, with beneficiaries expected to return to their countries of origin after processing, and described their stay in Kinshasa as strictly limited in duration.
The lawmaker also welcomed the broader diplomatic cooperation between Kinshasa and Washington, arguing that recent agreements have strengthened bilateral ties and improved the DRC’s international positioning.
He further linked this diplomatic dynamic to developments at the international level, including shifts within the United Nations Security Council and the adoption of Resolution 2773, which he said reflects increased international engagement on regional security issues.
Government officials have reiterated that the arrangement does not constitute a resettlement policy, but rather a temporary and regulated framework governed by national immigration law and international commitments. They also confirmed that the first phase involves controlled reception conditions, with logistical and financial support provided by the United States.
However, the initiative has sparked concern among opposition figures, civil society actors, and human rights organizations, who question the implications of the agreement and call for greater transparency regarding its scope and implementation.
Some critics have also drawn historical parallels with past humanitarian and cross-border crises in the Great Lakes region, warning about potential security sensitivities linked to population movements in fragile areas.
Authorities maintain that the program is strictly regulated, temporary in nature, and aligned with both sovereignty principles and humanitarian standards.

title: Provisional Governor of Sankuru Calls for Unity After Election Victory
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - Provisionally declared governor of Sankuru province by the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI), following the April 15 vote, Senator Jules Lodi Emongo has called for unity and pledged to meet expectations as he prepares to assume leadership
title_en: Provisional Governor of Sankuru Calls for Unity After Election Victory
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - Provisionally declared governor of Sankuru province by the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI), following the April 15 vote, Senator Jules Lodi Emongo has called for unity and pledged to meet expectations as he prepares to assume leadership
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 19, 2026 - Provisionally declared governor of Sankuru province by the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI), following the April 15 vote, Senator Jules Lodi Emongo has called for unity and pledged to meet expectations as he prepares to assume leadership of the province.
The newly elected governor was received in Kinshasa on April 18 by the Permanent Secretary of the Sacred Union of the Nation, André Mbata, alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs Jacquemain Shabani. The meeting took place at the headquarters of the Sacred Union of the Nation, the ruling political platform supporting President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo.
The discussions focused on consolidating political support following the provisional election results and preparing the incoming provincial leadership for governance responsibilities. Officials urged the new governor to prioritize development, institutional cohesion, and effective administration in Sankuru.
Speaking to the press after the meeting, Lodi Emongo emphasized unity as a central priority for his mandate, describing it as essential for addressing the province’s challenges. He said he was committed to working with all stakeholders to ensure stability and progress in Sankuru.
The Permanent Secretary of the Sacred Union congratulated provincial deputies for supporting the ruling platform’s candidate and urged the incoming leadership to align its actions with the priorities of the national leadership.
The electoral process remains ongoing, with the appeals phase scheduled to run from April 17 to 24 before the Sankuru Court of Appeal acting as an administrative court. Final validation procedures, including judicial review and official proclamation of results, are expected in early May, followed by submission of the file for presidential investiture.
Although Lodi Emongo ran as an independent candidate, he was presented by the Sacred Union as its preferred contender, a political alignment that has reportedly sparked internal tensions within the ruling coalition.
Once confirmed by the courts and formally invested by the Head of State, he is expected to succeed the outgoing provincial governor following institutional procedures governing provincial leadership transitions.

title: DRC Describes Temporary US Migrant Reception as a “Service” Under Bilateral Arrangement
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has said that the country’s temporary reception of migrants deported from the United States is being carried out as a cooperative “service” under a bilateral arrangement between Kinshasa and Washing
title_en: DRC Describes Temporary US Migrant Reception as a “Service” Under Bilateral Arrangement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has said that the country’s temporary reception of migrants deported from the United States is being carried out as a cooperative “service” under a bilateral arrangement between Kinshasa and Washing
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has said that the country’s temporary reception of migrants deported from the United States is being carried out as a cooperative “service” under a bilateral arrangement between Kinshasa and Washington.
Speaking in a media interview, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka confirmed that the program involves the temporary hosting of third-country nationals transferred from the United States, describing the initiative as strictly transitional and time-limited.
She indicated that the individuals concerned are asylum seekers and suggested they originate from several Latin American countries, while noting that their presence in the DRC is part of an agreement involving U.S. immigration authorities and international partners, including the International Organization for Migration.
According to the Prime Minister, the arrangement is not intended as a long-term settlement mechanism, but rather a short-term humanitarian and logistical solution while alternative destinations are identified for the individuals concerned.
She emphasized that the United States is covering all associated costs, including accommodation and basic needs, and described the agreement as a form of cooperation in which the DRC is providing logistical support to a partner country.
Authorities in Kinshasa have reiterated that the program is temporary in nature and will be implemented in compliance with international humanitarian law and national legislation governing the entry and residence of foreigners.
The initiative has already begun with the arrival of an initial group of 15 individuals in Kinshasa on April 17, marking the start of the operational phase of the arrangement.
The program has, however, drawn political attention domestically, with parliamentary questions submitted to the National Assembly seeking clarification on its legal and operational framework. The initiatives have yet to be scheduled for plenary debate.
Government officials maintain that the arrangement is strictly controlled, temporary, and part of broader diplomatic cooperation between the DRC and the United States.

title: DRC Turns to Turkey to Boost Military Capabilities Amid Security Challenges in the East
excerpt: Ankara, April 20, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen defense cooperation with Turkey as part of efforts to modernize and strengthen the operational capacity of its armed forces, the government has announced. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National
title_en: DRC Turns to Turkey to Boost Military Capabilities Amid Security Challenges in the East
excerpt_en: Ankara, April 20, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen defense cooperation with Turkey as part of efforts to modernize and strengthen the operational capacity of its armed forces, the government has announced. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National
body_en:
Ankara, April 20, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen defense cooperation with Turkey as part of efforts to modernize and strengthen the operational capacity of its armed forces, the government has announced.
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita is on an official mission in Ankara, where he visited several Turkish defense industry facilities focused on advanced military technologies.
The visit follows a series of diplomatic and security engagements, including participation in a maritime security forum in Paris and bilateral discussions with French defense officials, as Kinshasa continues to diversify its international defense partnerships.
According to the Ministry of National Defense, the Ankara visit is a technical and exploratory mission aimed at gaining a detailed understanding of Turkey’s defense industrial capacity and identifying potential areas of cooperation in military modernization.
Turkey, a NATO member with a rapidly expanding defense sector, has become a reference point for countries seeking to develop domestic capabilities in areas such as drones, cybersecurity, and command-and-control systems.
During the visit, Congolese officials examined facilities linked to Turkish defense industry actors, including HAVELSAN, a company specializing in software systems, simulation technologies, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity solutions for military and civilian applications.
Authorities in Kinshasa say the objective is to support broader reforms aimed at building a more modern, self-reliant, and operationally effective defense structure capable of responding to evolving security threats.
The mission takes place against the backdrop of ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, where government forces continue to face armed groups, including the AFC/M23 rebellion, as well as broader regional security tensions.
Officials also referenced previous engagements with Turkish defense institutions, including participation in international defense exhibitions and bilateral agreements aimed at strengthening cooperation in military training, equipment, and industrial development.
At the end of his visit, the defense minister expressed satisfaction with the expertise observed and reaffirmed Kinshasa’s intention to strengthen military cooperation with Ankara, particularly in areas related to defense technology transfer and operational capacity building.
The government says such partnerships are part of a broader strategy to modernize the armed forces and enhance national sovereignty in defense capabilities.

title: IOM Clarifies Role in DRC-US Migrant Arrangement as Debate Grows in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has clarified that it does not participate in bilateral agreements such as the arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States concerning the temporary reception of deported m
title_en: IOM Clarifies Role in DRC-US Migrant Arrangement as Debate Grows in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has clarified that it does not participate in bilateral agreements such as the arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States concerning the temporary reception of deported m
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has clarified that it does not participate in bilateral agreements such as the arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States concerning the temporary reception of deported migrants.
The clarification comes after the Congolese government requested humanitarian support for the first group of 15 migrants who arrived in Kinshasa under the agreement between Washington and Kinshasa.
In a statement, the UN migration agency stressed that it is not involved in the negotiation or implementation of bilateral migration deals and reserves the right to limit or suspend its involvement if minimum protection standards cannot be guaranteed. It added that any questions regarding the scope or terms of such agreements should be directed to national authorities.
The IOM also reiterated that its assistance is strictly humanitarian and includes voluntary return programs only when migrants provide free, prior, and informed consent.
The clarification comes amid growing debate over the agreement, which has already seen its first operational phase implemented with the arrival of an initial group of migrants in Kinshasa on April 17.
Government authorities maintain that the arrangement is temporary, regulated under national law, and part of a broader diplomatic cooperation framework with the United States. Officials have described the program as a short-term hosting mechanism rather than a permanent resettlement policy.
However, the initiative continues to generate political and civil society reactions within the country. Critics, including opposition figures and human rights organizations, have raised concerns about transparency, security implications, and the lack of clarity over the migrants’ nationalities and final destinations.
Some voices have also drawn historical parallels with past regional displacement crises in the Great Lakes region, warning about potential risks associated with cross-border population movements in fragile security contexts.
Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has previously described the arrangement as a cooperative service provided by the DRC to the United States, while emphasizing its temporary nature and the fact that the costs of accommodation and support are covered by the U.S. side.
As discussions continue, the government maintains that the framework remains strictly transitional and subject to international humanitarian standards and national immigration law.

title: Mining Sector Under Scrutiny as Government Flags Link to Insecurity
excerpt: Bunia, April 20, 2026 - The Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, has arrived in Bunia for an official visit aimed at assessing the mining sector amid growing concerns over its role in financing armed groups and sustaining insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The
title_en: Mining Sector Under Scrutiny as Government Flags Link to Insecurity
excerpt_en: Bunia, April 20, 2026 - The Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, has arrived in Bunia for an official visit aimed at assessing the mining sector amid growing concerns over its role in financing armed groups and sustaining insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The
body_en:
Bunia, April 20, 2026 - The Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, has arrived in Bunia for an official visit aimed at assessing the mining sector amid growing concerns over its role in financing armed groups and sustaining insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The visit, part of a broader tour covering Ituri, Bas-Uélé, and Maniema provinces from April 19 to 23, focuses on strengthening oversight of both artisanal and industrial mining activities in resource-rich areas, particularly those linked to gold production.
Authorities say the mission seeks to improve governance of the sector, enhance state control over extraction and trade chains, and address informal mining networks that largely operate outside regulatory frameworks.
However, the government acknowledges that mining remains closely tied to insecurity in several territories of Ituri. In areas such as Djugu and Mambasa, mineral exploitation has repeatedly been associated with the financing of armed groups and the expansion of illicit trade networks.
Speaking during the visit, the minister stressed the need for stronger mineral traceability systems and reforms aimed at cutting off illegal flows that deprive the state of revenue while fueling instability.
Local observers and stakeholders have long raised concerns over unregulated extraction, warning that competition for control of mining sites has become a key driver of violence in the region.
In Ituri, minerals are increasingly viewed not only as an economic asset but also as a strategic resource that shapes armed group activity and territorial control. Despite ongoing military operations, weak regulation of extraction and trade continues to sustain a parallel economy linked to conflict dynamics.
The minister’s mission is expected to feed into broader reform efforts, though analysts note that lasting impact will depend on coordinated action between security forces, mining authorities, and governance institutions to disrupt illicit supply chains and restore state oversight.

title: SAEMAPE Launches Artisanal Miner Identification After Evacuation of Radioactive Site
excerpt: Kolwezi, April 7, 2026 - The Service for Assistance and Support of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (SAEMAPE) has launched an operation to identify artisanal miners in Lualaba province, following the evacuation of the T17 tailings site over concerns related to radioactive materia
title_en: SAEMAPE Launches Artisanal Miner Identification After Evacuation of Radioactive Site
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, April 7, 2026 - The Service for Assistance and Support of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (SAEMAPE) has launched an operation to identify artisanal miners in Lualaba province, following the evacuation of the T17 tailings site over concerns related to radioactive materia
body_en:
Kolwezi, April 7, 2026 - The Service for Assistance and Support of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (SAEMAPE) has launched an operation to identify artisanal miners in Lualaba province, following the evacuation of the T17 tailings site over concerns related to radioactive materials.
The T17 site, located within the Kamoto Copper Company concession, was declared a radiological emergency zone, prompting the removal of artisanal miners and triggering a broader reorganization of informal mining activities in the area.
As part of this transition, SAEMAPE began its identification campaign on April 4 at the Kasulo site in Kolwezi. The initiative follows an earlier phase focused on registering mining cooperatives, with the aim of establishing a reliable database of actors operating in the artisanal mining sector.
Officials say the operation is intended to formalize artisanal mining, improve oversight, and enhance safety conditions for miners working in often unregulated and hazardous environments.
SAEMAPE leadership described the process as a key step toward structuring the sector and reducing disorder at mining sites. Provincial authorities emphasized that better identification would also help enforce safety standards and improve governance in mining areas.
On the ground, the process began with the symbolic issuance of identification cards to representatives of several mining cooperatives operating at Kasulo, alongside individual artisanal miners.
Stakeholders involved in the sector have largely welcomed the initiative, viewing it as a move toward greater organization and recognition of their activities. Many miners expressed hope that formal identification would improve working conditions and provide greater legitimacy for their work.
According to SAEMAPE, the initial phase targets miners relocated from the T17 site and plans to redistribute them to designated artisanal zones, including Kasulo, UCK, and Menuiserie.
Authorities indicate that the program will be gradually extended across Lualaba province as part of broader efforts to regulate artisanal mining and strengthen control over mineral extraction activities.

title: ENGIP-RDC and SEP-Congo Sign Oil Infrastructure Management Contracts
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The national oil infrastructure management company ENGIP-RDC SA has signed four operational contracts with SEP-Congo, marking a new phase in the management of petroleum logistics assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The signing ceremony took place
title_en: ENGIP-RDC and SEP-Congo Sign Oil Infrastructure Management Contracts
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The national oil infrastructure management company ENGIP-RDC SA has signed four operational contracts with SEP-Congo, marking a new phase in the management of petroleum logistics assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The signing ceremony took place
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 7, 2026 - The national oil infrastructure management company ENGIP-RDC SA has signed four operational contracts with SEP-Congo, marking a new phase in the management of petroleum logistics assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The signing ceremony took place at the Ministry of Portfolio under the coordination of Minister Julie Shiku, in the presence of the Minister of Hydrocarbons, Acacia Bandubola, along with senior officials from the petroleum sector.
ENGIP-RDC Chief Executive Officer Richard Beya Ilunga described the agreement as a key milestone in securing the continuity and efficiency of oil infrastructure operations, particularly along the strategic supply corridor between Matadi and Kinshasa.
The contracts cover the use of pipelines and associated infrastructure, the rental of industrial equipment, as well as commercial and residential facilities linked to oil logistics operations.
Officials indicated that the agreements have been integrated into the existing petroleum pricing structure, with assurances that they will not negatively impact fuel prices. On the contrary, authorities suggested the arrangement could contribute to reducing logistical costs and improving overall price stability.
SEP-Congo Managing Director Malick Ndiaye welcomed the deal, describing it as a sign of renewed confidence from the government and the outcome of months of negotiations. He emphasized that the partnership is expected to improve operational efficiency and strengthen infrastructure management in the sector.
He added that the collaboration would provide a more stable working environment for oil logistics operations, with anticipated benefits for both public institutions and consumers.
ENGIP-RDC SA, established in January 2026, is mandated to ensure the operation, security, and modernization of national petroleum infrastructure. Authorities say its creation reflects broader government efforts to improve governance of strategic assets and attract investment through a more structured and transparent framework.

body_en:
Antalya, April 7, 2026 - Mali has reinforced its engagement in international sports diplomacy through participation in the 8th World Ethnosports Union Forum held in Antalya, Türkiye.
The Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Education and Citizenship Development, Abdoul Kassim Ibrahim Fomba, attended the closing ceremony of the biennial event alongside several international counterparts.
The forum brought together representatives from multiple countries to promote traditional sports and cultural heritage as tools for social cohesion, peacebuilding, and intercultural dialogue.
Following Mali’s accession to the World Ethnosports Union, Minister Fomba announced a key national priority: the establishment of a Malian Federation of Traditional Sports. This initiative is expected to receive technical support from the Union to develop standardized rules and competitive frameworks.
The Ethnosports movement promotes traditional sporting practices alongside cultural expressions such as music, culinary heritage, and indigenous games, positioning them as instruments for fostering unity and shared identity.
Officials described Mali’s participation as part of a broader effort to strengthen its cultural visibility and expand its sports diplomacy on the international stage.

Bamako, April 10, 2026 - Military cooperation between Mali and the United States was at the center of a closed-door meeting held in Bamako between senior defense officials and the U.S. diplomatic mission.
The United States Ambassador to Mali, Rachna Korhonen, paid a courtesy visit to the Ministry of Defense and Veterans Affairs, where she was received by the Minister of State, Lieutenant General Sadio Camara.
The meeting, which lasted just over thirty minutes, took place at the ministry headquarters around 10:00 a.m. and was held behind closed doors. It was attended by senior Malian military officials, including Major General Oumar Diarra and Major General Sidiki Samaké, alongside members of the minister’s advisory team.
While no official communiqué was released detailing the substance of the discussions, the meeting underscores ongoing engagement between Bamako and Washington on defense-related matters, at a time when Mali continues to face significant security challenges across several regions.

title_en: Mali and Cameroon Pledge to Deepen Bilateral Cooperation After Diplomatic Accreditation

body_en:
Yaoundé, April 8, 2026 - Mali and Cameroon have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening diplomatic and cooperative relations following the presentation of credentials by Mali’s new ambassador in Yaoundé.
On behalf of President Paul Biya, Cameroon’s Minister of External Relations, Lejeune Mbella Mbella, received the Letters of Credence from Nina Oualet Intallou, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Mali, resident in Libreville.
Following the formal ceremony, the Malian diplomat held discussions with the Cameroonian foreign minister, during which she conveyed greetings from Mali’s highest authorities and reiterated her commitment to strengthening friendship and cooperation between the two countries.
Both sides highlighted the long-standing historical and cultural ties linking Bamako and Yaoundé, stressing the importance of preserving and expanding this partnership through renewed cooperation frameworks.
The two parties also called for increased high-level exchanges, revitalized institutional cooperation mechanisms, and stronger people-to-people engagement, emphasizing solidarity and shared interests as the foundation of future relations.

Bamako, April 7, 2026 - Mali has reinforced its partnership with the International Labour Organization in discussions centered on social justice, decent work, and youth employment.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the Director-General of the International Labour Organization, Gilbert F. Houngbo, during an official visit to Mali.
Talks focused on strategies to expand economic opportunities for young people, particularly through projects aimed at strengthening local capacities and promoting employment-driven development. Both sides emphasized the importance of scaling up labor-intensive programs designed to support infrastructure development while prioritizing local labor and materials.
The discussions also highlighted broader multilateral considerations, with Malian authorities urging an approach that takes into account regional realities, including the specific challenges faced in the Sahel and within emerging confederal frameworks.
Officials described the meeting as a step toward deepening cooperation on inclusive development and reinforcing policies that link economic growth with job creation.

body_en:
Bamako, April 4, 2026 - Mali has reaffirmed the strategic importance of its diaspora in national development during a gala event marking five years of activity by the Union of Ambassadors (UDA) in the country.
The event, held in Bamako, brought together members of the UDA, an organization composed of professionals and entrepreneurs, many of whom belong to the Malian diaspora and contribute to socio-economic development initiatives within the country.
Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, attended the ceremony at the invitation of the organization, conveying the congratulations of Mali’s highest authorities to diaspora communities and acknowledging their role in national progress.
In his remarks, Minister Diop emphasized that diaspora contributions extend beyond financial remittances, highlighting their expertise, skills, and civic engagement as key drivers of development. He reiterated government support for initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration between diaspora networks and domestic development projects.
UDA representatives, for their part, reaffirmed their commitment to fostering stronger links between talent, investment networks, and structured development initiatives, with the aim of increasing the impact of diaspora engagement on Mali’s economic and social transformation.

body_en:
Bamako, April 10, 2026 - The Government of Mali has announced a significant shift in its diplomatic position on the Western Sahara issue, withdrawing its recognition of the self-proclaimed “Sahrawi Republic” and expressing support for Morocco’s autonomy initiative.
In an official statement, Bamako described the Moroccan proposal as a “serious and realistic” framework for resolving the long-standing dispute, emphasizing the importance of solutions that respect Moroccan sovereignty. The announcement also highlighted the historical ties between Mali and Morocco, as well as Morocco’s role in supporting regional stability and development.

The announcement has drawn criticism from Algerian sources, which described the move as provocative and questioned the legitimacy of Mali’s transitional authorities to take such a position on the matter.
The development marks a notable recalibration of Mali’s foreign policy orientation within the broader regional diplomatic landscape.

title: Mali Launches National Museum Modernization Project with Spanish Support

title_en: Mali Launches National Museum Modernization Project with Spanish Support
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 21, 2026 - Mali has officially launched an ambitious initiative to modernize and revitalize its National Museum, in partnership with Spain, as part of broader efforts to promote and preserve the country’s cultural heritage. The project, titled “Rethinking the Nation
body_en:
Bamako, April 21, 2026 - Mali has officially launched an ambitious initiative to modernize and revitalize its National Museum, in partnership with Spain, as part of broader efforts to promote and preserve the country’s cultural heritage.
The project, titled “Rethinking the National Museum of Mali,” was inaugurated on Tuesday during a ceremony held at the National Museum of Bamako. The event was presided over by the Minister of Crafts, Culture, Industry and Tourism, Mamou Daffé.
Backed by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), the initiative marks a significant step toward enhancing the museum’s role as a key cultural institution.
The project is structured around three main pillars: strengthening the capacity of museum staff through specialized training, improving the conservation and security of collections, and expanding cultural outreach to engage wider audiences, particularly young people.
Officials emphasized that the initiative aims not only to safeguard Mali’s rich cultural assets but also to make them more accessible and relevant to contemporary society.
The partnership reflects growing cultural cooperation between Mali and Spain, while underscoring the importance of heritage preservation as a driver of education, identity, and sustainable development.

title: Mali-Canada Economic Ties: Diaspora-Led Initiative Seeks to Boost Investment and Partnerships

excerpt_en: Bamako, April 15, 2026 - Efforts to strengthen economic cooperation between Mali and Canada are gaining momentum, driven by a new initiative spearheaded by members of the Malian diaspora. The Minister of Malians Living Abroad and African Integration held talks on Wednesday with M
body_en:
Bamako, April 15, 2026 - Efforts to strengthen economic cooperation between Mali and Canada are gaining momentum, driven by a new initiative spearheaded by members of the Malian diaspora.
The Minister of Malians Living Abroad and African Integration held talks on Wednesday with Moustapha Diop, co-founder of DFA Communication, who presented plans for the establishment of a Mali-Canada Business Council aimed at fostering closer commercial ties between the two countries.
The proposed council, led by a network of Malian and Canadian business leaders, seeks to promote investment opportunities, enhance bilateral cooperation, and support the development of sustainable economic partnerships.
According to its promoters, the organization will bring together around thirty founding members from diverse sectors of the business community, creating a platform for dialogue and collaboration between private sector actors in both countries.
During the meeting, Diop outlined the strategic objectives of the initiative, emphasizing its role in facilitating trade exchanges and encouraging cross-border investment.
The official launch of the Mali-Canada Business Council is scheduled for April 30, 2026, in Bamako, where it will be held under the patronage of the Minister of Malians Living Abroad and African Integration.
The initiative highlights the growing role of diaspora communities in shaping economic diplomacy and contributing to national development through international partnerships.

title: Mali Advances PPP Framework as Government Moves to Standardize Investment Tools
excerpt: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Mali is taking a significant step toward strengthening its infrastructure financing strategy through the development of a standardized framework for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, acting on behalf of the
title_en: Mali Advances PPP Framework as Government Moves to Standardize Investment Tools
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Mali is taking a significant step toward strengthening its infrastructure financing strategy through the development of a standardized framework for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, acting on behalf of the
body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Mali is taking a significant step toward strengthening its infrastructure financing strategy through the development of a standardized framework for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).
Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, acting on behalf of the Head of State, officially launched a workshop on Monday dedicated to validating key standard documents that will guide the implementation of PPP projects across the country.
The initiative is part of broader efforts to address Mali’s infrastructure deficit while improving the quality and sustainability of public investments. Authorities aim to leverage private sector participation as a strategic mechanism to mobilize financing, enhance efficiency, and ensure the optimal use of public resources.
Officials emphasized that the PPP framework aligns with Mali’s long-term development vision, known as “Mali Kura Ɲɛtaasira ka bɛn san 2063 ma,” as well as the National Strategy for Emergence and Sustainable Development (SNEDD) 2024-2033.
At the core of the reform are several draft standard documents currently under review. These include a methodological guide for PPP implementation, model tender and consultation documents, and standardized contractual clauses designed to establish a coherent and transparent structure for partnerships between the public and private sectors.
The adoption of these tools is expected to streamline project development, reduce risks for investors, and improve governance in infrastructure delivery.
In a related development, Mali’s economic outlook was also highlighted during a session of the National Credit Council of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) in Mali. Minister of Economy and Finance Alousséïni Sanou pointed to key strengths of the national economy, including a positive trade balance and a resilient banking sector with strong liquidity levels.
Together, these developments signal Mali’s intent to reinforce its economic foundations while creating a more attractive environment for both domestic and international investment.

body_en:
Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Mali’s economic and financial situation came under review as the National Credit Council of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) convened under the chairmanship of Minister of State and Minister of Economy and Finance, Alousséïni Sanou.
The meeting brought together council members alongside national representatives of the BCEAO to assess the performance and operating conditions of the country’s banking and financial system, with a particular focus on private sector financing.
The council serves as a key platform for evaluating economic trends and ensuring that financial institutions effectively support national development priorities.
Discussions during the session covered a range of issues, including the overall health of the banking sector and its capacity to meet the financing needs of businesses and economic operators.
Following the closed-door deliberations, Minister Sanou indicated that several matters were examined, with some presented for information and others leading to concrete decisions by the council.
He also highlighted the resilience of Mali’s economy, pointing to a positive trade balance and a well-liquidated banking sector as key indicators of stability.
The meeting underscores ongoing efforts by Malian authorities and regional financial institutions to maintain sound economic governance and strengthen the role of the financial system in supporting growth.

title: WAEMU Workshop in Bamako Highlights Role of Mutual Societies in Universal Health Coverage
excerpt: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Experts and stakeholders gathered in Bamako on Monday for a national workshop dedicated to the dissemination and training on West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) provisions governing the management and supervision of mutual societies and their
title_en: WAEMU Workshop in Bamako Highlights Role of Mutual Societies in Universal Health Coverage
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Experts and stakeholders gathered in Bamako on Monday for a national workshop dedicated to the dissemination and training on West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) provisions governing the management and supervision of mutual societies and their
body_en:
Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Experts and stakeholders gathered in Bamako on Monday for a national workshop dedicated to the dissemination and training on West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) provisions governing the management and supervision of mutual societies and their umbrella organizations.
The workshop focused on regulatory standards, including prudential ratios and oversight mechanisms, aimed at strengthening the governance of mutual health organizations across member states.
Participants underscored the strategic importance of mutual societies in expanding social protection systems and reinforcing solidarity within the WAEMU space. These organizations were presented as key instruments for advancing Universal Health Coverage, a shared policy priority among member countries.
In his opening remarks, the WAEMU representative stressed that mutual societies play a central role in extending health insurance coverage, particularly in communities where access to formal healthcare financing remains limited. The workshop seeks to position these structures as a major lever for consolidating the social protection floor within the regional community.
The initiative forms part of broader regional efforts to harmonize social protection policies and improve access to healthcare services through community-based and inclusive financing mechanisms.
In a separate development, Mali continues to expand its international academic cooperation. The Rector of Al-Moustapha University was received by Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye, in discussions focused on strengthening university partnerships between Mali and Iran.

Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Opportunities for enhanced cooperation in the telecommunications sector were at the center of discussions on Tuesday between the Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, and the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer of Moov Africa Malitel, Abdellah Tabhiret.
During the meeting, Minister Ag Attaher extended his congratulations to the new CEO, wishing him success in his leadership of the telecommunications company.
The discussions focused on consolidating the existing partnership between the ministry and Moov Africa Malitel, with both parties expressing a shared commitment to strengthening collaboration.

The meeting reflects ongoing efforts to deepen public-private partnerships in the ICT sector, with a focus on improving accessibility, service delivery, and engagement with Malian communities worldwide.

excerpt_en: Mogadishu, April 6, 2026 - A new milestone in regional scientific cooperation was marked with the launch of an artificial intelligence initiative aimed at strengthening digital tools for the Somali language, through collaboration between Djibouti and Somalia. The initiative was p
body_en:
Mogadishu, April 6, 2026 - A new milestone in regional scientific cooperation was marked with the launch of an artificial intelligence initiative aimed at strengthening digital tools for the Somali language, through collaboration between Djibouti and Somalia.
The initiative was presented during a ceremony held at the Jazeera Hotel in Mogadishu, bringing together researchers, policymakers, and academic institutions. Two major developments were unveiled: a research project focused on detecting fake news in Somali-language social media content, and the launch of the Somali-Language AI & Innovation Lab (SAIL).
The research project, titled “Somali-Written Fake News on Social Media using NLP & Deep Learning,” applies natural language processing and deep learning techniques to identify misinformation targeting Somali-speaking users online.
The program is the result of collaboration between the University of Djibouti, through its Center for Research in Mathematics and Digital Technology (CRMN) and CEALT, and Jamhuuriya University of Science and Technology in Mogadishu, via its Center for Graduate Studies.
Djiboutian researchers, including Houssein Ahmed Assoweh, Director of CRMN, and Souleiman Omar Hoch, Director of CEALT, played key roles in the development and implementation of the project.
Officials described the initiative as part of a broader strategy to position the Horn of Africa as an emerging hub for artificial intelligence applied to African languages. Beyond institutional cooperation, the project aims to expand the use of Somali in modern digital technologies.
The research has already received international recognition, including the Best Paper Award at the AfricaNLP workshop, held within the ACI international conference, a major event in the field of artificial intelligence and natural language processing.
According to researchers involved in the project, the long-term objective is to strengthen the presence of Somali in digital ecosystems, enabling applications such as machine translation, voice assistants, education technologies, and misinformation detection tools.
“This collaboration is set to strengthen in order to put artificial intelligence at the service of the linguistic and cultural preservation of the Somali language,” said Assoweh. “Our objective is to transform Somali from a language with limited resources to one fully equipped and integrated into modern technologies.”
The initiative reflects a growing emphasis on regional cooperation in innovation and digital sovereignty, with both countries seeking to attract international funding and build sustainable AI capacity in the region.

title: Djibouti Economic Task Force Engages Private Sector Over Regional Supply Chain Pressures
excerpt: Djibouti, April 12, 2026 - The National Task Force on the economy met on Sunday with private sector representatives to assess the impact of ongoing tensions in the Middle East on Djibouti’s trade flows and supply chains. Chaired by the Minister of Economy and Finance, Ilyas Mouss
title_en: Djibouti Economic Task Force Engages Private Sector Over Regional Supply Chain Pressures
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 12, 2026 - The National Task Force on the economy met on Sunday with private sector representatives to assess the impact of ongoing tensions in the Middle East on Djibouti’s trade flows and supply chains. Chaired by the Minister of Economy and Finance, Ilyas Mouss
body_en:
Djibouti, April 12, 2026 - The National Task Force on the economy met on Sunday with private sector representatives to assess the impact of ongoing tensions in the Middle East on Djibouti’s trade flows and supply chains.
Chaired by the Minister of Economy and Finance, Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh, the meeting brought together government officials and business leaders, including the President of the Chamber of Commerce, Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh.
According to officials, discussions focused on disruptions to supply chains, delays in deliveries, and rising logistics costs linked to instability in a key global trade corridor used for energy and essential goods transport.
Business leaders were invited to present their assessment of the situation and its concrete effects on commercial activity and pricing within the domestic market.
The Minister of Economy and Finance reassured participants that national stocks of essential goods remain sufficient for several months, adding that hydrocarbon reserves are secured through June.
He also praised wholesale operators for what he described as their contribution to maintaining relative price stability under difficult conditions. However, he strongly criticized certain retail practices, warning against opportunistic price increases. “This is unacceptable,” he said, adding that authorities would take strict measures to prevent speculation.
The meeting forms part of the ongoing work of the National Task Force, a framework designed to maintain continuous dialogue between the state and economic actors in order to manage external shocks and reinforce national economic resilience.
Social and Health
