title_en: Deepen Investment Ties as Chinese Delegation Explores Coffee, Industry and Tourism Opportunities
excerpt_en: Uganda, China April 13, 2026 - A high-level Chinese business delegation is currently in Uganda to explore investment opportunities in coffee production, industrial infrastructure, and tourism, as Kampala strengthens its economic partnership with China. The visit forms part of the
body_en:
Uganda, China April 13, 2026 - A high-level Chinese business delegation is currently in Uganda to explore investment opportunities in coffee production, industrial infrastructure, and tourism, as Kampala strengthens its economic partnership with China.
The visit forms part of the Uganda-China Coffee Investment and Destination Tour 2026, a coordinated initiative aimed at expanding trade, investment flows, and market linkages between the two countries. The delegation arrived this week and will remain in Uganda from April 10 to 23, 2026.
The mission is being facilitated by Uganda’s diplomatic missions in Beijing and Guangzhou, and brings together representatives from several major Chinese companies, including firms operating in manufacturing, infrastructure, agriculture, and tourism.
During their stay, investors are expected to tour key industrial zones such as the Sino-Uganda Mbale Industrial Park, Liao Shen Industrial Park, and Namanve Industrial Park, where they will assess potential opportunities in manufacturing, infrastructure development, and export-oriented production.
A central focus of the visit is Uganda’s coffee sector, one of the country’s top foreign exchange earners. Delegates will engage directly with producers at the Ankole Coffee Producers Cooperative Union and visit a coffee processing facility in Bushenyi to observe the full value chain from production to export.
The programme also includes an extensive tourism component designed to showcase Uganda’s natural attractions. The delegation is scheduled to visit Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, Queen Elizabeth National Park, Rwenzori Mountains National Park, and the Source of the Nile, highlighting the country’s biodiversity and tourism potential.
Officials say the combined investment and tourism exposure is intended to position Uganda as a competitive destination for both foreign direct investment and international tourism, particularly targeting Asian markets.
The Uganda-China Coffee Investment and Destination Tour reflects broader efforts to deepen bilateral cooperation in agro-industrialisation, tourism development, mineral-based industrialisation, and science and technology.
Government authorities in Kampala say the initiative is expected to enhance market access for Ugandan exports, attract new investment inflows, and strengthen long-term economic cooperation between Uganda and China.

title: Uganda Maintains Lower Fuel Prices Than Regional Neighbours Despite Global Oil Shock
excerpt: Kampala April 15, 2026 - Uganda continues to record comparatively lower fuel prices than several East African countries, even as a global surge in crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions drive up pump costs across the region. International oil markets have remained under press
title_en: Uganda Maintains Lower Fuel Prices Than Regional Neighbours Despite Global Oil Shock
excerpt_en: Kampala April 15, 2026 - Uganda continues to record comparatively lower fuel prices than several East African countries, even as a global surge in crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions drive up pump costs across the region. International oil markets have remained under press
body_en:
Kampala April 15, 2026 - Uganda continues to record comparatively lower fuel prices than several East African countries, even as a global surge in crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions drive up pump costs across the region.
International oil markets have remained under pressure in recent weeks, with crude prices exceeding $100 per barrel amid supply disruptions and heightened instability in the Middle East since late February 2026. The situation has been further aggravated by rising freight and insurance costs affecting global fuel shipments.
Despite these challenges, Uganda remains slightly more affordable at the pump compared to its regional peers, including Kenya, Rwanda, and Burundi, though it remains dependent on fuel imports routed through the Kenyan corridor.
Regional price comparison
In Kenya, petrol averages about Shs5,871 per litre, with diesel at similar levels. In contrast, Uganda’s petrol prices stand at approximately Shs5,244 per litre, while diesel averages around Shs5,085, although prices in parts of Kampala have reportedly reached about Shs5,600.
In Rwanda, petrol is priced at around Shs5,814 and diesel at Shs5,558, while Tanzania records averages of Shs5,415 for petrol and Shs5,387 for diesel. Ethiopia remains significantly lower, with petrol at roughly Shs3,363 and diesel at Shs3,848. Burundi reports average prices of about Shs4,959 for petrol and Shs4,874 for diesel.
Structural reforms and supply chain changes
Uganda’s relatively lower prices have been partly attributed to reforms in its fuel importation system. In 2024, authorities implemented the Petroleum Supply (Amendment) Act, 2023, which assigned the Uganda National Oil Company (UNOC) sole responsibility for fuel imports.
The reform reduced reliance on intermediaries in Kenya, a system previously criticised for adding costs through middlemen margins. Uganda now directly sources fuel from international suppliers under long-term contracts, while still relying on regional infrastructure for transportation.
Taxation differences across East Africa also continue to shape retail prices. Kenya applies relatively higher fuel taxes, including a 16% Value Added Tax alongside excise duties and other levies, contributing significantly to higher pump prices. Uganda’s tax regime remains comparatively lower, helping cushion consumers against global shocks.
In Rwanda, fuel pricing is tightly regulated, with the government periodically setting maximum retail prices and occasionally subsidising costs to stabilise the market during global price spikes.
Supply outlook and government assurances
Ugandan authorities have sought to reassure the public over fuel availability, noting that additional shipments are expected to strengthen national reserves.
The Uganda National Oil Company confirmed that about 119 million litres of fuel were expected to arrive through Mombasa on Wednesday to boost national stock levels.
“This shipment will further strengthen national fuel reserves and ensure continued availability across the country,” UNOC said.
The developments underscore how global market volatility, national procurement systems, taxation policies, and regional logistics continue to shape fuel price dynamics across East Africa.

title: Uganda Courts Chinese Investors in ATMS-Led Economic Transformation DriveKampala April 16, 2026 - Uganda has intensified efforts to attract foreign capital under its long-term economic transformation strategy following a high-level engagement between the Ministry of Finance and a 40-member delegation of Chinese investors exploring opportunities across key priority sectors.

title_en: Uganda Courts Chinese Investors in ATMS-Led Economic Transformation DriveKampala April 16, 2026 - Uganda has intensified efforts to attract foreign capital under its long-term economic transformation strategy following a high-level engagement between the Ministry of Finance and a 40-member delegation of Chinese investors exploring opportunities across key priority sectors.
excerpt_en: The visit underscores deepening economic cooperation between Uganda and China, while reinforcing Kampala’s ambition to position itself as a competitive investment hub within East Africa and the broader African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Minister of State for Investment
body_en:
The visit underscores deepening economic cooperation between Uganda and China, while reinforcing Kampala’s ambition to position itself as a competitive investment hub within East Africa and the broader African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).
Minister of State for Investment and Privatisation, Evelyn Anite, described the engagement as a significant milestone in advancing Uganda’s “tenfold growth strategy,” which seeks to expand the country’s Gross Domestic Product to approximately US$500 billion over the long term.
“The delegation’s investment interests are closely aligned with Uganda’s development blueprint. Foreign direct investors are increasingly focusing on agriculture, manufacturing, and tourism, which remain central to structural transformation and economic expansion,” Anite said.
The Chinese delegation has already undertaken sector-specific visits, including tourism sites, and is now advancing discussions into manufacturing value chains. Officials say the progression from exploratory visits to structured engagements signals potential long-term investment commitments.
Strategic Investment Sectors
Uganda presented investment opportunities under its ATMS framework-Agriculture, Tourism, Manufacturing, and Science & Technology.
In agriculture and agro-processing, Uganda remains Africa’s leading exporter of Robusta coffee, generating US$1.5 billion in export earnings in 2024, a 60 percent year-on-year increase. Authorities say this growth creates strong prospects for value addition and agro-industrial expansion.
The mining sector also features prominently, with deposits of gold, phosphates, iron ore, cobalt, and rare earth minerals. Existing infrastructure such as the Entebbe gold refinery and active mining operations in Busia enhance the sector’s attractiveness. Uganda’s emerging oil and gas industry-anchored by the Tilenga and Kingfisher projects and the East African Crude Oil Pipeline-adds further strategic weight.
Tourism continues to expand, driven by attractions including mountain gorilla tracking, the River Nile, and national parks. The sector currently records over 1.5 million tourist nights annually, with growing demand for hospitality infrastructure and eco-tourism facilities.
Manufacturing has also shown strong momentum, with export earnings reaching US$8.7 billion in 2024, representing a 26 percent increase from the previous year. Uganda is leveraging industrial parks, competitive energy costs, and preferential access to regional and continental markets through the East African Community and AfCFTA.
The ICT and digital economy is emerging as another growth frontier, expanding by 16.2 percent in 2024, supported by fintech innovation, start-up ecosystems, and a youthful population.
Expanding Bilateral Economic Cooperation
Key areas of proposed collaboration include agro-industrial processing, mineral beneficiation, infrastructure development, and expanded exports of coffee and agro-commodities to the Chinese market, coordinated through the Uganda Investment Authority.
Uganda’s Ambassador to China, Oliver Wonekha, said the visiting delegation is conducting a comprehensive assessment of the country’s investment climate.
She noted that investors are reviewing incentives such as tax exemptions, regulatory facilitation, and profit repatriation guarantees, adding that the mission reflects growing confidence in Uganda’s economic trajectory and bilateral relations with China.
Macroeconomic Outlook
Uganda’s economy, valued at approximately US$61.3 billion, is projected to grow by 6.3 percent in the 2024/25 financial year, with inflation remaining below 5 percent.
With a population exceeding 45.9 million and a median age of 17, Uganda offers a large and youthful labour force. The country also maintains a liberalised investment regime allowing 100 percent profit repatriation and provides access to a combined market of over 300 million people within the East African Community and approximately 1.4 billion under the African Continental Free Trade Area.
Officials say ongoing infrastructure development, macroeconomic stability, and logistics improvements continue to strengthen Uganda’s positioning as a regional investment destination.

title: Uganda, World Bank Chart New Financing Path at Spring Meetings
excerpt: Washington, D.C. April 16, 2026 - Uganda has engaged in high-level discussions with the World Bank’s Africa leadership on future financing priorities, economic growth, and development cooperation, as part of the ongoing Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the W
title_en: Uganda, World Bank Chart New Financing Path at Spring Meetings
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. April 16, 2026 - Uganda has engaged in high-level discussions with the World Bank’s Africa leadership on future financing priorities, economic growth, and development cooperation, as part of the ongoing Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the W
body_en:
Washington, D.C. April 16, 2026 - Uganda has engaged in high-level discussions with the World Bank’s Africa leadership on future financing priorities, economic growth, and development cooperation, as part of the ongoing Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank in Washington, D.C.
The Ugandan delegation met with the World Bank Vice President for the Africa region, Ndiame Diop, to review the country’s macroeconomic performance and assess the status of the Bank’s expanding portfolio in Uganda.
Uganda’s Minister of State for Finance in charge of General Duties said the economy continues to demonstrate resilience despite global headwinds, with growth currently estimated at 6.3 percent and projected to rise to between 6.5 and 7 percent by the end of the financial year.
He noted that the medium-term outlook remains robust, with the government targeting double-digit growth rates as part of its long-term ambition to expand the economy tenfold by 2040.
“This growth trajectory is well aligned with our ambition to grow the economy tenfold by 2040,” the minister said.
Expanding Financing Portfolio
Uganda’s World Bank portfolio has grown significantly, increasing from US$3.9 billion in March 2025 to approximately US$4.74 billion, now covering 18 active projects and programmes across multiple sectors.
The government welcomed the Bank’s recent approval of the Uganda Cities and Municipal Infrastructure Programme, as well as additional financing for the Integrated Water Management Development Project.
Officials also expressed optimism over pending approvals, including the Uganda-Tanzania transmission line project and further funding for Lot 1 of the North Eastern Road Asset Management Project.
Focus on Strategic Infrastructure
Uganda is seeking enhanced World Bank support through a programmatic financing approach targeting key growth drivers under its tenfold strategy. Priority areas include development of the Standard Gauge Railway, expansion of hydropower generation, and investments in urban infrastructure such as drainage systems and waste management.
Additional focus areas include strengthening electricity transmission networks, particularly in industrial parks, and improving private sector access to credit through development policy operations.
World Bank Perspective
Ndiame Diop commended Uganda for maintaining macroeconomic stability but emphasized the need to ensure that growth translates into tangible outcomes, particularly job creation and poverty reduction.
He also praised Uganda’s progressive refugee policy, noting that the World Bank is prepared to design a dedicated programme to support refugee-hosting communities.
At the same time, Diop called for improvements in project implementation, highlighting the importance of efficiency and faster disbursement to accelerate development impact.
Sector Reforms and Technical Discussions
The two sides also reviewed the INVITE export guarantee scheme, with discussions pointing to the need for restructuring to better align it with beneficiary needs.
In the energy sector, technical engagements focused on reforms aimed at improving efficiency, performance, and sustainability.
Japan Cooperation on Infrastructure
In a separate meeting, Uganda’s delegation held talks with officials from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), including Yushi Nagano and Shinohara Shunei, to explore financing for major infrastructure projects.
Key proposals include the Kampala Flyover Project and the Kampala Metropolitan Transmission System, both designed to enhance urban mobility and strengthen electricity transmission capacity in the greater Kampala area.
Officials say the engagements reflect Uganda’s broader strategy to mobilize diversified financing partnerships to support infrastructure development, sustain economic growth, and accelerate progress toward its 2040 transformation agenda.

title: Two Finance Bills Cleared to Boost Rural Development and Economic Recovery
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The National Assembly has declared admissible two draft finance laws aimed at supporting rural development and economic recovery, marking an initial step toward the approval of new development funding agreements. The texts, presented during Tuesday’s ple
title_en: Two Finance Bills Cleared to Boost Rural Development and Economic Recovery
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The National Assembly has declared admissible two draft finance laws aimed at supporting rural development and economic recovery, marking an initial step toward the approval of new development funding agreements. The texts, presented during Tuesday’s ple
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The National Assembly has declared admissible two draft finance laws aimed at supporting rural development and economic recovery, marking an initial step toward the approval of new development funding agreements.
The texts, presented during Tuesday’s plenary session by Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba Likunde Li-Botayi, relate to the ratification of loan agreements concluded with international financial partners, including the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa, the International Fund for Agricultural Development, and the OPEC Fund for International Development.
Following deliberations described as constructive, lawmakers referred the proposals to a joint parliamentary committee for detailed examination ahead of final adoption.
The financing package, valued at approximately 150 million US dollars, is intended to support key government priorities under the social development agenda of President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo.
Two major programs are central to the funding. The first, the Inclusive and Resilient Rural Development Support Program (PADRIR), allocated 70 million US dollars, focuses on reducing poverty and improving connectivity in provinces including Maniema, Lomami, Kasai-Central, and Kasai-Oriental. Planned interventions include the rehabilitation of nearly 1,000 kilometers of rural roads, notably the Kindu-Kasongo axis, as well as the development of social infrastructure expected to benefit more than one million people.
The second initiative, the Agricultural SME Incubator Project (PIIPME), with a budget of 16 million US dollars, aims to promote entrepreneurship and employment among young people and women. The project plans to establish eight modern incubation centers across several provinces, including Tanganyika, North Kivu, and Kongo Central, to support local processing of agricultural products such as cassava, maize, coffee, and cocoa.
The Finance Minister described the programs as strategic investments designed to promote social equity, strengthen national cohesion, and improve food security while stimulating local economies.
The government expressed optimism that parliamentary review will proceed swiftly, allowing for the rapid disbursement of funds and the timely implementation of the projects in rural communities.

title: DRC’s First Eurobond “Mbote” Marks $1.25 Billion Breakthrough into Global Markets
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 9-14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed a historic entry into international capital markets with the successful issuance of its first Eurobond, raising $1.25 billion in a transaction that officials describe as a major milestone in the country’s
title_en: DRC’s First Eurobond “Mbote” Marks $1.25 Billion Breakthrough into Global Markets
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 9-14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed a historic entry into international capital markets with the successful issuance of its first Eurobond, raising $1.25 billion in a transaction that officials describe as a major milestone in the country’s
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 9-14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed a historic entry into international capital markets with the successful issuance of its first Eurobond, raising $1.25 billion in a transaction that officials describe as a major milestone in the country’s economic transformation.
The operation, carried out under the leadership of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo and coordinated through the Ministry of Finance led by Doudou Fwamba, was presented as both a financing breakthrough and a signal of improved sovereign credibility on global markets.
Dubbed “Mbote,” the issuance attracted strong investor interest, with total demand exceeding $5.3 billion-more than four times the amount raised. It was structured in two tranches, comprising $600 million over five years at 8.75% and $650 million over ten years at 9.00%.
Government officials said the oversubscription reflects growing international confidence in the country’s macroeconomic management and reform trajectory, supported by improved fiscal discipline and stabilizing economic indicators.
Prior to the issuance, authorities conducted investor roadshows in major financial centers including Washington, New York, London, and Paris to present the country’s economic outlook, reform agenda, and development priorities.
The proceeds will be allocated to priority infrastructure projects under the 2024-2028 national development program, notably the modernization of N’djili International Airport, the construction of the Katende hydroelectric dam, and improvements to interprovincial transport infrastructure aimed at boosting urban mobility and economic integration.
The transaction was supported by an international banking consortium including Citigroup and Standard Chartered Bank, alongside local institution Rawbank, which participated in structuring and coordination.
Officials emphasized that the Eurobond also reflects a broader improvement in macroeconomic stability, with inflation contained at around 2.3%, public debt estimated at about 18% of GDP, and growth averaging around 7% in recent years. They added that reserves remain sufficient to cover at least three months of imports, reinforcing external stability.
Finance authorities described the issuance as recognition of improved sovereign credit perception, attributing progress to reforms implemented since 2019. They also highlighted the country’s strategic position in global mineral supply chains, particularly in cobalt, copper, and other critical resources.
In remarks following the issuance, the Finance Minister described the operation as a signal of international market confidence in the country’s reforms, emphasizing that the funds will serve as leverage for long-term development rather than short-term financing needs.
With this debut Eurobond, the DRC joins a select group of African issuers on global capital markets, positioning itself to broaden access to financing while strengthening its profile among international investors.

title: DRC Central Bank Cuts Key Rate and Tightens Foreign Currency Controls
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in
title_en: DRC Central Bank Cuts Key Rate and Tightens Foreign Currency Controls
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in Kinshasa.
Chaired by Governor André Wameso, the committee said the decision aims to preserve macroeconomic stability amid ongoing global economic uncertainty, including energy market disruptions and rising international pressures on inflation and trade.
The BCC also reduced the marginal lending facility rate from 19% to 17.5%, while maintaining reserve requirement ratios unchanged for deposits in both local and foreign currency.
According to the central bank, the Congolese economy continues to show resilience, with growth projected at 6.2% in 2026, up from 5.8% the previous year, driven by strong performance in both mining and non-mining sectors. Inflation, meanwhile, has declined significantly, standing at 2.2% at the end of March 2026 compared to 10.1% a year earlier.
A key structural decision announced by the bank concerns foreign currency management. The BCC will establish exclusive authority over the physical importation of foreign currency banknotes within 12 months. Starting April 9, 2027, commercial banks will no longer be allowed to import physical foreign currency, and cash transactions in foreign currency are expected to be fully replaced by electronic payments.
Authorities say the measure is intended to strengthen financial system security, improve oversight, and combat money laundering and illicit financial flows.
The central bank also plans to introduce six-month maturity instruments for BCC bonds to improve liquidity management.
Officials noted that the Congolese franc has shown mixed performance, with slight appreciation on the parallel market but depreciation on the official market since the beginning of the year, reflecting cyclical demand for foreign exchange and seasonal pressures.
The monetary authorities stressed that the policy adjustments are part of broader efforts to maintain stability in a challenging global environment marked by volatile energy prices, geopolitical tensions, and tightening international financial conditions.

title: DRC Adopts Strategic Mineral Reserve Framework to Strengthen State Control Over Key Resources
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources. Th
title_en: DRC Adopts Strategic Mineral Reserve Framework to Strengthen State Control Over Key Resources
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources. Th
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources.
The measure was adopted during the 86th meeting of the Council of Ministers held on April 10 in Kinshasa, under the chairmanship of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. The text was presented by the Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, and concerns mineral substances deemed essential both to the Congolese economy and to international markets.
According to the government, the creation of this strategic reserve is intended to help stabilize prices of key mineral resources, support the structured development of the sector, and reinforce the country’s economic sovereignty over its natural wealth.
In the same session, the government also approved amendments to the decree governing the Regulatory and Control Authority for Markets of Strategic Mineral Substances, known as ARECOMS. The revised framework strengthens the institution’s mandate, which includes the regulation, supervision, and stabilization of strategic mineral markets across the country.
ARECOMS, a public administrative and technical body with legal, administrative, and financial autonomy, operates under the supervision of the Ministry of Mines. It is responsible for overseeing production and export activities in the strategic minerals sector, improving the business climate, and ensuring compliance with national regulations, including provisions related to anti-money laundering and the financing of terrorism.
Authorities also confirmed that ARECOMS will be responsible for managing the newly created strategic reserve and will have the capacity to establish operational offices and branches throughout the national territory to ensure effective implementation of its mandate.
Officials say the reform reflects a broader effort by the government to strengthen governance in the mining sector, enhance market stability, and improve the country’s economic and industrial positioning in global strategic mineral supply chains.

Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a recovery and audit strategy to address an estimated $300 million in outstanding debts owed to the Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), in a move aimed at unlocking blocked resources for industrial development.
The issue was presented at the 86th meeting of the Council of Ministers held on April 10 in Kinshasa, under the chairmanship of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. The briefing was delivered by the Minister of State, acting Minister of Industry, during discussions focused on improving the efficiency and financial sustainability of state development institutions.
According to the government, the unpaid debts-owed by various insolvent or non-compliant borrowers-represent a significant financial constraint on the Industrial Promotion Fund, which is intended to finance structuring projects for national economic development.
Officials stressed that recovering these funds is considered essential to support ongoing efforts to stimulate industrial growth and strengthen domestic production capacity.
The Minister of Industry also proposed the creation of a special government commission to oversee the recovery process. The body would be responsible for classifying debtors based on good or bad faith, negotiating settlement agreements, initiating legal recovery actions where necessary, and recommending measures to safeguard assets belonging to insolvent borrowers.
The proposal also includes the identification of internal operational weaknesses within the FPI, including governance gaps, limited technical capacity, and informal practices in project financing, which may have contributed to the accumulation of unpaid debts.
However, authorities cautioned that delays in recovery could further weaken both the institution and the broader industrial sector, which continues to require significant financial support.
The Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), established under Ordinance-Law No. 89/031 of 1989 and later restructured into a public administrative and financial institution, is mandated to finance industrial development, support local production, and contribute to infrastructure linked to productive investment. It also manages resources derived from the industrial promotion tax and supports projects aimed at reducing import dependence.
The government says the recovery initiative is part of broader reforms to improve public financial management and ensure that development funds are effectively mobilized for industrial transformation and economic diversification.

title: IRDH Calls for Creation of Mining Royalties Observatory Amid Rising Scrutiny of Extractive Sector
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties
title_en: IRDH Calls for Creation of Mining Royalties Observatory Amid Rising Scrutiny of Extractive Sector
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties Observatory.
The Institute for Human Rights Research (IRDH) says the initiative is necessary to address persistent inequalities in the extractive sector and ensure that revenues from mining activities translate into tangible benefits for local communities.
The proposal comes as the country strengthens copper export partnerships with the United States, targeting annual shipments of around 500,000 tons. The operations involve state-owned interests through Gécamines, trading and logistics arrangements with Mercuria Energy Group, and financial backing from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation.
According to IRDH, the expansion of mining cooperation is reshaping governance expectations in the sector, particularly through emerging initiatives that emphasize traceability and supply chain transparency, including what stakeholders refer to as the “Vault” framework.
The organization argues that while new investors such as KoBold Metals and Virtus Minerals Inc. are generating optimism, human rights compliance must become a binding condition rather than a voluntary commitment.
IRDH notes that the Congolese mining landscape remains dominated by major international groups, including Glencore and other global operators active in copper and cobalt production. It warns that the concentration of mining rights among a limited number of actors makes independent oversight increasingly necessary.
The sector continues to attract substantial financing from international institutions such as the World Bank Group, the African Development Bank, and the Africa Finance Corporation. However, IRDH says these investments have not yet translated into proportionate improvements in living conditions in mining-affected communities.
The proposed Mining Royalties Observatory would aim to shift civil society engagement from advocacy to legal enforcement. It would be tasked with consolidating documentation on mining revenues and contractual obligations into legally actionable evidence for Congolese courts, particularly in cases involving fraud, embezzlement, or environmental non-compliance.
Beyond the national level, the initiative also envisions cooperation with international regulatory bodies, including securities market authorities in major jurisdictions, to increase corporate accountability.
IRDH argues that linking compliance with environmental and social standards to access to international finance could significantly alter incentives for multinational companies operating in the country.
As global competition intensifies over critical minerals, the proposal reflects broader debates over resource governance, revenue transparency, and the balance of power between states, corporations, and affected communities.
Social and Health

title: Japan Funds Major Electricity Upgrade Project in Kinshasa’s Mont-Amba District
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access. The funding, equiv
title_en: Japan Funds Major Electricity Upgrade Project in Kinshasa’s Mont-Amba District
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access. The funding, equiv
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access.
The funding, equivalent to 3.898 billion Japanese yen, has been provided to the National Electricity Company SNEL SA under a cooperation framework supported by the Japan International Cooperation Agency Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
The project targets the stabilization of electricity distribution across several communes in Mont-Amba, including Limete, Lemba, Matete, Ngaba, and Kisenso. It involves the installation of new 220 kV high-voltage transformers and the construction of control rooms at the Funa and Liminga substations.
Authorities say the infrastructure upgrade is expected to improve electricity reliability, support local economic activity, and enhance living conditions in one of Kinshasa’s most densely populated districts.
The works, initially planned for 2025 following the signing of the grant agreement between Japan and the DRC, officially began two weeks ago and are scheduled to run for 24 months.
Implementation is being carried out by international engineering firms selected through a competitive procurement process, including Trust Engineering Partners and Yachiyo Engineering.
According to project stakeholders, the grant does not involve direct cash transfers to the national utility. Instead, funds are managed jointly within the cooperation framework between both governments, with contractors selected through tender procedures after technical feasibility studies.
Officials involved in the project emphasize that the initiative reflects a model of infrastructure cooperation focused on transparency, technical oversight, and results-based implementation, in line with public procurement standards.
The project is part of broader efforts to strengthen urban energy infrastructure in Kinshasa, where demand for electricity continues to outpace supply due to rapid population growth and expanding economic activity.

title: Reception of Deportees from the United States Sparks Mixed Reactions in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 18, 2026 - The arrival of a first group of migrants deported from the United States under a bilateral arrangement with the Democratic Republic of Congo has triggered debate and mixed reactions among residents of the capital. The group, consisting of around 15 peop
title_en: Reception of Deportees from the United States Sparks Mixed Reactions in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 18, 2026 - The arrival of a first group of migrants deported from the United States under a bilateral arrangement with the Democratic Republic of Congo has triggered debate and mixed reactions among residents of the capital. The group, consisting of around 15 peop
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 18, 2026 - The arrival of a first group of migrants deported from the United States under a bilateral arrangement with the Democratic Republic of Congo has triggered debate and mixed reactions among residents of the capital.
The group, consisting of around 15 people from several Latin American countries, arrived in Kinshasa on April 17 and was transferred to a reception facility in Bibwa for administrative and humanitarian processing under Congolese authorities.
While the government maintains that the arrangement is temporary and strictly regulated, public opinion in Kinshasa remains divided over the decision.
Some residents view the initiative as part of broader diplomatic cooperation. Entrepreneur Gradi Abolambay said the move could be interpreted as a strategic gesture aimed at strengthening relations between Kinshasa and Washington, although he questioned whether it aligns with the country’s immediate social priorities.
Others expressed concern about the financial and social implications. Lawyer Yann Kitungwa warned that such agreements could raise issues of sovereignty, resource allocation, and international perception, particularly if not accompanied by clear legal safeguards and adequate funding.
More critical voices also referenced historical precedents in the region, drawing parallels with past refugee flows into eastern DRC and warning about potential unintended security and social consequences if such arrangements are not carefully managed.
A third perspective, voiced by residents, focused on security concerns linked to the origins and backgrounds of some deportees, with calls for greater caution and stricter screening mechanisms.
Congolese authorities, however, have reiterated that the arrangement does not involve permanent resettlement. Officials insist it is a temporary mechanism governed by national law, international humanitarian standards, and security oversight procedures, with the DRC retaining full authority over the status and duration of stay of those admitted.
The issue continues to generate discussion in public spaces, reflecting broader questions about diplomacy, national priorities, and migration management in the country’s evolving foreign policy landscape.

title: Lake Tanganyika Boat Accident Leaves 22 Dead Near Kalemie
excerpt: Kalemie, April 15, 2026 - At least 22 people have died following a boating accident on Lake Tanganyika in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, authorities announced. The incident occurred on Monday, April 13, a few kilometers from Kalemie, the capital of Tanganyika province
title_en: Lake Tanganyika Boat Accident Leaves 22 Dead Near Kalemie
excerpt_en: Kalemie, April 15, 2026 - At least 22 people have died following a boating accident on Lake Tanganyika in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, authorities announced. The incident occurred on Monday, April 13, a few kilometers from Kalemie, the capital of Tanganyika province
body_en:
Kalemie, April 15, 2026 - At least 22 people have died following a boating accident on Lake Tanganyika in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, authorities announced.
The incident occurred on Monday, April 13, a few kilometers from Kalemie, the capital of Tanganyika province, involving a wooden dugout canoe carrying passengers across the lake.
According to the Ministry of Transport, the vessel capsized after being caught in strong winds while also being overloaded, a combination officials say contributed to the tragedy.
The boat had reportedly departed in the early hours of the morning from an unauthorized docking point in Kasama, a village located roughly 18 kilometers from Kalemie. Several passengers survived the accident, though the exact number has not been confirmed.
Authorities described the port of departure as “illegal,” raising renewed concerns over informal transport routes and safety standards on Lake Tanganyika, where maritime accidents have frequently been linked to overloading and poor regulation.
Rescue and recovery operations were carried out following the incident, while local officials continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the sinking.

title: Government Details Alleged Abuses by AFC/M23 During Uvira Occupation
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The Congolese government has released a report outlining alleged large-scale human rights violations committed by AFC/M23 rebels during their occupation of Uvira and surrounding areas in South Kivu province. Presented on April 7 by Minister of Human Righ
title_en: Government Details Alleged Abuses by AFC/M23 During Uvira Occupation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The Congolese government has released a report outlining alleged large-scale human rights violations committed by AFC/M23 rebels during their occupation of Uvira and surrounding areas in South Kivu province. Presented on April 7 by Minister of Human Righ
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 8, 2026 - The Congolese government has released a report outlining alleged large-scale human rights violations committed by AFC/M23 rebels during their occupation of Uvira and surrounding areas in South Kivu province.
Presented on April 7 by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba, the document details the impact of the occupation, describing widespread abuses against civilians. According to the report, thousands of people were killed during the period, both as a direct result of armed violence and due to limited access to healthcare.
The report also cites extensive cases of sexual violence, with more than 14,000 women reportedly affected. In addition, over 300,000 people are said to have been displaced, while the education of more than 12,000 children was disrupted.
Authorities describe a climate marked by insecurity and fear, characterized by reported bombings, summary executions, kidnappings, looting, and other forms of violence. The government also alleges large-scale looting of property, including the reported movement of goods across the border.
The report further indicates the discovery of several mass graves in areas previously occupied by AFC/M23 forces. Sites identified include Mayi Moto, Kilomani, Kala, and Rutembo, where dozens of bodies were reportedly recovered.
Officials have pledged that those responsible for the alleged abuses will be held accountable, emphasizing the need for justice for victims.
AFC/M23 forces had taken control of Uvira in December 2025 following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo groups. The group later announced its withdrawal in January 2026, describing the move as a confidence-building measure in support of ongoing peace efforts.

title: Police Arrest 63 People in Security Sweep in Beni Amid Ongoing Anti-Crime Operations
excerpt: Beni, April 19, 2026 - Security forces in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo have arrested 63 individuals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation carried out across several neighborhoods of Beni city. The joint operation, conducted by the Congolese National Police,
title_en: Police Arrest 63 People in Security Sweep in Beni Amid Ongoing Anti-Crime Operations
excerpt_en: Beni, April 19, 2026 - Security forces in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo have arrested 63 individuals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation carried out across several neighborhoods of Beni city. The joint operation, conducted by the Congolese National Police,
body_en:
Beni, April 19, 2026 - Security forces in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo have arrested 63 individuals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation carried out across several neighborhoods of Beni city.
The joint operation, conducted by the Congolese National Police, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and intelligence services, targeted suspected criminal networks operating in urban areas of Bungulu and Beu communes.
According to security officials, the operation led to the arrest of 63 people, including four women. Authorities also reported the seizure of military-related items and a significant quantity of cannabis during the searches.
The intervention focused primarily on the Trois Cents Maisons and Biautu neighborhoods, areas that have previously been identified by security services as vulnerable to criminal activity.
Police stated that all suspects will undergo screening before being transferred to judicial authorities for further legal proceedings, depending on the results of ongoing investigations.
Security officials reiterated that public cooperation is essential in combating insecurity, calling on residents to report suspicious behavior to relevant authorities.
The operation forms part of a broader series of security measures aimed at restoring order and strengthening civilian protection in Beni and surrounding areas, which have long faced instability linked to armed groups and organized crime.
Earlier in the week, security services had already presented around ten suspected criminals to provincial police authorities in Beni. Those individuals were accused of involvement in burglaries and alleged collaboration with armed groups, including the ADF.
Authorities say such coordinated operations will continue as part of ongoing efforts to dismantle criminal networks and reinforce state presence in conflict-affected regions of North Kivu.

title: FARDC Seize Arms Cache, 14 Militants Surrender After ADF Attack
excerpt: Ituri, April 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have discovered a third arms cache linked to the CRP-Zaire coalition and secured the surrender of fourteen of its members in Ituri province, following a deadly attack by the Allied Democratic Forc
title_en: FARDC Seize Arms Cache, 14 Militants Surrender After ADF Attack
excerpt_en: Ituri, April 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have discovered a third arms cache linked to the CRP-Zaire coalition and secured the surrender of fourteen of its members in Ituri province, following a deadly attack by the Allied Democratic Forc
body_en:
Ituri, April 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have discovered a third arms cache linked to the CRP-Zaire coalition and secured the surrender of fourteen of its members in Ituri province, following a deadly attack by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambasa territory.
The developments were outlined during the April 3 meeting of the Council of Ministers, where Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo briefed the government on the evolving security situation in the eastern provinces.
According to the briefing, the ADF attack in Mambasa left more than 40 people dead and caused extensive material damage. The army has since intensified operations to contain the violence and prevent further displacement of civilians.
In Djugu territory, FARDC units uncovered an additional weapons cache attributed to the CRP-Zaire coalition. The surrender of fourteen fighters was described by authorities as a positive outcome of ongoing military pressure. Security forces are continuing operations to track down remaining elements accused of attacks against civilians and ambushes.
In North Kivu’s Walikale territory, the army is also implementing commitments related to the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), as part of broader efforts to stabilize the region.
Beyond Ituri, military operations are ongoing in other parts of the country. In Haut-Katanga province, the FARDC Chief of Staff has launched actions aimed at neutralizing insurgent groups. Authorities also reported continued operations against Mobondo militia elements in areas surrounding Kinshasa and in Maï-Ndombe province.
The latest developments highlight the persistent instability in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to ease tensions with neighboring Rwanda and address the conflict involving the AFC/M23 rebellion.
The ADF, originally from Uganda and now affiliated with the Islamic State, remains one of the deadliest armed groups in the region, continuing to carry out attacks against civilians across the DRC-Uganda border despite joint military operations.

excerpt: Goma, April 7, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in parts of North Kivu, where renewed movements by AFC/M23 rebels have been reported in Walikale and neighboring Masisi territories. Local sources indicate that since April 4, the group has reinforced its presence in seve
title_en: AFC/M23 Reinforces Positions in Walikale and Masisi
excerpt_en: Goma, April 7, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in parts of North Kivu, where renewed movements by AFC/M23 rebels have been reported in Walikale and neighboring Masisi territories. Local sources indicate that since April 4, the group has reinforced its presence in seve
body_en:
Goma, April 7, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in parts of North Kivu, where renewed movements by AFC/M23 rebels have been reported in Walikale and neighboring Masisi territories.
Local sources indicate that since April 4, the group has reinforced its presence in several strategic areas, including Bukumbirwa and Ihula in Walikale territory, as well as Malemo in Masisi. These localities are considered sensitive zones due to their proximity to active conflict fronts and vulnerable civilian populations.
The reported troop movements are said to be accompanied by logistical deployments, fueling concerns over possible preparations for new military operations in an area already affected by chronic insecurity.
The latest developments come shortly after a reported withdrawal of rebel elements from some of these positions, suggesting a rapid reversal that has heightened uncertainty among residents.
Civilian populations in the affected areas fear a renewed escalation of violence, as the region has frequently experienced clashes between armed groups, often resulting in casualties and large-scale displacement.

title: AFC/M23 Seizes Several Localities in Kalehe After Clashes, Thousands Displaced
excerpt: Bukavu, April 7, 2026 - Heavy fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and local Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory has led to the capture of multiple localities and triggered large-scale civilian displacement, amid a rapidly deteriorating security situation. Clashes erupted on April
title_en: AFC/M23 Seizes Several Localities in Kalehe After Clashes, Thousands Displaced
excerpt_en: Bukavu, April 7, 2026 - Heavy fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and local Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory has led to the capture of multiple localities and triggered large-scale civilian displacement, amid a rapidly deteriorating security situation. Clashes erupted on April
body_en:
Bukavu, April 7, 2026 - Heavy fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and local Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory has led to the capture of multiple localities and triggered large-scale civilian displacement, amid a rapidly deteriorating security situation.
Clashes erupted on April 6 in the Ziralo area of Buhavu chiefdom, with intense confrontations reported in villages including Kusisa and Nyalugusha, as well as along key axes such as Braza, Lulamba, and Bushege. Additional fighting was recorded along the Kaziba-Katale-Kafufula-Katanga corridor, notably in Bundje and Bushugulu.
On the ground, AFC/M23 elements faced off against Wazalendo fighters drawn from several local armed groups, including factions led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, Grevisse Nsimparingira, and Haguma Kanyengwenye.
As the day progressed, the balance of power shifted in favor of the rebels. By late afternoon, multiple areas-including Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege, and Lulamba-had fallen under AFC/M23 control, according to local sources.
The escalation has forced thousands of civilians to flee their homes. Residents from the affected localities, as well as nearby areas such as Kashebere, Tushunguti, Ruchuro, Kirambo, and Bunyangungu, have sought refuge in safer zones, particularly in Mianda in the Bulembwe area.
Humanitarian conditions are rapidly worsening, with many displaced families spending the night outdoors without shelter, food, or basic assistance. Women, children, and vulnerable individuals are among the most affected.
Reports also indicate that AFC/M23 fighters continue to advance toward Tushunguti, the main center of the Ziralo group, located roughly seven kilometers from the initial combat zones, raising fears of further escalation in the coming days.

title: MONUSCO Reconnaissance Mission in Mambasa Blocked by Protesters
excerpt: Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). The deployment, carried out by
title_en: MONUSCO Reconnaissance Mission in Mambasa Blocked by Protesters
excerpt_en: Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). The deployment, carried out by
body_en:
Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).
The deployment, carried out by the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO), aimed to assess the security situation and support efforts to protect civilians in the area.
According to MONUSCO officials, the mission was conducted in coordination with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) as part of its civilian protection mandate. The initiative follows a series of deadly ADF attacks that have left dozens of civilians dead in recent weeks.
Local sources confirmed the arrival of peacekeepers on the outskirts of Mambasa. However, the convoy was blocked by groups of young protesters who erected barricades and burned tires to prevent MONUSCO forces from entering the area.
Residents cited growing frustration and mistrust toward the UN mission, which some accuse of failing to respond effectively to recurring violence by armed groups. Local authorities also reported a tense climate marked by skepticism among sections of the population.
Facing the resistance, MONUSCO personnel were forced to withdraw, according to multiple accounts. The incident underscores ongoing tensions between the peacekeeping mission and local communities, particularly in areas heavily affected by armed group activity.
Mambasa territory has experienced a resurgence of ADF attacks in recent months, with civilians frequently targeted in rural and mining zones. These attacks, often involving killings, abductions, and the destruction of property, have led to significant population displacement.
Despite joint military operations conducted by the FARDC and Ugandan forces, the ADF continues to operate across parts of Ituri as well as neighboring territories such as Irumu and Beni, maintaining a persistent threat to civilian populations.

title_en: AFC/M23 Takes Control of Tushunguti, Biriko Under Threat
excerpt_en: South Kivu, April 8, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have taken control of the town of Tushunguti in Kalehe territory after intense clashes with local Wazalendo fighters, marking a further deterioration of the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The fighting, which
body_en:
South Kivu, April 8, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have taken control of the town of Tushunguti in Kalehe territory after intense clashes with local Wazalendo fighters, marking a further deterioration of the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The fighting, which occurred on April 7 in the Ziralo area of South Kivu, forced self-defense groups to retreat, allowing the rebels to seize the town, considered a strategic location near the border with North Kivu.
Local sources report that the fall of Tushunguti now places the town of Biriko, in Walikale territory, under direct threat. The area is regarded as particularly sensitive due to its proximity to recent conflict zones.
The escalation has triggered new waves of displacement, with hundreds of households fleeing toward safer areas. This movement adds to an already severe humanitarian crisis affecting the region.
No official casualty figures have been released at this stage. However, sources on the ground describe a rapidly worsening situation, with urgent needs for both security intervention and humanitarian assistance.
Residents, already affected by years of conflict, remain in a state of heightened fear as uncertainty persists over further advances and the broader trajectory of the violence.

title: Tanzania Commits to Strengthening Regional Security Cooperation
excerpt: Dodoma, April 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania have agreed to reinforce bilateral military cooperation and deepen regional security dialogue, following high-level talks between defense officials in the Tanzanian capital. The discussions were led by Deputy
title_en: Tanzania Commits to Strengthening Regional Security Cooperation
excerpt_en: Dodoma, April 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania have agreed to reinforce bilateral military cooperation and deepen regional security dialogue, following high-level talks between defense officials in the Tanzanian capital. The discussions were led by Deputy
body_en:
Dodoma, April 11, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania have agreed to reinforce bilateral military cooperation and deepen regional security dialogue, following high-level talks between defense officials in the Tanzanian capital.
The discussions were led by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, who was received by Tanzania’s Minister of Defense and National Service Rhimo Nyansaho. The meeting focused on defense cooperation, border security, and broader regional security coordination.
According to the Congolese Ministry of Defense, the visit aligns with directives from President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi and forms part of ongoing efforts to strengthen military partnerships, support armed forces reform, and promote stability in the region.
Both delegations emphasized the importance of maintaining regular and structured consultations between their respective defense institutions, particularly in light of persistent security challenges in the Great Lakes region.
Congolese officials stressed the need for continuous dialogue to prevent incidents, harmonize security approaches, and reinforce mutual trust between neighboring states. Tanzanian authorities, for their part, reaffirmed their commitment to supporting peace and stability efforts in the DRC.
The two sides also agreed to expand cooperation in areas such as military training, capacity building, coordination of peace initiatives, and operational support.
The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania maintain longstanding diplomatic and defense relations, with Tanzania contributing troops to regional and United Nations peacekeeping missions, including deployments under the Southern African Development Community (SADC) framework.
The engagement comes in a broader regional context marked by ongoing instability in eastern DRC, where foreign and regional forces have previously suffered casualties during operations against armed groups, including the AFC/M23 rebellion.

title: Army Reports Partial Surrenders Amid Ongoing Mobondo Threat in Kwamouth
excerpt: Kikwit, April 11, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have reported continued progress in operations against Mobondo militias, while warning that pockets of resistance remain active in Kwamouth territory, considered the epicenter of the insurgency
title_en: Army Reports Partial Surrenders Amid Ongoing Mobondo Threat in Kwamouth
excerpt_en: Kikwit, April 11, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have reported continued progress in operations against Mobondo militias, while warning that pockets of resistance remain active in Kwamouth territory, considered the epicenter of the insurgency
body_en:
Kikwit, April 11, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have reported continued progress in operations against Mobondo militias, while warning that pockets of resistance remain active in Kwamouth territory, considered the epicenter of the insurgency in Maï-Ndombe province.
During a briefing on April 9 in Kikwit, the spokesperson for the 11th Military Region indicated that ongoing operations have shifted focus from direct combat to awareness campaigns aimed at encouraging militia members to surrender.
According to the army, several hundred combatants have already laid down their arms in recent weeks. Many of them are currently in military facilities, while others have been redirected toward civic and vocational reintegration programs under state supervision. Authorities also confirmed the recovery of a significant number of surrendered weapons.
Despite these developments, military officials stressed that the situation remains fragile. They noted that an armed movement active for more than three years cannot be dismantled quickly and that efforts to secure additional surrenders are ongoing.
The army reported that most of the individuals who have surrendered originate from Kwango province, while fewer have come from Kwamouth itself, raising concerns about continued resistance in the movement’s main stronghold. Some militia leaders, according to military sources, continue to reject calls to demobilize.
Authorities also indicated that certain fighters willing to surrender have expressed readiness to do so through government channels, including the Ministry Delegate for Veterans Affairs.
During recent pacification efforts, more than 600 Mobondo militiamen reportedly surrendered across several operations, including in Kwango and parts of the Maluku commune. Some were transferred to national service centers, including Kaniama Kasese, for vocational training and reintegration.
While officials estimate that the majority of fighters have laid down their arms, they acknowledge that an estimated residual threat remains in Kwamouth, where localized insecurity continues to pose a challenge for stabilization efforts.

title: Calm Returns to Kalembe and Kalonge After Night Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt: Goma, April 13, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Kalembe and Kalonge in North Kivu following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the border area between Masisi and Walikale territories. According to local sources, fighting erupted on Sunday eve
title_en: Calm Returns to Kalembe and Kalonge After Night Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt_en: Goma, April 13, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Kalembe and Kalonge in North Kivu following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the border area between Masisi and Walikale territories. According to local sources, fighting erupted on Sunday eve
body_en:
Goma, April 13, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Kalembe and Kalonge in North Kivu following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the border area between Masisi and Walikale territories.
According to local sources, fighting erupted on Sunday evening around 8:00 p.m. when Wazalendo forces launched coordinated attacks on positions held by AFC/M23 elements. The exchange of fire triggered panic among civilians, many of whom sought refuge inside their homes.
Preliminary reports indicate at least two fatalities, including one civilian and one combatant from the AFC/M23. Instances of looting were also reported during the clashes, further worsening the situation for already vulnerable communities.
By Monday morning, hostilities had ceased, although tensions remained high. Residents expressed fear of a possible resumption of fighting despite the temporary lull. Sources on the ground indicated that Wazalendo fighters had withdrawn from the area, leaving AFC/M23 in control of the two localities.
The incidents are part of a broader pattern of recurring violence in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where Masisi and Walikale territories remain frequent flashpoints between armed groups. The instability continues to drive population displacement and deepen humanitarian needs across the region.
The situation in Kalembe and Kalonge highlights the fragility of security conditions in North Kivu, where localized ceasefires often fail to hold amid ongoing rivalries between armed actors.

title: Three Civilians Killed in Shooting in Bankoko Neighborhood
excerpt: Bunia, April 14, 2026 - Three civilians were killed and another seriously injured in a shooting incident that occurred on Monday evening in the Bankoko neighborhood of Bunia, in Ituri province, raising renewed concern over security incidents involving armed personnel in urban are
title_en: Three Civilians Killed in Shooting in Bankoko Neighborhood
excerpt_en: Bunia, April 14, 2026 - Three civilians were killed and another seriously injured in a shooting incident that occurred on Monday evening in the Bankoko neighborhood of Bunia, in Ituri province, raising renewed concern over security incidents involving armed personnel in urban are
body_en:
Bunia, April 14, 2026 - Three civilians were killed and another seriously injured in a shooting incident that occurred on Monday evening in the Bankoko neighborhood of Bunia, in Ituri province, raising renewed concern over security incidents involving armed personnel in urban areas.
According to local sources, the alleged perpetrator-suspected of being a member of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC)-opened fire during a domestic dispute in which he accused his partner of infidelity. The gunfire also struck nearby civilians, turning a private altercation into a deadly incident.
Witnesses reported that the victims included a woman, her partner, and a child estimated to be around ten years old. Another civilian sustained serious injuries and was evacuated to a medical facility for urgent treatment.
The incident has reignited public concern over the presence of armed individuals carrying weapons outside official duties in a city already marked by heightened security sensitivities. Residents expressed alarm over the recurrence of such cases, which they say undermine public confidence and safety.
As of now, no official statement has been issued by either military or local authorities regarding the circumstances of the shooting or the identity of the suspected shooter.

title_en: 17 Schools Relocated to Nia-Nia After ADF Attacks Displace Students
excerpt_en: Mambasa, April 15, 2026 - Educational activities in parts of Mambasa territory, Ituri province, have been severely disrupted following renewed attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), forcing the relocation of 17 schools from the Badengaido area to Nia-Nia. Accor
body_en:
Mambasa, April 15, 2026 - Educational activities in parts of Mambasa territory, Ituri province, have been severely disrupted following renewed attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), forcing the relocation of 17 schools from the Badengaido area to Nia-Nia.
According to local education authorities, students and teachers from the affected schools are now living as internally displaced persons after fleeing recent violence in the region. The villages affected by the March attacks remain largely deserted, with displaced populations concentrated in Nia-Nia and Bafwasende, where access to basic services remains limited. Humanitarian conditions are reported to be deteriorating.
Local sources estimate that nearly 100 civilians have been killed in recent weeks in successive attacks attributed to the ADF, an armed group operating in the Mambasa territory and surrounding areas.

title: HRW Reports Forced Recruitment and Civilian Threats by Twirwaneho in High Plateaus
excerpt: Bukavu, April 15, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has raised alarm over alleged human rights abuses committed by the armed group Twirwaneho in the High Plateaus of South Kivu, citing threats, forced recruitment, and restrictions on civilian movement in territories including Minembwe, F
title_en: HRW Reports Forced Recruitment and Civilian Threats by Twirwaneho in High Plateaus
excerpt_en: Bukavu, April 15, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has raised alarm over alleged human rights abuses committed by the armed group Twirwaneho in the High Plateaus of South Kivu, citing threats, forced recruitment, and restrictions on civilian movement in territories including Minembwe, F
body_en:
Bukavu, April 15, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has raised alarm over alleged human rights abuses committed by the armed group Twirwaneho in the High Plateaus of South Kivu, citing threats, forced recruitment, and restrictions on civilian movement in territories including Minembwe, Fizi, and Mwenga.
In a new report, the organization states that civilians have been subjected to coercion, including demands that each family provide a fighter or pay financial compensation. Those who refuse are reportedly exposed to reprisals, including intimidation and punishment.
The report further alleges that Twirwaneho, at times in coordination with AFC/M23 elements, has forcibly recruited civilians and restricted population movements in areas under its influence, preventing residents from leaving Minembwe despite ongoing insecurity.
According to the findings, the town of Minembwe-reported to have been taken by AFC/M23 forces in previous fighting-remains encircled by government forces and allied groups. The continued clashes in the surrounding area have disrupted humanitarian access, complicating the delivery of aid and worsening food insecurity.
Human Rights Watch also highlights deteriorating living conditions, including severe shortages of medicines and essential goods. In some areas, the cost of basic commodities such as sugar and salt has reportedly increased several times above normal levels due to supply constraints.
The report notes that the humanitarian impact extends beyond rebel-held areas, affecting zones under government control as well, where shortages of medical supplies are also being reported.
Twirwaneho, a self-defense group originally formed between 2019 and 2020, claims to protect Banyamulenge communities in the region. However, it has since become a significant armed actor in South Kivu, with allegations of collaboration and clashes with other armed groups, including AFC/M23. The group was previously led militarily by Michel Rukunda, known as Makanika, who was killed in a drone strike in February 2025.
In a separate development, authorities recently released several Twirwaneho fighters who had surrendered during earlier clashes in Uvira, as part of ongoing judicial and reconciliation measures linked to armed group defections.

title: Three Dead in Several Days of Youth Clashes in Mangobo and Makiso
excerpt: Kisangani, April 15, 2026 - At least three people have been killed in Kisangani following several days of violent clashes between groups of youths in the Mangobo commune and nearby areas, triggering displacement and property destruction. In the Imbolo neighborhood of Mangobo, fig
title_en: Three Dead in Several Days of Youth Clashes in Mangobo and Makiso
excerpt_en: Kisangani, April 15, 2026 - At least three people have been killed in Kisangani following several days of violent clashes between groups of youths in the Mangobo commune and nearby areas, triggering displacement and property destruction. In the Imbolo neighborhood of Mangobo, fig
body_en:
Kisangani, April 15, 2026 - At least three people have been killed in Kisangani following several days of violent clashes between groups of youths in the Mangobo commune and nearby areas, triggering displacement and property destruction.
In the Imbolo neighborhood of Mangobo, fighting erupted on April 12 after armed individuals reportedly raided three houses near the Bobokoli School Complex. Tensions escalated the following day when a young man from the Segama neighborhood was assaulted and later died, with reports indicating his body was burned.
The incident sparked retaliatory attacks, as groups of youths from Segama entered Imbolo and vandalized homes. In response, local youths from Imbolo mobilized and launched counterattacks, leading to continuous clashes that persisted until Wednesday morning.
According to local accounts, two additional youths from Segama were killed during the confrontations on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the total death toll in Mangobo to at least three.
The violence has forced several residents in Imbolo to flee their homes in search of safety. Police presence has been reported in the area, although sporadic tensions continue, with some groups still resisting.
A similar wave of unrest has also been reported in the Makiso commune, particularly between 0th and 5th Avenues in Camp Ketele. There, youth clashes have been ongoing since Monday for reasons that remain unclear. Preliminary reports indicate several serious injuries and cases of looted businesses.
Authorities have yet to issue an official statement on the coordinated nature of the incidents or the measures being taken to restore calm in the city.

excerpt: Goma, April 17, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo fighters, have repelled an offensive by AFC/M23 rebels in the locality of Ndurumo, in Masisi territory, amid ongoing tensions along a key strategic axis. The clashes occurred
title_en: FARDC Repel AFC/M23 Offensive in Ndurumo
excerpt_en: Goma, April 17, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo fighters, have repelled an offensive by AFC/M23 rebels in the locality of Ndurumo, in Masisi territory, amid ongoing tensions along a key strategic axis. The clashes occurred
body_en:
Goma, April 17, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo fighters, have repelled an offensive by AFC/M23 rebels in the locality of Ndurumo, in Masisi territory, amid ongoing tensions along a key strategic axis.
The clashes occurred in an area linking Pinga to Lukweti toward Nyabiondo, a corridor considered vital for both civilian movement and military operations. According to local sources, AFC/M23 elements had sought to establish a position in Ndurumo, near Lukweti, with the apparent aim of cutting off this route and isolating surrounding communities.
In response, FARDC and allied forces launched coordinated operations beginning on April 15, leading to intense fighting in the area. The offensive was ultimately contained and repelled, preventing the establishment of a blockade along the axis.
Despite this development, concerns remain over a possible regrouping of rebel elements in nearby forested areas, which are difficult to access and monitor. Residents in the region continue to express fear of renewed clashes.
Observers on the ground have called for reinforced security measures to secure the corridor and ensure the continued movement of civilians and goods in this part of North Kivu, where instability has persisted for several months.
