title: U.S. Sanctions Target Rwandan Army-Linked Economic Network, Raising Broader Regional Pressure
excerpt: March 30, 2026 - A recent analysis by the Egmont Institute highlights the wide-ranging impact of U.S. sanctions imposed on Rwanda’s defense establishment, warning that the measures could extend far beyond the military sector and reshape economic and financial networks linked to t
title_en: U.S. Sanctions Target Rwandan Army-Linked Economic Network, Raising Broader Regional Pressure
excerpt_en: March 30, 2026 - A recent analysis by the Egmont Institute highlights the wide-ranging impact of U.S. sanctions imposed on Rwanda’s defense establishment, warning that the measures could extend far beyond the military sector and reshape economic and financial networks linked to t
body_en:
March 30, 2026 - A recent analysis by the Egmont Institute highlights the wide-ranging impact of U.S. sanctions imposed on Rwanda’s defense establishment, warning that the measures could extend far beyond the military sector and reshape economic and financial networks linked to the country’s armed forces.
The sanctions, announced on March 2 by the U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), target four senior officers of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), as well as the institution itself. The measures restrict access to U.S. dollar transactions and effectively exclude the designated entities from the global financial system, including the SWIFT network.
According to the analysis, the restrictions could significantly complicate procurement of military, logistical, and technical equipment, while also affecting broader economic operations tied to defense-linked structures.
The report notes that the RDF operates through a wide network of commercial entities active in sectors such as construction, agriculture, finance, industry, and healthcare. These include companies such as Horizon Construction, Agro Processing Trust Corporation (APTC), Rwanda Fertilizer Company, and Rwanda Engineering and Manufacturing Corporation (REMCO), which is involved in both civilian and defense-related production.
Financial institutions linked to the security sector, including the Zigama Credit and Savings Society, are also identified as potentially affected due to their role in managing salaries and financial services for military personnel and security forces.
The analysis further highlights the influence of holding companies and state-linked investment structures such as Crystal Ventures and Ngali Holdings, which operate across mining and infrastructure sectors and are considered part of a broader economic ecosystem associated with the ruling political-military establishment.
Experts cited in the report argue that the sanctions may prompt international banks and commercial partners to adopt a more cautious stance toward transactions involving Rwanda’s defense-linked entities, potentially amplifying the economic impact beyond the initial targets.
Strategically, the measures are seen as part of a broader shift in United States policy in the Great Lakes region, including closer engagement with the Democratic Republic of Congo under a strategic minerals partnership signed in December 2025.
While Washington continues cooperation with Kigali in selected areas such as health supply chains and industrial inputs, the sanctions are widely interpreted as a tool of pressure linked to regional security tensions, particularly allegations surrounding Rwanda’s role in eastern Congo.
The report concludes that the evolving financial restrictions could reshape regional economic alignments while adding further uncertainty to already strained diplomatic relations in the Great Lakes region.

title: AFC/M23 Reoccupy Kateku and Kanune After Brief Withdrawal
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - AFC/M23 fighters have returned to the villages of Kateku and Kanune on Saturday, March 28, just two days after withdrawing from the area in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The villages, located in the Ikobo group of Walikale Territory i
title_en: AFC/M23 Reoccupy Kateku and Kanune After Brief Withdrawal
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - AFC/M23 fighters have returned to the villages of Kateku and Kanune on Saturday, March 28, just two days after withdrawing from the area in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The villages, located in the Ikobo group of Walikale Territory i
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - AFC/M23 fighters have returned to the villages of Kateku and Kanune on Saturday, March 28, just two days after withdrawing from the area in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The villages, located in the Ikobo group of Walikale Territory in North Kivu Province, had experienced a temporary absence of armed presence following recent movements linked to clashes with Wazalendo forces.
The fighters reportedly re-entered Kanune with logistical supplies after passing through Miriki in neighboring Lubero Territory. At the same time, those who had previously left Kateku are said to have returned from Buleusa, where they had repositioned after pressure from Wazalendo elements.
Wazalendo forces had briefly occupied Kateku but withdrew without reported fighting. In Kanune, no armed group had maintained control following the rebels’ pullback on March 26, leaving the area temporarily unoccupied.
The renewed deployment has increased uncertainty among residents, many of whom were preparing to return home after weeks of displacement. Fear of renewed clashes between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo forces remains high across the region.
The reasons for this rapid repositioning remain unclear, fueling concern among local observers who warn of a possible escalation of violence in an already unstable part of eastern Congo.

title: Two Wazalendo Killed, Eight Arrested in Clashes with Army in Shabunda
excerpt: Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the a
title_en: Two Wazalendo Killed, Eight Arrested in Clashes with Army in Shabunda
excerpt_en: Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the a
body_en:
Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the armed forces.
The confrontation broke out in the morning when government troops intervened against an armed group linked to the Sisawa faction, accused of extorting and intimidating civilians in the area. An exchange of fire followed during the operation.
The group targeted was associated with the network led by Amisi Sisawa, also known as “Muswahili,” who had been accused of maintaining an unauthorized armed structure operating under the Wazalendo label.
Local civil society figures reported that the intervention resulted in the deaths of two armed men on the spot, while their commander and eight other members were captured.
Military authorities stated that the operation was conducted against a criminal group presenting itself as part of the Wazalendo movement and accused of multiple abuses against civilians, including looting, extortion, and forced labor in mining zones.
It was further reported that the same group had previously attacked a provincial delegation led by the South Kivu justice authorities during an earlier incident in Shabunda, aimed at obstructing judicial proceedings.
The arrested individuals are expected to face legal proceedings as investigations continue into the activities of the armed group operating in the region.

title: AFC/M23 Seizes Control of Humura and Mukohwa After Heavy Fighting
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Repu
title_en: AFC/M23 Seizes Control of Humura and Mukohwa After Heavy Fighting
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Repu
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo groups.
Fighting reportedly lasted throughout the day, with heavy exchanges forcing pro-government forces to withdraw and leave the two localities in rebel hands.
The advance is seen as part of a broader shift in control across parts of Masisi, increasing concerns over the security of surrounding areas and key positions.
Local sources indicate that the fall of nearby positions has also put the strategic area of Rutoboko under pressure, particularly due to its role as a logistical hub for government forces. The site is known for its use in military supply operations, including helicopter landings supporting frontline deployments.
A fragile calm was reported on Monday in Humura and Mukohwa, although the situation remains tense, with fears of renewed fighting.
The latest developments come amid ongoing instability in Masisi Territory, where control frequently shifts between FARDC, Wazalendo allies, and AFC/M23 forces. Civilians continue to bear the brunt of repeated clashes, facing displacement and worsening humanitarian conditions.

title_en: A Nurse and Red Cross Volunteer Arrested and Injured in Kalembe by Armed Fighters
excerpt_en: Kalembe, Masisi, North Kivu March 31, 2026 - A nurse and a Red Cross volunteer were arrested and injured on Monday, March 30, in Kalembe, in the Mweso health zone of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, after being targeted by armed AFC/M23 fighters. The incident occurred at
body_en:
Kalembe, Masisi, North Kivu March 31, 2026 - A nurse and a Red Cross volunteer were arrested and injured on Monday, March 30, in Kalembe, in the Mweso health zone of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, after being targeted by armed AFC/M23 fighters.
The incident occurred at the Kalembe health center, where the head nurse, identified as Kapita Lucien, was reportedly beaten and shot in the hand during the attack. The local Red Cross coordinator, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, was also physically assaulted before both men were taken away on motorcycles to an unknown destination.
The two humanitarian workers are alleged to have been accused-without evidence-of having links to AFC/M23.
Their abduction has raised alarm among local residents, who fear for their safety and are calling for urgent intervention by humanitarian organizations, including the International Committee of the Red Cross and Médecins Sans Frontières, to secure their release.
The incident has heightened concerns over the protection of medical and humanitarian personnel operating in conflict-affected areas of Masisi Territory, where insecurity remains widespread and access to health services is already severely constrained.
No official response has yet been issued by AFC/M23 regarding the incident.

title: Heavy Clashes Erupt Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Shoa
excerpt: Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
title_en: Heavy Clashes Erupt Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Shoa
excerpt_en: Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
body_en:
Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
Local sources reported sustained exchanges of heavy and light weapons fire from the early hours of the morning, indicating intense and ongoing clashes that left the situation highly unstable and unclear throughout the day.
The offensive is believed to have been launched by AFC/M23 fighters attempting to retake a strategic position in Shoa, as part of broader efforts to expand their influence across Masisi Territory, a region that has remained highly volatile for months.
No confirmed information is yet available regarding casualties or material damage. However, the renewed fighting has heightened fears among civilians of further displacement in an area already severely affected by repeated cycles of armed conflict.

body_en:
Bafwakoa, Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province April 2, 2026 - At least 43 civilians were killed and extensive material destruction recorded on Thursday, April 2, following a deadly attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Bafwakoa, a village located about 148 kilometers from Mambasa along the Kisangani road in Ituri Province in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The attack occurred in the evening when armed assailants stormed the village, opening fire on civilians and setting fire to homes and vehicles. Local reports indicate that 44 houses were burned, along with several motorcycles and a truck, leaving significant material losses in the community.

excerpt_en: Kisimba, Walikale, North Kivu April 3, 2026 - Several villages in the Kisimba area, including Ndumbi, Buma, Iteya, Buhaya, Mpety, and Minjenje, have come under the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo fighters following the
body_en:
Kisimba, Walikale, North Kivu April 3, 2026 - Several villages in the Kisimba area, including Ndumbi, Buma, Iteya, Buhaya, Mpety, and Minjenje, have come under the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo fighters following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels without reported clashes.
The shift in control marks a significant change in the security landscape of this part of Walikale Territory in North Kivu Province, where frontlines have remained fluid amid ongoing fighting between armed groups.
The rebel withdrawal reportedly occurred without resistance, allowing government forces and their local allies to quickly reoccupy the affected villages and reestablish positions on the ground.
Following the pullback, AFC/M23 fighters are believed to have repositioned toward Malemo, a locality near Kalembe in neighboring Masisi Territory, suggesting a tactical redeployment rather than a full retreat from the broader area.
The development has created mixed reactions among local communities. While some residents cautiously welcome the return of government control and hope for improved stability, others remain fearful that the situation could quickly reverse, given the region’s history of repeated changes in territorial control.
Military forces are currently consolidating their positions in the recaptured villages in an effort to secure the area and prevent any possible counteroffensive, as tensions remain high despite the absence of active clashes at present.

title: DRC, UNHCR, and Burundi Prepare Tripartite Meeting on Refugee Returns as Authorities Report Progress in Uvira
excerpt: Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establis
title_en: DRC, UNHCR, and Burundi Prepare Tripartite Meeting on Refugee Returns as Authorities Report Progress in Uvira
excerpt_en: Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establis
body_en:
Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establish a framework for repatriation in the coming months.
The discussions come as authorities in South Kivu report what they describe as an improving socio-political and security situation in several areas, including the city of Uvira, following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces and the gradual restoration of state authority.
Officials indicate that stabilization efforts are ongoing in areas previously affected by intense fighting, with government presence being progressively re-established in territories that had fallen under rebel control during recent escalations.
The South Kivu provincial leadership estimates that more than 1.2 million people remain internally displaced, while around 800,000 Congolese refugees are still hosted in neighboring countries, particularly in Burundi and Tanzania. These populations were displaced amid years of conflict marked by grave human rights violations, including killings, kidnappings, torture, and sexual violence across several localities in the east.
Preparatory measures for returns are already underway, including demining operations aimed at clearing explosives left behind in conflict-affected zones to allow for safe resettlement of civilians.
The upcoming Kalemie meeting is expected to define practical modalities, timelines, and coordination mechanisms for the phased return of refugees, in collaboration with host countries and international partners.
Authorities say the return process has already begun in limited cases, but stress that large-scale repatriation will depend on sustained security guarantees and continued stabilization in eastern Congo, where pockets of insecurity persist despite recent withdrawals of armed groups from certain areas.

excerpt_en: Nia-Nia, Ituri Province April 3, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured on Friday, April 3, during violent unrest in Nia-Nia in Ituri Province, as public anger over repeated ADF attacks escalated into clashes between residents and security forces. The v
body_en:
Nia-Nia, Ituri Province April 3, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured on Friday, April 3, during violent unrest in Nia-Nia in Ituri Province, as public anger over repeated ADF attacks escalated into clashes between residents and security forces.
The violence erupted when a gold miner suspected of collaboration with armed groups was brought to the police station, sparking outrage among residents who gathered in large numbers and attempted to storm the facility.
Tensions quickly escalated into confrontations between protesters and police officers. In an effort to disperse the crowd, security forces opened fire, leaving one civilian dead and two others wounded.
During the unrest, another individual suspected by residents of involvement in recruitment activities for armed groups was also targeted by the crowd, highlighting the depth of mistrust and fear within the community.
The protests come amid growing anger over a series of deadly attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), including recent killings in nearby localities that left dozens of civilians dead, homes burned, and significant destruction of property.
Authorities have not yet issued a detailed statement on the incident, while tensions remain high in the area as communities continue to demand stronger protection against repeated armed violence.

title: Internal Divisions and Rivalries Weaken Cohesion Within M23 Leadership, Report Warns
excerpt: April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution. The assessment indicates
title_en: Internal Divisions and Rivalries Weaken Cohesion Within M23 Leadership, Report Warns
excerpt_en: April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution. The assessment indicates
body_en:
April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution.
The assessment indicates that the movement is divided along three main fault lines: tensions between its leadership and its external backers, rivalries between senior military commanders, and growing friction between its armed wing and its political structure, the Congo River Alliance (AFC).
At the military level, long-standing mistrust between M23 Chief of Staff General Sultani Makenga and external supporters is described as a structural source of instability. While Makenga has historically maintained close ties with regional actors, relations have been repeatedly strained by past conflicts, shifting alliances, and concerns over discipline and reliability within the chain of command.
The report also points to escalating competition between senior commanders, particularly between Makenga and General Baudouin Ngaruye, whose rivalry dates back to earlier phases of rebellion in eastern Congo. Although the two leaders were temporarily reconciled after rejoining the movement in recent years, tensions have reportedly re-emerged over operational authority and control of strategic resources, including customs revenue streams in areas under their influence.
Beyond military leadership disputes, the study underscores growing friction between the armed wing of M23 and its political leadership under the AFC, led by Corneille Nangaa. The political structure was created to broaden the movement’s base beyond its traditional support base, but has increasingly been marked by competing visions over strategy and end goals.
While the military leadership is largely focused on consolidating territorial control in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the political leadership is described as pursuing a broader national agenda, creating divergence in priorities and command structure.
The report warns that these internal divisions could significantly complicate any future peace process, recalling that similar fractures contributed to the collapse of the movement in previous years and remain a key vulnerability amid ongoing conflict dynamics in the region.

title: Deadly Ambush in Virunga National Park Leaves Two Dead and Several Abducted
excerpt: Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic
title_en: Deadly Ambush in Virunga National Park Leaves Two Dead and Several Abducted
excerpt_en: Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic
body_en:
Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The attack targeted vehicles traveling along the Kiwanja-Butembo axis when unidentified armed men opened fire on passengers. Two victims died instantly, while another was seriously wounded, according to accounts from the scene.
Several passengers were also taken hostage by the attackers, whose identity and whereabouts remain unknown, raising fears of further violence and insecurity for travelers using the route.
The ambush occurred just weeks after transport services had resumed along the Kiwanja-Kanyabayonga road following a temporary suspension caused by persistent insecurity in the region.
The area, which lies along a strategic corridor frequently affected by armed group activity, has experienced repeated attacks in recent months, further complicating efforts to restore safe civilian movement and stabilize transport networks in North Kivu Province.

title: M23 Expands Regional Influence Through Armed Alliances From Ituri to South Kivu
excerpt: April 5, 2026 - A new analysis indicates that the M23 movement has significantly expanded its influence beyond eastern North Kivu by building a structured network of armed alliances stretching from Ituri to South Kivu, reshaping the dynamics of armed conflict in eastern Democrati
title_en: M23 Expands Regional Influence Through Armed Alliances From Ituri to South Kivu
excerpt_en: April 5, 2026 - A new analysis indicates that the M23 movement has significantly expanded its influence beyond eastern North Kivu by building a structured network of armed alliances stretching from Ituri to South Kivu, reshaping the dynamics of armed conflict in eastern Democrati
body_en:
April 5, 2026 - A new analysis indicates that the M23 movement has significantly expanded its influence beyond eastern North Kivu by building a structured network of armed alliances stretching from Ituri to South Kivu, reshaping the dynamics of armed conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The report highlights the emergence of two main alliance axes since 2023: one in the northeast in Ituri Province and another in the south in South Kivu Province, enabling the movement and its political wing, the AFC, to extend operational reach beyond territories under its direct control.
In Ituri, M23-linked networks are said to have developed ties with local armed groups including Self-Defense of Victimized Communities of Ituri (ADCVI), also known as Zaïre, and the Convention for the People’s Revolution led by Thomas Lubanga. These relationships are described as being reinforced through training exchanges, leadership contacts, and battlefield coordination, with hundreds of fighters reportedly integrated into training structures associated with M23 over recent years.
The report notes that these connections were facilitated by intermediary commanders with longstanding influence in the region, contributing to the gradual integration of fighters from Ituri into broader operational structures linked to M23 and AFC leadership.
In South Kivu, the alliance-building process has centered on relations with Twirwaneho, an armed group rooted in the Banyamulenge community. Unlike in Ituri, the partnership developed more slowly due to initial mistrust and political hesitations within local leadership, but gradually solidified amid rising insecurity and repeated attacks against civilian populations in highland areas.
The alignment was ultimately strengthened through internal community pressures and shifting perceptions of protection and survival, leading Twirwaneho to formally integrate into the M23-linked framework in 2024.

title: Rwanda’s “Strategic Depth” Doctrine Shapes Its Involvement in Eastern Congo, Report Says
excerpt: April 5, 2026 - A new analysis argues that Rwanda’s support for the M23 operates within a broader military and geopolitical framework centered on the doctrine of “strategic depth,” resource interests, and regional security calculations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The
title_en: Rwanda’s “Strategic Depth” Doctrine Shapes Its Involvement in Eastern Congo, Report Says
excerpt_en: April 5, 2026 - A new analysis argues that Rwanda’s support for the M23 operates within a broader military and geopolitical framework centered on the doctrine of “strategic depth,” resource interests, and regional security calculations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The
body_en:
April 5, 2026 - A new analysis argues that Rwanda’s support for the M23 operates within a broader military and geopolitical framework centered on the doctrine of “strategic depth,” resource interests, and regional security calculations in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The report states that Kigali’s engagement in the conflict extends beyond the objectives of the M23 itself, combining military strategy, economic incentives, and domestic security considerations into a long-term regional posture.
On the military level, Rwanda is described as having adopted the concept of strategic depth as a core element of its defense doctrine, aiming to neutralize perceived threats beyond its borders before they reach national territory. Senior Rwandan officials have previously emphasized that cross-border security threats justify preventive military measures in eastern Congo, while acknowledging coordination with allied armed actors in the region.
The analysis also highlights the evolving nature of security cooperation between Kigali and armed groups operating in eastern Congo, including political and military coordination mechanisms that have developed in recent years.
Economically, the report points to a sharp rise in Rwanda’s mineral exports, particularly tantalum, and notes a significant increase in trade flows following the M23’s takeover of key mining areas in North Kivu, including Rubaya. These developments are presented as part of a broader pattern linking armed conflict zones to regional resource supply chains.
Beyond military and economic factors, the report identifies internal political and regional rivalry dynamics involving Uganda and Burundi as additional drivers shaping Kigali’s security posture, particularly in border areas where competing armed and military interests overlap.
The analysis stresses, however, that the relationship between Rwanda and the M23 should not be viewed as purely instrumental or one-sided. While interests often converge, the two do not always align, and historical precedent shows that alliances in the region remain fluid, with strategic priorities occasionally taking precedence over partnership commitments.

title: Uganda’s Discreet Role in M23 Resurgence and Recruitment Exposed, Report Says
excerpt: April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new anal
title_en: Uganda’s Discreet Role in M23 Resurgence and Recruitment Exposed, Report Says
excerpt_en: April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new anal
body_en:
April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new analysis.
The report outlines how, after the movement’s military defeat in 2013, most M23 fighters were relocated to Ugandan military facilities in southwestern Uganda, where they remained for several years under army supervision.
In 2017, M23 military leader Sultani Makenga reportedly left a Ugandan military camp and moved toward the border area around Mount Sabyinyo, near the tri-border zone between Uganda, Rwanda, and the DRC. His departure is described as having been quietly facilitated by elements within Uganda’s military structure, allowing a gradual return of leadership figures into Congolese territory.
The analysis further indicates that Uganda later became a key recruitment base during the M23’s remobilization phase beginning in 2021, with former encampment sites serving as a pool for new fighters joining the movement. This recruitment dynamic is presented as part of a broader and informal network involving military environments and cross-border mobility.
Tensions between regional states are also cited as a contributing factor to shifting alliances, particularly between Uganda and Rwanda, as competing security interests and military deployments in eastern Congo intensified.
The report also notes allegations of coordination between elements of the Ugandan armed forces and M23 recruits during training activities conducted in border regions of eastern Congo, alongside other regional military actors.
However, it emphasizes that the exact nature of Uganda’s involvement remains complex and not fully defined, and does not clearly distinguish between official state policy and the actions of individual military actors operating within broader regional security dynamics.
Conclusion
The period from late March to early April 2026 reflects a Democratic Republic of Congo navigating between meaningful institutional progress and enduring structural fragility. While authorities in Kinshasa advanced key reforms and strengthened international partnerships, the eastern regions remain gripped by insecurity and humanitarian strain.
Institutional and Economic Foundations
The launch of the second General Population and Housing Census marks a historic step toward modern governance, supported by an $80 million commitment from the African Development Bank. This initiative aims to close a decades-long data gap, laying the groundwork for better public policy and equitable development. At the same time, renewed mining diplomacy-through agreements with China and strategic discussions on lithium and cobalt-highlights the country’s ambition to move up the global value chain and assert greater economic sovereignty.
Political Tensions and Constitutional Debate
However, political dynamics remain fragile. The debate over constitutional revision continues to polarize national actors. The National Episcopal Conference of Congo has warned against initiating reforms without broad consensus, citing the current security climate. Meanwhile, opposition figure Moïse Katumbi has firmly rejected any attempt to amend the constitution, framing it as a potential threat to democratic stability. In parallel, President Félix Tshisekedi has called for improved cooperation between provincial institutions, underscoring persistent governance challenges linked to decentralization.

title: Interior Minister Reviews Preparations Ahead of Djibouti Presidential Election
excerpt: Djibouti, April 1, 2026 - With nine days remaining before the presidential election scheduled for April 10, the Minister of the Interior, Said Nouh Hassan, conducted a working visit to the Djibouti Prefecture to assess the progress of electoral preparations. According to an offic
title_en: Interior Minister Reviews Preparations Ahead of Djibouti Presidential Election
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 1, 2026 - With nine days remaining before the presidential election scheduled for April 10, the Minister of the Interior, Said Nouh Hassan, conducted a working visit to the Djibouti Prefecture to assess the progress of electoral preparations. According to an offic
body_en:
Djibouti, April 1, 2026 - With nine days remaining before the presidential election scheduled for April 10, the Minister of the Interior, Said Nouh Hassan, conducted a working visit to the Djibouti Prefecture to assess the progress of electoral preparations.
According to an official statement, the visit forms part of ongoing efforts to ensure compliance with national guidelines and the electoral calendar. Authorities indicated that preparations have entered their final phase and are progressing “satisfactorily” and within established deadlines.
During the visit, the minister praised the mobilization of local administrative services and the coordination among stakeholders involved in organizing the vote. He also commended the Prefect of Djibouti, Abdi Hassan Ahmed, for the quality of the work carried out, urging teams to maintain their efforts through to election day.
Preparations have focused on two main areas: the training of polling station personnel and the finalization of electoral materials.
Training sessions for presiding officers and polling staff were held on March 31 and April 1. Minister Said Nouh Hassan highlighted the importance of these sessions, describing them as essential to ensuring the proper conduct of the election. The training covered electoral regulations, voting procedures, vote counting, results centralization, and the roles and responsibilities of polling staff.
At the same time, logistical preparations are nearing completion, including the assembly and verification of ballot boxes, the distribution of official documents such as voter lists and ballots, and the provision of necessary equipment.
Authorities stated that these measures, carried out under the supervision of the prefectural administration, are designed to ensure full compliance with electoral standards and to facilitate a process that is free, transparent, and credible.

title: Djiboutian Gendarmerie Deploys Peacekeeping Contingent to Central African Republic
excerpt: Djibouti, April 6, 2026 - A contingent of gendarmes from the fourth rotation of the Joint Force departed Djibouti at dawn on April 6 for deployment to the Central African Republic, underscoring the country’s continued participation in international peacekeeping operations. The de
title_en: Djiboutian Gendarmerie Deploys Peacekeeping Contingent to Central African Republic
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 6, 2026 - A contingent of gendarmes from the fourth rotation of the Joint Force departed Djibouti at dawn on April 6 for deployment to the Central African Republic, underscoring the country’s continued participation in international peacekeeping operations. The de
body_en:
Djibouti, April 6, 2026 - A contingent of gendarmes from the fourth rotation of the Joint Force departed Djibouti at dawn on April 6 for deployment to the Central African Republic, underscoring the country’s continued participation in international peacekeeping operations.
The deployment took place under the supervision of the Chief of Staff of the National Gendarmerie, Zakaria Hassan Aden, who oversaw the departure alongside senior military officials.
The personnel boarded a United Nations-chartered aircraft as part of their mission to support stability and security operations in the Central African Republic, reinforcing Djibouti’s role in regional and international peace efforts.
Speaking at the departure ceremony, Colonel Zakaria Hassan Aden expressed pride in the departing troops and emphasized the importance of their mission. He urged them to uphold discipline and courage in defending the principles of peace and security in line with Djibouti’s international commitments.
He also acknowledged the support of the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, noting that sustained institutional backing has made such deployments possible. According to military officials, the operation reflects the National Gendarmerie’s broader strategy of contributing to international cooperation and peacekeeping frameworks.
The deployment is part of Djibouti’s ongoing contribution to United Nations missions in conflict-affected regions, where its forces serve alongside international partners in stabilization efforts.

title_en: AMIA Entrance Exam Kicks Off for 18th Cohort in Arta
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 9, 2026 - The first round of entrance examinations for the 18th cohort of the Joint Military Academy of Arta (AMIA) was launched on Thursday, marking the beginning of a rigorous selection process for future military officers. Following a preliminary screening phas
body_en:
Djibouti, April 9, 2026 - The first round of entrance examinations for the 18th cohort of the Joint Military Academy of Arta (AMIA) was launched on Thursday, marking the beginning of a rigorous selection process for future military officers.
Following a preliminary screening phase based on application reviews, only candidates meeting the required criteria were selected to participate in the competitive examination.
The opening day was dedicated to physical and athletic assessments designed to evaluate candidates’ endurance, strength, and discipline. The tests included pull-ups, sit-ups, push-ups, and a 1,000-meter run.
Military officials described the exercise as a key stage in identifying future leaders, emphasizing the importance of physical readiness, resilience, and determination as core qualities for admission into the academy.

title: Djibouti Coast Guard Intercepts Migrant Smuggling Vessel Near Obock

body_en:
Djibouti, April 12, 2026 - The Djiboutian Coast Guard has intercepted a vessel carrying undocumented migrants and armed smugglers off the coast of Obock, near the strategic Bab el-Mandeb maritime corridor.
According to security authorities, the operation was carried out during reinforced maritime surveillance activities around the Seven Brothers Islands, a key transit zone at the entrance to the Red Sea.
A patrol unit based in Khor Angar detected and intercepted the vessel as it attempted to enter Djiboutian territorial waters near Assa Fod, after reportedly departing from the Yemeni coast.
Nine undocumented migrants were taken into custody during the operation. Authorities stated that the vessel also carried armed smugglers in possession of an AK-47 assault rifle and two loaded magazines, allegedly intended to facilitate an illegal landing along the Obock coastline.
The Coast Guard has opened an investigation through its Criminal Investigation Brigade to determine the circumstances of the operation and to assess possible links to transnational smuggling networks operating between Yemen and Djibouti.
The individuals apprehended are expected to be referred to judicial authorities in the coming days as investigations continue.

title: MONUSCO Welcomes 14 New International Police Officers to Strengthen Civilian Protection
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 9, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) has officially welcomed fourteen new Individual Police Officers (IPOs), including six women, following the completion of their initial training aimed at strengthen
title_en: MONUSCO Welcomes 14 New International Police Officers to Strengthen Civilian Protection
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 9, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) has officially welcomed fourteen new Individual Police Officers (IPOs), including six women, following the completion of their initial training aimed at strengthen
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 9, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) has officially welcomed fourteen new Individual Police Officers (IPOs), including six women, following the completion of their initial training aimed at strengthening civilian protection efforts.
The new officers come from eleven contributing countries: Djibouti, Gambia, Togo, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Brazil, Tanzania, Canada, Chad, and Bangladesh.
The closing ceremony of their induction training was marked by remarks from the Head of the UN Police component, Inspector General Mamouna Ouedraogo, who underscored the importance of MONUSCO’s mandate in protecting civilians and supporting the restoration of state authority in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
She urged the new officers to embody core United Nations values, including discipline, self-control, and teamwork, while maintaining strict professionalism and operational effectiveness in the field.
Ouedraogo also reiterated the UN’s zero-tolerance policy on sexual exploitation and abuse, calling on personnel to uphold the highest ethical standards and avoid any conduct that could harm communities or undermine the mission’s credibility.
Highlighting the operational context in the DRC, she emphasized the expected impact of their deployment on both local populations and MONUSCO’s broader stabilization efforts.
The fourteen officers completed a structured training program designed to equip them with essential skills for their mission. The curriculum, delivered by experienced UN experts, covered a wide range of strategic and operational topics relevant to peacekeeping policing duties.
Conclusion
The first half of April 2026 was defined by a major democratic milestone and the continued expansion of Djibouti’s strategic infrastructure. The period was marked by the re-election of President Ismail Omar Guelleh and significant international partnerships aimed at long-term economic resilience.
Political Stability and Electoral Outcomes
The national political landscape was dominated by the presidential election held on April 10.
Decisive Re-election: President Ismail Omar Guelleh secured a fifth term with 97.81% of the vote, defeating challenger Mohamed Farah Samatar.
International Recognition: Delegations from the African Union, IGAD, and the OIC observed the process, and world leaders from France, Somalia, and Saudi Arabia extended congratulations, praising the election's transparency.
National Cohesion: Following his concession, Samatar met with President Guelleh at the Presidential Palace to wish him success, a gesture presented by officials as a sign of political maturity.
Mourning of a Political Figure: Earlier in the month, the nation mourned the passing of Ali Mohamed Daoud, president of the FRUD, leading to a temporary three-day suspension of the presidential campaign.
Economic Development and Infrastructure
Djibouti made substantial progress in its ambition to become a regional maritime and technological hub.
Maritime Advancement: The inauguration of the €107.5 million Djibouti Ship Repair Yard (DSRY) near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait provides the region with its largest floating dock, expected to generate up to 1,750 direct and indirect jobs.
Water Security: A $36.5 million agreement with the World Bank was signed to increase national drinking water coverage to 98% by 2030. Additionally, the Douda wastewater treatment plant expansion was highlighted during a French diplomatic visit.
Innovation in AI: A joint initiative with Somalia saw the launch of the Somali-Language AI & Innovation Lab (SAIL), focusing on using deep learning to detect fake news in the Somali language.

Authorities and humanitarian agencies continue search and rescue operations as concerns grow over migration routes across the Horn of Africa.

title: Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia reinforce cooperation on maritime security and migration
excerpt: Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 - Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows. The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improv
title_en: Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia reinforce cooperation on maritime security and migration
excerpt_en: Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 - Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows. The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improv
body_en:
Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 - Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows.
The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improving coordination in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, particularly in response to rising migration risks and maritime safety concerns.
Officials from the three countries emphasized their shared interest in promoting regional stability and addressing irregular migration challenges through joint efforts.
Conclusion
Djibouti enters April 2026 at a decisive moment, shaped mainly by the April 10 presidential election, where final preparations are complete and voter participation is expected to be strong.
At the same time, the country is pursuing economic diversification, with major investments in infrastructure, housing, mining, and new partnerships with international financial institutions.
However, humanitarian and security challenges remain, especially migration risks in the Red Sea, recurring shipwrecks off Obock, and ongoing regional tensions that require continued vigilance.
Overall, Djibouti is balancing electoral stability, economic reform, and regional pressures, with the coming election seen as a key moment for its political and economic trajectory in 2026.
By Kader K.
Jeff Buleli

excerpt: Bamako, April 10, 2026 - Mali has strengthened its cooperation with the International Organization for Migration in efforts to improve coordination and governance of migration-related policies. The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, rece
title_en: Mali and IOM Reinforce Cooperation on Migration Governance Ahead of Global Forum
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 10, 2026 - Mali has strengthened its cooperation with the International Organization for Migration in efforts to improve coordination and governance of migration-related policies. The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, rece
body_en:
Bamako, April 10, 2026 - Mali has strengthened its cooperation with the International Organization for Migration in efforts to improve coordination and governance of migration-related policies.
The Minister for Malians Living Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, received the Head of Mission of the International Organization for Migration, Dr. Boubacar Seybou, alongside his technical team for discussions in Bamako.
Talks focused on reinforcing the existing dialogue framework between the ministry and the IOM, as well as ensuring regular monitoring of joint activities. Both sides reviewed the implementation of a shared roadmap that guides their cooperation on migration governance.
The two parties also agreed on the need to convene a broader coordination meeting involving all relevant stakeholders to harmonize interventions and strengthen overall effectiveness in the field of migration management.
Preparations for the upcoming International Migration Review Forum in New York were also discussed, with an emphasis on increasing Mali’s participation and ensuring its priorities are effectively represented at the global level.

body_en:
Bamako, April 3, 2026 - Mali is reinforcing its commitment to youth empowerment and sustainable economic development through closer collaboration with civic organizations, following a meeting between government officials and young entrepreneurs in Bamako.
The Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Vocational Training, Oumou Sall Seck, received Kindia Cissé, Local President of the Junior Chamber International Bamako Ciwara, along with her delegation.
During the audience, the JCI representative sought ministerial sponsorship for the organization’s 2026 activities and requested strategic guidance to support the successful implementation of its initiatives.
Discussions highlighted the alignment between the organization’s programs and the government’s priorities, particularly in the areas of green entrepreneurship and vocational training. Among the key initiatives presented were the “J’Entreprends” project, focused on promoting environmentally sustainable business ventures, and the “Kalanso” program, aimed at strengthening access to training and skills development.
Officials emphasized the importance of such partnerships in fostering innovation, supporting youth-led initiatives, and advancing inclusive economic growth in Mali.

body_en:
Bamako, April 2, 2026 - Mali’s transitional government has reaffirmed its commitment to agricultural development following a high-level review meeting chaired by Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga.
The 16th session of the National Executive Committee for Agriculture (CENA), held at the Prime Minister’s Office, brought together key stakeholders to assess the 2025 agricultural campaign and outline projections through 2028.
Discussions were framed within the long-term national vision “Mali Kura ɲɛtaasira ka bɛn san 2063 ma,” reflecting the country’s ambition for sustained growth and resilience in the agricultural sector.
According to official figures presented during the session, the 2025 campaign delivered encouraging results, with cereal production reaching over 11.4 million tons, alongside significant outputs in cotton, livestock, dairy, and fisheries. Prime Minister Maïga praised producers for their resilience in maintaining productivity despite ongoing challenges.
Looking ahead, the government projects an increase in cereal production to nearly 11.9 million tons in 2026, while cotton output is expected to rise substantially. Authorities also announced a planned budget allocation of 164.4 billion CFA francs for the 2026 agricultural campaign, marking a 2 percent increase compared to the previous year.
Officials emphasized that these projections and investments aim to strengthen food security, boost rural incomes, and support sustainable agricultural transformation across Mali.

body_en:
Bamako, March 28, 2026 - Mali’s authorities and Chinese partners have conducted a joint inspection of the Safo solar power plant construction site, underscoring ongoing efforts to expand renewable energy capacity in the country.
The visit was led by the Minister of Energy and Water, Prof. Tiémoko Traoré, alongside the Ambassador of China to Mali, Li Xiang.
The inspection brought together representatives from the Presidency of Mali, officials from the energy sector, the management of Énergie du Mali (EDM-SA), as well as engineers and contractors from Sinohydro, the firm responsible for executing the project.
The mission focused on assessing the progress of the 50 MWp Safo photovoltaic solar power plant, particularly Phase I of construction, and ensuring compliance with contractual timelines and technical requirements.
Authorities described the visit as part of strengthened oversight efforts aimed at accelerating infrastructure delivery and improving energy access across Mali.

title_en: Mali Introduces Fuel Price Regulation Measures Amid Global Oil Price Surge
excerpt_en: Bamako, March 31, 2026 - The Government of Mali has announced new regulatory measures on petroleum product pricing in response to rising global oil costs linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. According to authorities, the decision aims to safeguard national fuel supp
body_en:
Bamako, March 31, 2026 - The Government of Mali has announced new regulatory measures on petroleum product pricing in response to rising global oil costs linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
According to authorities, the decision aims to safeguard national fuel supplies and ensure the continuity of economic activity despite external market pressures. The government also confirmed that it has temporarily waived a portion of customs revenue to help mitigate the impact of price increases on consumers.
The Directorate General of Trade, Consumer Affairs, and Competition stressed that any adjustments to fuel prices must strictly comply with the national legal framework. Economic operators have been urged to exercise restraint and engage in dialogue to limit the effects of international price volatility on the domestic market.
Officials further warned that unjustified price increases will not be tolerated and will be subject to sanctions under existing regulations. The government called for collective responsibility to maintain price stability and protect consumers across the country.

title_en: Mali Reviews Fuel Supply Chain as Authorities Report Sustained Hydrocarbon Imports
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 9, 2026 - The Government of Mali has reaffirmed its efforts to stabilize petroleum product supply and strengthen oversight of the hydrocarbons sector amid ongoing distribution constraints. The 19th consultation meeting with stakeholders in the sector was chaired by
body_en:
Bamako, April 9, 2026 - The Government of Mali has reaffirmed its efforts to stabilize petroleum product supply and strengthen oversight of the hydrocarbons sector amid ongoing distribution constraints.
The 19th consultation meeting with stakeholders in the sector was chaired by Minister Moussa Alassane Diallo, and focused on monitoring national fuel availability, identifying logistical bottlenecks, and reinforcing measures against illegal practices in the market.
Officials reported that between March 30 and April 5, a total of 640 fuel tankers were received, corresponding to approximately 29 million liters of petroleum products. Authorities described these figures as evidence of continued efforts by operators to sustain supply levels despite persistent challenges.
For the current week, projections indicate the dispatch of 522 tankers across the country, signaling ongoing distribution operations aimed at meeting national demand.
The meeting also reviewed March import data, which recorded a cumulative volume of 116 million liters of fuel entering the country.
Authorities emphasized that these coordination efforts are intended to ensure market stability, maintain supply continuity, and strengthen regulatory enforcement across the hydrocarbons sector.

body_en:
Bamako, April 4, 2026 - Mali has renewed its focus on strengthening oral healthcare as a key component of public health policy, during the opening of the 8th Scientific Conference of the Malian Order of Dental Surgeons.
The conference, held in Bamako, comes amid ongoing reforms within the national health sector and has placed particular emphasis on repositioning bucco-dental health as a strategic public policy priority.
From the opening session, health authorities called for stronger integration of oral healthcare into national health systems, especially in terms of financing, accessibility, and service delivery. Participants stressed that persistent structural challenges continue to limit equitable access to dental care across the country.
The Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali highlighted what he described as insufficient attention historically given to oral health, urging reforms to better align it with broader national health objectives.
The conference is expected to produce recommendations aimed at improving policy coordination, strengthening professional capacity, and expanding access to dental services nationwide.

The Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship, and Customs, Dr. Mahamadou Koné, received the coordinator of the national NGO Think Peace, Abdou Kola Bocoum, for discussions aimed at strengthening national peacebuilding strategies.

title: Security Deteriorates in Azawad as Rights Group Reports Civilian Abuses Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt: Azawad, March 2026 - The security and humanitarian situation in northern Mali’s Azawad region has sharply deteriorated, with civilians increasingly caught in escalating violence, according to the monthly report No. 03/AKA/2026 published by the Kal Akal Association. The report doc
title_en: Security Deteriorates in Azawad as Rights Group Reports Civilian Abuses Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt_en: Azawad, March 2026 - The security and humanitarian situation in northern Mali’s Azawad region has sharply deteriorated, with civilians increasingly caught in escalating violence, according to the monthly report No. 03/AKA/2026 published by the Kal Akal Association. The report doc
body_en:
Azawad, March 2026 - The security and humanitarian situation in northern Mali’s Azawad region has sharply deteriorated, with civilians increasingly caught in escalating violence, according to the monthly report No. 03/AKA/2026 published by the Kal Akal Association.
The report documents a rise in abuses against civilians during March 2026, including executions, massacres, arbitrary arrests, and forced disappearances. It attributes some incidents to armed elements linked to the Islamic State group, while also citing operations conducted by joint patrols involving the Malian Armed Forces and Russian personnel from the Afrika Korps.
According to the findings, nine cases of executions and massacres were recorded, alongside three cases of arrests and disappearances, including detentions in the Timbuktu region and the disappearance of a shepherd near Kidal. One serious injury was also reported during a military operation involving the Malian Armed Forces, supported by Russian forces.
The report further highlights seven incidents of destruction and looting, including the burning of homes, destruction of water wells, confiscation of livestock, and damage to civilian property. These incidents, it notes, have severely affected already vulnerable rural and nomadic communities.
The Kal Akal Association strongly condemned the violence and called for an end to impunity, urging the international community to pay closer attention to the situation in Azawad. It also called for independent investigations and urgent measures to protect civilians.

body_en:
Bamako, April 10, 2026 - Future pilgrims from Mali have begun structured physical preparation sessions ahead of the 2026 Hajj, as part of a joint initiative by government ministries aimed at improving pilgrims’ fitness and readiness.
The program was launched under the supervision of the Ministry of Religious Affairs, Worship, and Customs in coordination with the Ministry of Sports. It brings together men and women selected for the pilgrimage in guided fitness sessions designed to strengthen endurance and physical capacity.
Participants responded in large numbers to the call, taking part in exercises in an atmosphere described as both disciplined and encouraging. Organizers say the initiative is intended to ensure that pilgrims are physically prepared to complete the demanding rites of the Hajj under optimal conditions.
The effort is also part of a broader national fitness promotion policy led by the Ministry of Sports, which aims to integrate physical well-being programs across different government sectors.
Officials emphasized that the initiative reflects a holistic approach to pilgrimage preparation, combining both spiritual readiness and physical conditioning to support a successful Hajj experience.

excerpt_en: Bamako, April 9, 2026 - Mali has inaugurated the 11th edition of the Donso N’Goni Festival, a major cultural gathering celebrating traditional hunters and West African heritage, with a strong message centered on peace and reconciliation. The opening ceremony was presided over by
body_en:
Bamako, April 9, 2026 - Mali has inaugurated the 11th edition of the Donso N’Goni Festival, a major cultural gathering celebrating traditional hunters and West African heritage, with a strong message centered on peace and reconciliation.
The opening ceremony was presided over by the Minister of Handicrafts, Culture, Hospitality, and Tourism, Mamou Daffé, at the Amadou Hampâté Bâ Cultural Center in Bamako. He was joined by the Minister of Environment, Sanitation, and Sustainable Development, Doumbia Mariam Tangara.
Organized by the Jigiya Blon Association under the leadership of Cheick Oumar Tembely, the festival runs from April 9 to 11, 2026, under the theme “Peace and Reconciliation in the ESA Countries.” The event is sponsored by former minister Abdramane Sylla.
The festival brings together traditional hunters (donso), researchers, and cultural enthusiasts from across the sub-region, including participants from Guinea, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
The opening ceremony featured cultural performances, including a notable appearance by artist Sékoubani Traoré, drawing strong audience engagement and highlighting the vitality of traditional music and spiritual expression.
Over three days, the festival is expected to feature performances, academic discussions, and exhibitions aimed at preserving and promoting cultural heritage while fostering regional unity through tradition.

Bamako, April 8, 2026 - Mali has launched a series of nationwide health promotion activities ahead of World Health Day 2026, focusing on prevention, awareness, and free medical services for the population.
The Ministry of Health and Social Development is organizing a major public event on April 9, 2026, at the Mamadou Konaté Stadium in Bamako. The program includes free medical consultations, screening campaigns, and panel discussions on communicable diseases, alongside sporting activities aimed at promoting healthy lifestyles.
The initiative is expected to be attended by senior government officials, including Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, alongside other ministerial representatives.
Ahead of the launch, the Secretary General of the Ministry, Dr. Abdoulaye Guindo, together with the Director General of Health and Public Hygiene and representatives of the World Health Organization, held a press conference to officially announce the start of the 2026 World Health Day activities.
The program extends beyond the capital, with awareness campaigns, free screenings, and community mobilization activities planned across Bamako and several regions of Mali.
Officials emphasized that the initiative aims to strengthen public health awareness and encourage preventive healthcare practices nationwide.

body_en:
Bamako, April 9, 2026 - Mali has marked International Women’s Day with a high-level ceremony dedicated to strengthening women’s access to justice and advancing gender equality reforms within the national legal system.
Organized at the Ministry of Justice conference room, the event featured a conference on women’s and girls’ access to justice, highlighting the implementation of the ministry’s newly adopted gender strategy.
The Minister of Justice, Mamoudou Kassogué, presented ongoing judicial reforms, including updates to the Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure. According to officials, these reforms aim to strengthen legal responses to gender-based violence and expand access to free legal aid services.
The ministry also announced the deployment of gender focal points within courts across the country, alongside continued training programs for judicial staff. Minister Kassogué reiterated the government’s commitment to combating impunity and protecting vulnerable groups, stressing that respect for women’s rights is fundamental to social stability.
The ceremony brought together key stakeholders, including Ms. Laurence Douyon, Project Manager and Gender Focal Point at the Ministry of Justice, as well as representatives of UN Women in Mali.
Participants welcomed the adoption of the ministry’s first gender strategy and called for coordinated action to ensure that legal equality is effectively implemented in practice. UN representatives also emphasized the role of justice systems in protecting women and urged sustained reforms to guarantee long-term social protection and stability within families.

body_en:
Bamako, April 7, 2026 - Mali has officially launched a new series of judicial training sessions aimed at strengthening the capacity and professionalism of actors within the country’s justice system.
The program was inaugurated by the Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, Mamoudou Kassogué, at the Me Demba Diallo National Institute for Judicial Training (INFJ). The ceremony was co-chaired by a representative of the Ambassador of the Netherlands and brought together judicial stakeholders, technical partners, and development actors.
According to INFJ Director General Dr. Toubaye Koné, the sessions mark the beginning of a broader capacity-building program for judicial personnel, with the first module focusing on the management of land disputes. Additional thematic training sessions are expected to follow in the coming months.
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) reaffirmed its support for judicial reforms in Mali, emphasizing its continued commitment to strengthening the rule of law and protecting fundamental rights through targeted training initiatives.
Minister Kassogué described the program as a key step in aligning judicial skills with the requirements of a modern, efficient, and credible justice system, stressing the importance of continuous professional development for all justice sector actors.

body_en:
Ménaka, April 2, 2026 - Armed violence intensified in northeastern Mali after the Islamic State in the Sahel claimed responsibility for a deadly attack on Malian military positions in and around the town of Ménaka.
According to statements attributed to the group, the assault took place on March 27, 2026, targeting an exit route toward Andéramboukane. The group claimed it killed two Malian soldiers, burned two military vehicles, and seized weapons and ammunition, including a heavy machine gun and Kalashnikov rifles.
The group also reported a separate clash at the entrance to Ménaka, during which one of its fighters was killed, while Malian forces and allied units allegedly suffered additional casualties and equipment losses.
Local sources cited in the report indicated that the fighting also had a civilian toll, with four people reportedly killed by stray bullets, including women and children, as hostilities unfolded in the area.
The claims could not be independently verified, and the Malian authorities had not issued an immediate official statement at the time of reporting.
The incident highlights the continuing insecurity in Mali’s northern regions, where armed groups remain active despite ongoing counterterrorism operations.

body_en:
Nouakchott, March 27, 2026 - The government of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania has issued a strong condemnation following reported violations against its citizens allegedly involving the Malian military near the shared border with Mali.
In an official statement, Mauritanian authorities expressed “profound indignation” and concern over recent security incidents on Malian territory close to the frontier, which resulted in the deaths of several Mauritanian nationals.
The government identified the victims as Alassane Mamadou Sow, Mahmoud Abou Sily, Yoro Abou Sow, Hamadou Kandouro Ba, and Mahmoud Kandouro Ba, and extended condolences to their families while affirming national solidarity.
Nouakchott called on Malian authorities to halt what it described as violations, open credible investigations, and ensure stronger protection for civilians in border regions. It also stressed the importance of safeguarding Mauritanian citizens and urged heightened vigilance along the frontier areas.
While reaffirming its commitment to maintaining peaceful bilateral relations, Mauritania stated that it reserves the right to take all appropriate measures in accordance with international law in response to the incident.

Gao, March 28, 2026 - Three nationals of Benin were abducted in northern Mali after being removed from a bus traveling along the Ansongo-Labbezanga road in the Gao region.
The incident occurred near Ouattagouna, where one woman and two men were reportedly intercepted and taken to an unknown destination by members of the Islamic State in the Sahel.
Local sources indicate the passengers were traveling through a corridor frequently affected by insecurity linked to armed groups operating in the area.
No further information has been released regarding the whereabouts of the abducted individuals, and authorities have not yet issued an official statement on the incident.
The abduction adds to ongoing concerns over civilian safety along key transit routes in northern Mali, where armed groups continue to operate despite security operations.

excerpt_en: Kidal, March 30, 2026 - The security situation in northern Mali remains highly volatile after the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) announced a coordinated attack targeting Malian forces and allied personnel in the Anefif area. In a statement, the group said it carried out the operat
body_en:
Kidal, March 30, 2026 - The security situation in northern Mali remains highly volatile after the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) announced a coordinated attack targeting Malian forces and allied personnel in the Anefif area.
In a statement, the group said it carried out the operation using two kamikaze drones and 18 shells against positions allegedly held by the Malian Armed Forces and Russian personnel affiliated with the Afrika Korps.
The FLA claimed the attack resulted in seven fatalities and nine injuries, as well as the destruction of two armored vehicles and one truck. It also reported the burning of a fuel depot and the disabling of a communications center. According to the statement, casualties were evacuated by helicopter to Gao.
The group further claimed it suffered no losses during the operation. Visual reports cited in local accounts described smoke rising from the targeted military camp following the assault.
As of publication, the Malian authorities had not issued an official statement confirming or denying the reported attack.

title_en: Bamako Faces Severe Utility Crisis Amid Widespread Power and Water Outages
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 2, 2026 - Mali’s capital is grappling with an acute public utility crisis marked by prolonged electricity outages, shortages of drinking water, and sharply rising fuel prices. Residents of Mali reported more than 24 hours without power in several districts of Bamako
body_en:
Bamako, April 2, 2026 - Mali’s capital is grappling with an acute public utility crisis marked by prolonged electricity outages, shortages of drinking water, and sharply rising fuel prices.
Residents of Mali reported more than 24 hours without power in several districts of Bamako, alongside disruptions in water supply systems and growing difficulties in accessing fuel.
The situation prompted an unusual public response from the Minister of Energy and Water, who personally distributed water in the Tabacoro area, an initiative that was welcomed by segments of the population as a gesture of solidarity amid worsening living conditions.
Despite the arrival of hundreds of fuel tankers in the capital, authorities acknowledged that supply levels remain insufficient to meet demand in a city increasingly affected by paralysis across essential services.
The combined shortages have intensified public concern, with transport, household consumption, and economic activity all severely impacted as Bamako continues to face simultaneous pressures on its energy and water infrastructure.

title: Fuel Shortages Persist in Mali Despite Recent Supply Arrivals
excerpt: Bamako, April 2026 - Fuel supply disruptions continue to affect several parts of Mali, with petrol and diesel shortages reported at multiple service stations operated under the Shell network. In a statement, Vivo Energy Mali confirmed temporary shortages of gasoline and diesel at
title_en: Fuel Shortages Persist in Mali Despite Recent Supply Arrivals
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 2026 - Fuel supply disruptions continue to affect several parts of Mali, with petrol and diesel shortages reported at multiple service stations operated under the Shell network. In a statement, Vivo Energy Mali confirmed temporary shortages of gasoline and diesel at
body_en:
Bamako, April 2026 - Fuel supply disruptions continue to affect several parts of Mali, with petrol and diesel shortages reported at multiple service stations operated under the Shell network.
In a statement, Vivo Energy Mali confirmed temporary shortages of gasoline and diesel at selected outlets, attributing the situation to ongoing supply chain disruptions affecting national distribution.
Authorities and industry sources indicate that the crisis, which began in September 2025, is linked to a broader fuel supply disruption caused by a blockade attributed to the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin). The situation has reportedly been punctuated by temporary arrangements involving negotiations for the passage of fuel convoys.
According to reports, a recent agreement reached on March 18 led to the release of approximately 200 individuals in exchange for the safe passage of fuel tankers toward the capital. Despite the arrival of hundreds of trucks in recent days, supply levels remain insufficient to meet the needs of Bamako, where economic activity continues to be heavily disrupted.
The fuel shortage adds to broader pressures on transport, electricity generation, and basic services, as the capital continues to experience periodic shortages and distribution constraints.

Bamako, April 2, 2026 - The Malian Armed Forces have announced the neutralization of more than fifty suspected militants during an operation in the Ségou region, according to a statement from the military General Staff.
The announcement stated that the operation followed a reconnaissance mission carried out on April 1, 2026, during which forces identified a training camp belonging to an armed group in a wooded area approximately 20 kilometers north of Markala.
Following the discovery, the Malian Armed Forces (Malian Armed Forces) reportedly launched an intervention against the site, which the army described as being used by an armed terrorist group.
The military indicated that the operation resulted in the neutralization of more than fifty individuals, though no independent verification of the figures has been provided.
The General Staff did not immediately release additional details regarding potential losses on the military side or the identity of those targeted.
The operation comes amid sustained security operations in central Mali, where armed groups remain active despite ongoing counterterrorism efforts.
