Kidal Region, April 7, 2026 - Armed activity intensified in northern Mali after Azawad forces announced two coordinated military operations targeting Malian and allied positions in the Kidal region.
In a statement accompanied by video material, the group said it carried out suicide drone strikes against positions held by the Malian Armed Forces and Russian personnel associated with the African Corps in Aguelhok. The group claimed the strikes caused casualties and material damage, though these assertions could not be independently verified.
The same day, the group also reported a separate attack targeting an armored vehicle in Tioraghen, located approximately 35 kilometers south of Kidal. According to its statement, this second operation likewise resulted in casualties and equipment losses.
No official confirmation of the incidents or their reported outcomes had been issued by Malian authorities at the time of reporting.
The claims come amid continued insecurity in northern Mali, where multiple armed actors remain active and frequently report clashes with government and allied forces.

excerpt_en: Azawad, April 6, 2026 - Several towns in northern Mali, including Tinzaouatène and Timbuktu, marked the 14th anniversary of the declaration of independence proclaimed on April 6, 2012, through symbolic gatherings and public commemorations. Residents participated in events reaffir
body_en:
Azawad, April 6, 2026 - Several towns in northern Mali, including Tinzaouatène and Timbuktu, marked the 14th anniversary of the declaration of independence proclaimed on April 6, 2012, through symbolic gatherings and public commemorations.
Residents participated in events reaffirming their attachment to Azawad identity and expressing continued support for self-determination. The commemorations were largely symbolic, featuring community gatherings and political messaging centered on regional identity.
The Strategic Reflection Forum for Azawad issued statements on April 6 and 9, 2026, urging the United Nations to recognize the right to self-determination and to initiate an international investigation into alleged human rights violations in the region.
The forum also criticized the Malian authorities, citing what it described as insufficient political representation and worsening security conditions. It further called for international protection measures for civilian populations affected by ongoing instability.
The commemorations highlight continuing political tensions in northern Mali, where questions of governance, security, and identity remain highly contested alongside persistent armed conflict.

title: Mali-Mauritania Border Tensions Rise Amid Disputed Reports of Military Movements
excerpt: Hodh El Gharbi / Border Areas, April 11, 2026 - Tensions have emerged along the frontier between Mali and Mauritania following reports of repeated movements involving Malian military forces in areas inhabited by Mauritanian nationals. Local accounts from the Hodh El Gharbi region
title_en: Mali-Mauritania Border Tensions Rise Amid Disputed Reports of Military Movements
excerpt_en: Hodh El Gharbi / Border Areas, April 11, 2026 - Tensions have emerged along the frontier between Mali and Mauritania following reports of repeated movements involving Malian military forces in areas inhabited by Mauritanian nationals. Local accounts from the Hodh El Gharbi region
body_en:
Hodh El Gharbi / Border Areas, April 11, 2026 - Tensions have emerged along the frontier between Mali and Mauritania following reports of repeated movements involving Malian military forces in areas inhabited by Mauritanian nationals.
Local accounts from the Hodh El Gharbi region have raised concerns among communities and political actors, prompting official clarifications from Mauritanian authorities. The governor of Hodh El Gharbi, Mohamed Ould Ahmed Mouloud, stated that the areas in question are located within Malian territory according to official cartographic references, despite being populated by Mauritanian citizens.
In a separate statement issued on April 11, the Mauritanian armed forces sought to ease concerns, describing the movements as routine visits to villages situated near the border, including Biyzia, Ktaâ Dafaou, Ahl Ibrahim, and Foussat. The military stressed that these localities fall within Malian territory and rejected interpretations of the movements as incursions.
However, political tensions have been fueled by criticism from some Mauritanian lawmakers. Fatma bint Ehel Mahmoud, a member of parliament for the Kobeni district, called for urgent clarification from authorities, citing what she described as repeated violations of border norms. She also warned that growing political rhetoric on both sides could further destabilize the already sensitive border zone.
The broader debate has been intensified by discussions surrounding historical border arrangements, including references to the 1963 Kais Agreement, with some voices warning against any revisionist claims that could heighten regional tensions.
While Mauritanian authorities have reaffirmed their commitment to securing national borders, officials on both sides emphasize the need for continued dialogue and clearer demarcation to prevent further misunderstandings in a region marked by close cross-border community ties.
Conclusion
The reporting period from March 29 to April 12, 2026, reflects a Mali navigating a complex landscape of assertive diplomacy, structural economic challenges, and a volatile security environment.
Diplomatic Realignment and Regional Leadership Mali has notably recalibrated its foreign policy, most significantly by withdrawing recognition of the Sahrawi Republic in favor of supporting Moroccan sovereignty, a move that has strengthened ties with Rabat while drawing criticism from Algiers. Simultaneously, Bamako has demonstrated leadership within the African Group at the UN and reaffirmed its commitment to the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), advocating for a multilateralism that prioritizes national sovereignty and regional solidarity.
Economic Resilience Amidst Utility Crises On the domestic front, the government reported strong agricultural performance for 2025, with cereal production exceeding 11.4 million tons, and set ambitious targets for 2026. However, these successes are contrasted by an acute utility crisis in Bamako, characterized by prolonged power and water outages and persistent fuel shortages. Despite the arrival of over 600 fuel tankers in early April, supply remains insufficient to stabilize the market against global oil price volatility and local distribution bottlenecks.
Security Volatility and Humanitarian Concerns The security situation remains the most critical challenge, marked by persistent IED attacks and abductions by groups such as JNIM and IS-Sahel across the northern, central, and southern corridors. While the Malian Armed Forces reported the neutralization of over 50 militants in the Ségou region, northern areas like Ménaka and Kidal continue to see escalating violence and reports of civilian abuses. Furthermore, border tensions with Mauritania have emerged following fatal incidents involving Mauritanian nationals, necessitating careful diplomatic engagement to maintain regional stability.
In summary, while Mali is making strategic strides in international diplomacy and agricultural planning, the immediate path forward is heavily pressured by the need for enhanced internal security and the stabilization of essential public services.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

title: Mali Secures Geographic Indication for Bogolan, Strengthening Protection of Textile Heritage
excerpt: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali has taken a major step in safeguarding its cultural heritage with the official presentation of the registration certificate recognizing Bogolan as a Protected Geographical Indication. The ceremony, held on Thursday at the Radisson Collection Hotel in
title_en: Mali Secures Geographic Indication for Bogolan, Strengthening Protection of Textile Heritage
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali has taken a major step in safeguarding its cultural heritage with the official presentation of the registration certificate recognizing Bogolan as a Protected Geographical Indication. The ceremony, held on Thursday at the Radisson Collection Hotel in
body_en:
Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Mali has taken a major step in safeguarding its cultural heritage with the official presentation of the registration certificate recognizing Bogolan as a Protected Geographical Indication.
The ceremony, held on Thursday at the Radisson Collection Hotel in Bamako, formally marked the international recognition of Malian Bogolan as a protected textile heritage product.
The event was presided over by the Minister of Industry and Trade, Moussa Alassane Diallo, in the presence of several government officials, including the Minister of Crafts, Culture, Hospitality and Tourism, Mamou Daffé, and the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye.
Also in attendance was the Director General of the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI), Denis Loukou Bohoussou, alongside local authorities from Bamako’s 4th district and other institutional and cultural stakeholders.
The recognition of Bogolan as a Protected Geographical Indication is expected to enhance its legal protection, preserve traditional know-how, and strengthen its value on international markets. It also aims to support local artisans and promote the textile as a symbol of Mali’s cultural identity and creative industry potential.
Officials emphasized that this certification represents not only a cultural achievement but also an economic opportunity, positioning Malian craftsmanship more firmly within global value chains while protecting it from imitation and misuse.
The initiative reflects broader national efforts to promote cultural industries as drivers of sustainable development and economic diversification.

Bamako, April 21, 2026 - Mali and Ghana have taken a significant step toward strengthening regional trade links with the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the Malian Shippers’ Council and the Ghana Shippers Authority.
The agreement was concluded in Bamako following a two-day working visit by a Ghanaian delegation, during which both parties held discussions focused on improving cooperation in transport and logistics.
The memorandum establishes a framework for bilateral collaboration aimed at enhancing the efficiency of the transport chain along the Ghana-Mali corridor, a key route for trade between the two countries.
Under the agreement, both institutions committed to a series of measures designed to facilitate smoother movement of goods and improve coordination among stakeholders. These include the exchange of information related to international trade, the conduct of joint studies on shared priorities, and mutual support for transport operators and users in both countries.
The partners also agreed to work together to ensure fair access to goods for carriers, in line with existing regulations, and to develop effective monitoring systems for freight transport along the corridor.
Officials say the initiative is expected to strengthen trade flows, reduce logistical bottlenecks, and support economic integration between Mali and Ghana.
The agreement reflects ongoing efforts by West African countries to improve connectivity and streamline cross-border trade as part of broader regional integration strategies.

body_en:
Bamako, April 21, 2026 - Mali is advancing discussions on the future of its health financing strategy as the Minister of Health and Social Development, Assa Badiallo Touré, held talks with a delegation from the Global Fund during a working visit to the country.
The meeting took place within the framework of the national dialogue on the upcoming funding cycle, bringing together key stakeholders to define priorities for continued support to Mali’s health sector.
Discussions focused on several strategic orientations, including the transition toward a more integrated financing approach, improvements in program performance, and the strengthening of the overall health system.
Members of the Global Fund delegation welcomed progress made in recent years, particularly in the absorption of allocated resources and the implementation of health programs. However, they also stressed the importance of enhancing planning mechanisms to ensure greater efficiency and impact.
Minister Touré expressed appreciation for the Global Fund’s sustained commitment to Mali, highlighting its critical role in supporting national health initiatives. She noted that the partnership has contributed to measurable progress and encouraging outcomes across key health indicators.
The exchange reflects ongoing efforts by Malian authorities and international partners to build a more resilient and effective health system capable of addressing current and future public health challenges.

title: Mali-China Health Cooperation: Joint Laboratory Project Targets Emerging Diseases
excerpt: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Mali is strengthening its scientific and health cooperation with China through a new joint laboratory initiative aimed at combating emerging infectious diseases. The Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development took part on Tuesday i
title_en: Mali-China Health Cooperation: Joint Laboratory Project Targets Emerging Diseases
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Mali is strengthening its scientific and health cooperation with China through a new joint laboratory initiative aimed at combating emerging infectious diseases. The Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development took part on Tuesday i
body_en:
Bamako, April 14, 2026 - Mali is strengthening its scientific and health cooperation with China through a new joint laboratory initiative aimed at combating emerging infectious diseases.
The Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development took part on Tuesday in the official presentation of the project, which brings together Malian and Chinese expertise in research and public health response.
The initiative is being jointly implemented by the Charles Mérieux Center for Infectious Diseases in Mali and the Institute of Pathogen Biology under the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences. The partnership reflects a shared commitment to advancing scientific collaboration in the face of increasingly complex global health threats.
Titled the “Sino-Malian Joint Laboratory Project for Combating Emerging Infectious Diseases,” the program is designed to enhance Mali’s national capacities in key areas, including biomedical research, disease diagnostics, and rapid response mechanisms.
The project will run over a three-year period and is funded by a strategic research and diagnostics program under China’s Ministry of Science and Technology, underscoring Beijing’s growing involvement in health cooperation initiatives across Africa.
In a separate development, regional governance issues were also in focus as Mali’s Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga held discussions with the President of Niger’s National Communication Observatory. The meeting addressed regulatory frameworks for media within the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), highlighting ongoing efforts to harmonize communication policies across member countries.
Together, these developments illustrate Mali’s dual approach of strengthening international scientific partnerships while actively engaging in regional coordination on governance and information management.

excerpt: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Academic cooperation between Mali and Iran was reinforced on Thursday as the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye, received Mr. Moustapha Nobacht, Rector of Al-Moustapha University of Iran based in Mali. The meet
title_en: Mali-Iran Academic Cooperation Strengthens Through High-Level University Engagement
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Academic cooperation between Mali and Iran was reinforced on Thursday as the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye, received Mr. Moustapha Nobacht, Rector of Al-Moustapha University of Iran based in Mali. The meet
body_en:
Bamako, April 16, 2026 - Academic cooperation between Mali and Iran was reinforced on Thursday as the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye, received Mr. Moustapha Nobacht, Rector of Al-Moustapha University of Iran based in Mali.
The meeting took place in a cordial atmosphere and forms part of ongoing efforts to deepen educational and scientific relations between the two countries.
During the discussions, the Rector expressed satisfaction with his experience in Mali, noting that he felt “as at home as in Iran.” He also reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to supporting Mali’s higher education priorities and invited the minister to specify national training needs in order to better align academic programs with local demands.
Mr. Nobacht further emphasized the university’s readiness to respond swiftly to Mali’s academic and scientific capacity-building requirements.
The exchange also touched on broader international developments. Minister Kansaye, speaking on behalf of the Malian academic community, conveyed condolences over recent human losses in Iran, including prominent public figures, scientists, and students.
He also paid tribute to the cooperation between Mali and Iran, particularly in the field of scientific training, describing it as a positive example of South-South academic partnership.
The meeting reflects Mali’s continued strategy of expanding university cooperation frameworks to strengthen skills development and scientific research through international collaboration.

body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - Efforts to promote national unity and peaceful coexistence were highlighted on Monday as the Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship, and Customs, Dr. Mahamadou Koné, received a delegation from the National Bureau of the High Islamic Council of Mali.
The delegation, led by the Council’s Eighth Vice-President, Sheikh Mohamed Maki Bah, met with the minister to present preparations for an upcoming major religious gathering dedicated to strengthening unity and reconciliation among Muslims.
According to the delegation, the event is scheduled for May 2, 2026, at the Palace of Culture in Bamako. It will bring together religious leaders from across the country to reflect on issues related to national cohesion, social harmony, and peaceful coexistence among Malian communities.
The initiative is part of broader efforts by religious and state authorities to reinforce dialogue and solidarity, particularly in a context where social unity is considered essential for national stability.
Minister Koné welcomed the initiative and reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement with religious institutions in promoting shared values of peace, tolerance, and unity across the country.

body_en:
Bamako, April 14, 2026 - The promotion of cultural heritage and national reconciliation was highlighted on Tuesday as the Minister of Crafts, Culture, Hospitality and Tourism, Mamou Daffé, received a delegation from the organizing committee of the Bambouck Festival in Sadiola.
Led by promoter Moro Macalou, the delegation presented preparations for the festival’s sixth edition, scheduled to take place from May 14 to 24, 2026, in Sadiola, located in Mali’s Kayes region.
Organized by the Paridiola Association, a socio-cultural organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the cultural, artistic, and historical heritage of Bambouck, the festival has established itself as a key platform for cultural expression in the region.
The initiative aims not only to showcase local traditions and artistic creativity but also to strengthen peace, social cohesion, and national reconciliation through a series of cultural, educational, and community-based activities.
Minister Daffé welcomed the presentation and commended the organizers for their commitment to promoting Mali’s cultural diversity. He emphasized the importance of such initiatives in reinforcing unity and fostering dialogue among communities through culture.
The upcoming edition is expected to bring together artists, cultural actors, and local communities in a celebration of shared heritage and collective identity.

title_en: Bamako Hosts Opening of 6th FIMAK Festival, Celebrating Mandingue Music and Cultural Unity
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The banks of the Niger River, at the Amadou Hampâté Bâ Cultural Center, provided the backdrop on Monday for the opening ceremony of the 6th edition of the Kéla International Mandingue Music Festival (FIMAK), a major cultural event dedicated to Mandé herit
body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The banks of the Niger River, at the Amadou Hampâté Bâ Cultural Center, provided the backdrop on Monday for the opening ceremony of the 6th edition of the Kéla International Mandingue Music Festival (FIMAK), a major cultural event dedicated to Mandé heritage.
The ceremony was presided over by the Minister of Crafts, Culture, Hospitality and Tourism, Mamou Daffé, represented by his Special Advisor, Adama Koïté. The festival is organized by Kaïra Ménagement Global and seeks to promote artistic diversity while showcasing Mali’s rich cultural heritage, particularly Mandingue music traditions.
This year’s edition is held under the theme “The Role of Mandé in Stabilizing the Country,” highlighting the contribution of culture as a driver of peace, stability, and social cohesion.
The program features a wide range of activities, including traditional music performances, exhibitions, culinary showcases, training sessions, workshops, and artistic competitions. These events aim to bring together artists, cultural actors, and the public in a shared celebration of heritage and creativity.
Scheduled to run until April 19, the festival continues to position itself as a key platform for cultural exchange and the promotion of Mali’s artistic identity, while reinforcing the role of culture in fostering unity and dialogue among communities.

title: Girls’ Education in Mali: PASCOFI Project Concludes After Five Years of Impact
excerpt: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The Project to Support Girls’ Education in Mali (PASCOFI), a major initiative aimed at reducing gender disparities in schooling and improving access to quality education in conflict-affected areas, has officially concluded after five years of implementati
title_en: Girls’ Education in Mali: PASCOFI Project Concludes After Five Years of Impact
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The Project to Support Girls’ Education in Mali (PASCOFI), a major initiative aimed at reducing gender disparities in schooling and improving access to quality education in conflict-affected areas, has officially concluded after five years of implementati
body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The Project to Support Girls’ Education in Mali (PASCOFI), a major initiative aimed at reducing gender disparities in schooling and improving access to quality education in conflict-affected areas, has officially concluded after five years of implementation.
The closing workshop was opened on Monday in Bamako at the Azalaï Salam Hotel under the chairmanship of the National Director of Basic Education, Issoufi Arbert Bédari Touré.
Launched in 2021, PASCOFI was designed to strengthen girls’ access to education and improve learning conditions in vulnerable regions, particularly in Ségou, Mopti, and Bandiagara, areas significantly affected by insecurity and displacement.
The project was initiated by World University Service Canada (WUSC) and funded by Global Affairs Canada, reflecting a broader commitment to supporting inclusive education and resilience in fragile contexts.
Over its five-year period, PASCOFI adopted a conflict-sensitive and context-adapted approach to promote equal access to education for children aged 7 to 12. It focused on strengthening both teaching capacity and school infrastructure, while supporting community engagement around girls’ schooling.

title: Education Reform in Mali: Ministers Outline Sovereignty-Driven Vision to Youth Leaders
excerpt: Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s education authorities have set out an ambitious reform agenda placing education at the heart of national sovereignty, during an exchange with the fifth cohort of the School of Citizenship. The session brought together the Minister of National Educa
title_en: Education Reform in Mali: Ministers Outline Sovereignty-Driven Vision to Youth Leaders
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s education authorities have set out an ambitious reform agenda placing education at the heart of national sovereignty, during an exchange with the fifth cohort of the School of Citizenship. The session brought together the Minister of National Educa
body_en:
Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali’s education authorities have set out an ambitious reform agenda placing education at the heart of national sovereignty, during an exchange with the fifth cohort of the School of Citizenship.
The session brought together the Minister of National Education, Amadou Sy Savane, and the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Professor Bouréma Kansaye, in a dialogue moderated by the Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Education and Citizenship Development.
Addressing young participants from Mali and the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), both ministers emphasized the strategic role of education in shaping the country’s future and reinforcing state sovereignty.
Minister Sy Savane described education as a “central strategic lever” for transformation, outlining a reform approach based on three key pillars: strengthening civic values and ethics, improving the quality of learning, and upgrading the school environment.
Professor Kansaye provided historical context, recalling that Mali had no universities at independence in 1960 before the reforms initiated in 1962 laid the foundation for the country’s higher education system. He highlighted the emergence of major national institutions that have since played a central role in training generations of professionals.
He noted that Mali’s higher education sector has since undergone significant expansion, now comprising 10 public universities across the country and more than 200 private institutions, alongside specialized centers of excellence such as the Ahmed Baba Institute in Timbuktu.
Beyond this quantitative growth, the minister stressed the need to focus on quality, relevance, and alignment with national development priorities, particularly in a context marked by evolving economic and social challenges.
The exchange underscored the government’s intention to place education at the core of its reform agenda, linking it directly to citizenship, national identity, and long-term development objectives.

title: Mali Signs Performance Contracts to Strengthen Hospital Governance and Care Quality
excerpt: Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali has taken a significant step toward improving the performance of its healthcare system with the introduction of performance contracts between the State and public health facilities. The signing ceremony, presided over by the Minister of Health and So
title_en: Mali Signs Performance Contracts to Strengthen Hospital Governance and Care Quality
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali has taken a significant step toward improving the performance of its healthcare system with the introduction of performance contracts between the State and public health facilities. The signing ceremony, presided over by the Minister of Health and So
body_en:
Bamako, April 20, 2026 - Mali has taken a significant step toward improving the performance of its healthcare system with the introduction of performance contracts between the State and public health facilities.
The signing ceremony, presided over by the Minister of Health and Social Development, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, formalizes a new framework aimed at enhancing hospital governance, accountability, and service delivery.
Under these agreements, healthcare facilities commit to specific performance targets related to the quality of care, management efficiency, and financial transparency. The contracts will run for a one-year period and will be monitored and evaluated by the National Hospital Evaluation Agency (ANEH).
Officials say the initiative is designed to reinforce results-based management within the health sector, ensuring that institutions are better equipped to meet the needs of the population.
The ceremony also featured the official handover of logistical resources to support healthcare delivery in the field. A total of 27 vehicles, including ambulances, along with 121 motorcycles, were distributed to strengthen operational capacity, particularly in remote and underserved areas.
The acquisition of this equipment was financed through the national budget, with additional support from the African Development Bank (AfDB) and the Vaccine Alliance (GAVI).
Authorities подчеркнули that these combined efforts aim to improve access to healthcare services while promoting efficiency and accountability across the system, as Mali continues its broader reforms in the health sector.

title: Sahel Displacement Cooperation: Mali, Burkina Faso, and UNHCR Renew Efforts on Refugee Repatriation
excerpt: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The 14th session of the Tripartite Commission between Mali, Burkina Faso, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) opened on Monday at the Salam Hotel in Bamako, focusing on coordinated responses to forced displacement in the Sahel. B
title_en: Sahel Displacement Cooperation: Mali, Burkina Faso, and UNHCR Renew Efforts on Refugee Repatriation
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The 14th session of the Tripartite Commission between Mali, Burkina Faso, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) opened on Monday at the Salam Hotel in Bamako, focusing on coordinated responses to forced displacement in the Sahel. B
body_en:
Bamako, April 13, 2026 - The 14th session of the Tripartite Commission between Mali, Burkina Faso, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) opened on Monday at the Salam Hotel in Bamako, focusing on coordinated responses to forced displacement in the Sahel.
Building on the outcomes of the previous session held in Ouagadougou, the meeting aims to strengthen cooperation between the three parties to facilitate the voluntary repatriation of Malian refugees residing in Burkina Faso, as well as Burkinabe refugees hosted in Mali.
The discussions reaffirmed the shared commitment of the two countries and UNHCR to develop durable solutions to displacement challenges affecting the sub-region, including voluntary return, local integration, and enhanced protection mechanisms for vulnerable populations.
According to figures presented by the UNHCR representative for Mali and Burkina Faso, Mali currently hosts more than 291,000 refugees and asylum seekers of various nationalities. This includes approximately 200,000 Burkinabe nationals and around 70,000 Malian displaced persons and returnees.
At the same time, more than 336,000 Malians are registered as refugees outside Burkina Faso, underscoring the scale of cross-border displacement in the region.
The Tripartite Commission remains a key platform for regional coordination, aimed at addressing humanitarian needs while promoting stability and cooperation between neighboring states.
Defense Infrastructure: Foundation Laid for New Military Camp in Dioïla
Dioïla, April 16, 2026 - In a separate development aimed at strengthening national security infrastructure, Mali has launched construction work on a new military installation in the Banico region.
The Minister of State, Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs, Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, officially laid the foundation stone for the future Dioïla military camp on Thursday.
The ceremony marks a significant step in enhancing the operational capacity of the Malian Armed Forces, particularly in strategic areas of the country.
Authorities say the new facility is expected to improve military readiness, reinforce territorial coverage, and support ongoing efforts to strengthen national defense capabilities.

body_en:
Mopti Region, April 16, 2026 - A Malian army patrol operating between Tenenkou and Djondjogori was reportedly targeted on Thursday by an improvised explosive device, in an incident claimed by the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM).
The attack is the second reported security incident in the same area within a single day, reflecting a renewed escalation of tensions in the central region of the country.
According to local and military sources, the repeated incidents point to a deterioration of the fragile security environment in Mopti, an area that has experienced persistent armed activity in recent years.
Preliminary assessments suggest that the latest developments may signal the end of a period of relative calm previously observed between Malian authorities and armed groups operating in the region. This has raised concerns about a possible return to intensified military operations.
Security forces are continuing operations in the area, while investigations are underway to assess the extent of the damage and the circumstances surrounding the attack.

title: Tensions Persist on the Mauritanian-Malian Border Amid Military Movements and Territorial Disputes

title_en: Tensions Persist on the Mauritanian-Malian Border Amid Military Movements and Territorial Disputes
excerpt_en: Border Region (Mali-Mauritania), April 2026 - A series of incidents along the Mauritanian-Malian border since early April have heightened tensions between the two countries, amid overlapping territorial claims, military movements, and diplomatic reactions. The situation has been
body_en:
Border Region (Mali-Mauritania), April 2026 - A series of incidents along the Mauritanian-Malian border since early April have heightened tensions between the two countries, amid overlapping territorial claims, military movements, and diplomatic reactions.
The situation has been particularly tense in the Hodh El Gharbi region of Mauritania and adjacent areas near the poorly demarcated border zone, where both sides have reported increased military presence.
On April 11, local sources reported that Malian army units, reportedly accompanied by elements of the Africa Corps, entered villages in the Kobeni area that are administratively linked to Mauritania. The patrols allegedly moved through several settlements, informing residents that the territory belonged to Mali. No clashes or casualties were reported during the incursion.
Mauritanian political figures quickly reacted. Local deputies condemned the movements while reaffirming the population’s attachment to their land. At the same time, calls were made for a definitive resolution of border demarcation, with warnings about the risk of further escalation.
Mauritanian regional authorities maintained that some of the contested villages fall within Malian territory according to official cartographic references, while also stressing their responsibility to protect Mauritanian citizens living in the area. Military officials further stated that national forces are capable of responding firmly to any threat against civilians.
In a parallel statement, the Mauritanian army identified several villages involved in the dispute and confirmed that the situation was being closely monitored.
Tensions escalated again on April 14, when a large Malian military convoy reportedly entered areas near Ketoul and Iklib Agour. The force is said to have dismantled telecommunications infrastructure, including transmission towers and equipment, citing interference with drone operations and affirming that the installations were located within Malian territory.
Following the operation, the convoy withdrew toward Nioro in Mali. Mauritanian National Guard units subsequently intercepted the force inside Malian territory, before being joined by special forces from Atwil, resulting in a standoff without direct confrontation.
Negotiations on the ground focused on the purpose of the operation, with Malian officers stating it was aimed at neutralizing technical interference affecting military drones. Mauritanian representatives, however, emphasized that the dismantled infrastructure served local civilian populations and required prior coordination.
The situation was eventually de-escalated after Mauritanian authorities authorized the withdrawal of their forces, following assurances that similar incidents would not be repeated. Malian units also retreated from the area.
While the confrontation ended without armed clashes, the sequence of events has further exposed long-standing sensitivities over border delimitation and highlighted the fragility of security cooperation in the region.

title: Mali Reports Major Counterterrorism Strikes and Coordinated Nationwide Attacks, AES Reaffirms Solidarity
excerpt: Bamako, April 22-25, 2026 - Mali’s security situation saw a rapid escalation this week, marked by counterterrorism airstrikes and coordinated attacks across multiple cities, prompting strong responses from both national authorities and the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). On
title_en: Mali Reports Major Counterterrorism Strikes and Coordinated Nationwide Attacks, AES Reaffirms Solidarity
excerpt_en: Bamako, April 22-25, 2026 - Mali’s security situation saw a rapid escalation this week, marked by counterterrorism airstrikes and coordinated attacks across multiple cities, prompting strong responses from both national authorities and the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). On
body_en:
Bamako, April 22-25, 2026 - Mali’s security situation saw a rapid escalation this week, marked by counterterrorism airstrikes and coordinated attacks across multiple cities, prompting strong responses from both national authorities and the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).
On April 22, the General Staff of the Armed Forces announced that surveillance operations in the Koulikoro region led to the detection of a convoy of around 40 motorcycles believed to belong to armed groups moving through the Faya classified forest, south of Zantiguila.
Military aircraft were deployed and conducted targeted strikes against the convoy. According to the army, the operation resulted in the neutralization of more than 70 combatants and the destruction of their equipment. The General Staff stated that follow-up operations were ongoing across the country to track remaining armed elements.
Coordinated nationwide attacks repelled
On April 25, 2026, the Transitional Government reported that multiple coordinated attacks targeted several strategic locations, including Kati, Sévaré, Gao, Kidal, and Bamako.
Authorities said the assaults caused 16 injuries among civilians and military personnel and resulted in limited material damage. The government stated that the attacks were rapidly repelled by the Malian Armed and Security Forces, who neutralized several attackers and restored control in all affected areas.
Officials praised the “promptness and professionalism” of the security forces and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to pursuing those responsible.
The population was urged to remain calm and vigilant, report suspicious activity, and rely on official communication channels.
AES expresses solidarity and condemnation
In a parallel statement, the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) strongly condemned the attacks, describing them as coordinated and premeditated attempts to destabilize Mali and the broader Sahel region.
The AES statement characterized the incidents as part of a wider effort targeting the confederal dynamic and accused hostile actors of seeking to undermine the sovereignty and stability of member states.
The confederation praised the response of the Malian Armed Forces, describing their actions as professional and decisive in repelling the assaults.
It also extended condolences to the families of victims and wished a speedy recovery to the injured, while reaffirming “total and fraternal solidarity” with the Malian authorities.
The AES further emphasized that such attacks would not weaken the determination of Sahel states to pursue their sovereignty, security, and integration agenda, and expressed gratitude to partners who have shown support in the aftermath of the incidents.
Overall, the events highlight a sharply heightened security environment in Mali, combining sustained counterterrorism operations with large-scale urban and regional attacks, amid growing regional diplomatic and security mobilization.

title: Kidal and Gao Situation: Competing Claims Emerge Amid Ongoing Security Operations
excerpt: April 25, 2026 - The security situation in northern Mali has become increasingly complex following competing statements from armed actors and the Malian Armed Forces regarding developments in Kidal and Gao. A statement attributed to the Front for the Liberation of Azawad (FLA) an
title_en: Kidal and Gao Situation: Competing Claims Emerge Amid Ongoing Security Operations
excerpt_en: April 25, 2026 - The security situation in northern Mali has become increasingly complex following competing statements from armed actors and the Malian Armed Forces regarding developments in Kidal and Gao. A statement attributed to the Front for the Liberation of Azawad (FLA) an
body_en:
April 25, 2026 - The security situation in northern Mali has become increasingly complex following competing statements from armed actors and the Malian Armed Forces regarding developments in Kidal and Gao.
A statement attributed to the Front for the Liberation of Azawad (FLA) announced that its forces had taken control of the city of Kidal early in the morning of April 25. The group claimed that only limited resistance remained in specific areas, including what it described as entrenched positions held by Malian soldiers and foreign personnel.
The FLA further stated that its operations were being conducted in coordination with other armed actors and framed its actions as part of a broader strategy aimed at what it described as territorial “liberation” and the creation of conditions for the return of displaced populations. The group also made political statements calling for international attention and a reassessment of foreign support to Mali’s transitional authorities.
The claims could not be independently verified, and authorities in Bamako have not confirmed any loss of control over Kidal or Gao.
Malian Army maintains control and continues operations
In response, the General Staff of the Armed Forces (EMGA) issued a statement affirming that military operations are ongoing in Kidal, Kati, and other areas following coordinated attacks earlier in the day.
The army described the incidents as part of a broader attempt to destabilize the country’s defense system and reiterated that such actions would not go unanswered.
Military authorities confirmed that security forces remain fully mobilized, with heightened alert levels nationwide. Measures include reinforced checkpoints, intensified patrols, and curfew enforcement in sensitive areas.
The General Staff emphasized that the Malian Armed Forces remain committed to defending national territory and restoring security, while commending the responsiveness of deployed units and the cooperation of civilian populations.
Situation remains fluid
The contrasting narratives highlight the volatility of the security environment in northern Mali, where military operations, armed group activity, and contested territorial control continue to overlap.
Authorities have urged calm and vigilance, while reinforcing reliance on official communications as operations continue across multiple regions.

title: Coordinated Multi-City Offensive and Claims of Territorial Gains Across Mali
excerpt: April 25, 2026 - A series of coordinated attacks and offensives were reported across multiple cities in Mali and the broader Azawad area, marking one of the most extensive and simultaneous security escalations in recent years. According to claims attributed to armed groups operat
title_en: Coordinated Multi-City Offensive and Claims of Territorial Gains Across Mali
excerpt_en: April 25, 2026 - A series of coordinated attacks and offensives were reported across multiple cities in Mali and the broader Azawad area, marking one of the most extensive and simultaneous security escalations in recent years. According to claims attributed to armed groups operat
body_en:
April 25, 2026 - A series of coordinated attacks and offensives were reported across multiple cities in Mali and the broader Azawad area, marking one of the most extensive and simultaneous security escalations in recent years.
According to claims attributed to armed groups operating in coordination, including Azawad forces and the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM), a multi-front operation was launched targeting strategic locations in Kidal, Gao, Sévaré, Mopti, and the outskirts of Bamako.
In Kidal, the group claimed that the city was fully recaptured following rapid fighting, ending a presence that had been established since November 2023. The former MINUSMA base was reportedly surrounded for several hours before foreign military personnel allegedly withdrew without resistance. These claims have not been independently verified.
In Sévaré, the situation was described as particularly intense, with reports of prolonged fighting that allegedly resulted in the takeover of the city and nearby military installations, along with the seizure of weapons and equipment.
In the Gao region, the same sources reported the capture of several strategic positions, including military installations and sites within and around the city. The attackers are said to have withdrawn afterward with military equipment.
In parallel, attacks were also reported in and around Bamako, including targeted operations near Sénou Airport, the Sirakoro area, and the city of Kati. These incidents were described as part of a broader escalation affecting both central and southern parts of the country.
Official confirmation from Malian authorities regarding territorial losses has not been provided, and the situation remains highly contested, with conflicting narratives emerging from different actors involved in the conflict.
The events underscore a rapidly evolving and highly volatile security landscape, with multiple simultaneous engagements across several regions of the country.

title: Reports of Military Withdrawals and High-Level Political Uncertainty Following Offensive
excerpt: April 26, 2026 - The aftermath of the coordinated offensive launched across Mali continued to unfold, with significant developments reported in both northern and central regions, alongside major political uncertainty in Bamako. In Kidal, reports indicated that negotiations led to
title_en: Reports of Military Withdrawals and High-Level Political Uncertainty Following Offensive
excerpt_en: April 26, 2026 - The aftermath of the coordinated offensive launched across Mali continued to unfold, with significant developments reported in both northern and central regions, alongside major political uncertainty in Bamako. In Kidal, reports indicated that negotiations led to
body_en:
April 26, 2026 - The aftermath of the coordinated offensive launched across Mali continued to unfold, with significant developments reported in both northern and central regions, alongside major political uncertainty in Bamako.
In Kidal, reports indicated that negotiations led to the opening of a secure corridor allowing the withdrawal of Malian forces and foreign military personnel associated with them. According to these accounts, the evacuation took place without direct confrontation, although heavy military equipment and vehicles were reportedly left behind. These claims have not been independently verified by official sources.
In parallel, Malian authorities confirmed the death of the Minister of State, Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs, Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, following an attack on his residence in Bamako. The attack also reportedly resulted in the deaths of members of his family.
Authorities have not released detailed information on the circumstances surrounding the incident, and security conditions in the capital remain tense.
In addition, uncertainty surrounds the status of transitional President General Assimi Goïta, who has not made any public appearance since the escalation of attacks. No official communication has clarified his whereabouts at this stage.
These developments come amid a rapidly evolving security and political situation, with competing reports and limited verified information, reflecting a period of heightened instability across multiple regions of the country.

title_en: Multiple Withdrawals and Renewed Fighting Across Mali Amid Escalating Insecurity
excerpt_en: April 27, 2026 - The security situation in Mali further deteriorated as multiple withdrawals, territorial changes, and renewed clashes were reported across several regions, alongside fresh incidents in the capital Bamako. In northern Mali, reports indicated the withdrawal of Mali
body_en:
April 27, 2026 - The security situation in Mali further deteriorated as multiple withdrawals, territorial changes, and renewed clashes were reported across several regions, alongside fresh incidents in the capital Bamako.
In northern Mali, reports indicated the withdrawal of Malian armed forces and associated foreign personnel from several towns across the Kidal, Gao, and Timbuktu regions. The affected localities reportedly included Adjelhoc and Tessalit in Kidal, Labbezanga, Tessit, and Intahaka in Gao, as well as Ber in Timbuktu.
According to conflicting field accounts, several of these areas subsequently came under the influence of armed groups, including the Azawad Liberation Front and the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM), although control of certain locations-particularly Labbezanga-remained contested.
In the Ménaka region, heavy clashes were also reported between the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISS) and Malian forces supported by allied partners and local militias. Armed confrontations reportedly reached the vicinity of the regional governor’s headquarters before nightfall, though casualty figures have not yet been confirmed.
Meanwhile, the capital Bamako experienced renewed tension in the evening, with residents reporting multiple loud explosions followed by intense gunfire around 10:30 p.m. Military helicopters and drones were deployed over the city as security forces responded to the incidents and searched for those involved.
The simultaneous incidents across several regions highlight a rapidly evolving and highly unstable security environment, with multiple armed actors active and territorial control remaining contested in several parts of the country.

According to the statement, armed groups identified as the Azawad Liberation Front and Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb launched a coordinated operation early in the morning, allegedly targeting key government and military installations, including the presidential palace in Bamako and administrative centers in cities such as Gao, Kidal, Kita, and Sévaré.
The statement further claimed that foreign fighters and mercenaries were involved in the operations and that advanced weaponry was used during the attacks. These assertions have not been independently verified.
The Africa Corps reported that it maintained control over strategic sites, including airfields and military installations, and played a central role in defending key government positions. It also stated that the attempted offensive was ultimately repelled, preventing what it described as an effort to destabilize the state.
According to figures provided in the statement, the attackers reportedly suffered heavy losses across multiple locations, while acknowledging casualties among its own personnel and reporting ongoing medical evacuation efforts.
The statement also described intense fighting along a wide operational front spanning several thousand kilometers, highlighting the scale and coordination of the attacks as presented by the group.
No independent confirmation of casualty figures or battlefield outcomes has been made available, and Malian authorities have not issued a detailed response addressing the specific claims contained in the statement.
The situation remains highly fluid, with multiple competing narratives emerging from different actors involved in the ongoing conflict.

excerpt_en: April 22, 2026 - Koulikoro Region (Bamako outskirts) Local sources reported that fighters from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) entered the courtyard of a school in the village of Marka-Kongo, located approximately 78 kilometers from Bamako. According to thes
body_en:
April 22, 2026 - Koulikoro Region (Bamako outskirts)
Local sources reported that fighters from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) entered the courtyard of a school in the village of Marka-Kongo, located approximately 78 kilometers from Bamako. According to these accounts, the armed individuals ordered the school to close before leaving the area. No casualties were reported.
April 19-ongoing - Mopti and Sévaré
Residents of Mopti and Sévaré have reported recurring power outages amid an intense heat wave exceeding 40°C. The electricity disruptions have further strained living conditions in the two central Malian cities, with no official explanation immediately confirmed regarding the cause of the outages.
April 22, 2026 - Tessit (Gao Region)
In the Gao region near the Niger border, fighters from the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS) launched a surprise attack on the town of Tessit. Reports indicate that the attackers briefly took control of the military camp before government forces withdrew and later returned with reinforcements, including elements from local militias affiliated with the Movement for the Salvation of Azawad (MSA). The attackers reportedly withdrew, leaving behind two motorcycles.
April 24, 2026 - Gao Region (Hourara area)
The Malian Armed Forces carried out drone strikes in the Hourara area near the Niger border. According to available reports, the operation did not result in casualties or significant material damage.
Conclusion
Mali Faces a Critical Juncture Amid Diplomatic Progress and Escalating Security Crisis
The period from April 12 to 27, 2026, reflects a moment of sharp duality in Mali’s trajectory, marked by notable diplomatic and economic advances alongside a rapid and far-reaching deterioration of the security environment.
On one hand, the transitional authorities pursued an active diplomatic agenda, consolidating and expanding international partnerships through the accreditation of new ambassadors from key partners including the European Union, Ghana, Qatar, and Cuba. This outreach was complemented by deeper regional coordination within the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), particularly in areas such as media regulation, cultural cooperation, and shared sovereignty frameworks.
At the same time, domestic reforms continued to progress in several strategic sectors. The government advanced infrastructure financing through a standardized public-private partnership framework, strengthened protections for cultural heritage through the recognition of Bogolan as a protected geographical indication, and supported increased academic and scientific cooperation with international partners. In parallel, improvements in regional mobility were noted following Morocco’s suspension of electronic travel authorization requirements for Malian citizens.
However, these developments were rapidly overshadowed by a severe escalation in insecurity.
A coordinated multi-city offensive on April 25 marked a turning point, with simultaneous attacks reported across major urban and strategic centers including Bamako, Kidal, Gao, and Sévaré. These events were accompanied by competing claims of territorial control, particularly in northern Mali, where conflicting narratives emerged regarding the situation in Kidal and other key locations.
The crisis was further compounded by reports of high-level political and military instability, including the death of the Minister of Defense, Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, following an attack in the capital, and uncertainty surrounding the public status of the head of state. These developments have intensified perceptions of institutional fragility at a critical moment.
Beyond the core conflict zones, tensions also extended to Mali’s borders, with reported military movements near Mauritania contributing to regional diplomatic strain. At the same time, the detention of humanitarian personnel in Gao added further complexity to an already constrained humanitarian operating environment.
In summary, Mali enters a highly uncertain phase in which diplomatic diversification and institutional reform efforts are being tested by an unprecedented multi-front security crisis. The immediate outlook will depend on the state’s capacity to reassert territorial control, stabilize political leadership, and manage escalating regional and humanitarian pressures, while the broader effectiveness of regional security cooperation mechanisms remains under significant strain.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

In summary, Mali enters a highly uncertain phase in which diplomatic diversification and institutional reform efforts are being tested by an unprecedented multi-front security crisis. The immediate outlook will depend on the state’s capacity to reassert territorial control, stabilize political leadership, and manage escalating regional and humanitarian pressures, while the broader effectiveness of regional security cooperation mechanisms remains under significant strain.

title_en: Rwandan Envoy Presents Credentials to Tunisia, Strengthening Bilateral TiesApril 15, 2026; Umutoni Shakilla has officially presented copies of her credentials to Mohamed Ali Nafti, marking her accreditation as Rwanda’s representative to Tunisia.
excerpt_en: The ceremony, held on April 15, 2026, represents a further step in strengthening diplomatic relations between Rwanda and Tunisia. Ambassador Umutoni, who is based in Rabat, will oversee Rwanda’s diplomatic interests in Tunisia as well as in Mauritania through the Rwandan Embassy
body_en:
The ceremony, held on April 15, 2026, represents a further step in strengthening diplomatic relations between Rwanda and Tunisia. Ambassador Umutoni, who is based in Rabat, will oversee Rwanda’s diplomatic interests in Tunisia as well as in Mauritania through the Rwandan Embassy in Morocco.
Following the presentation, the two officials held discussions focused on enhancing bilateral cooperation and identifying opportunities to deepen collaboration in areas of shared interest.
Rwanda and Tunisia maintain cooperation across several sectors, with particular emphasis on transport. In February 2020, both countries signed an air services agreement during the 33rd Ordinary Session of the African Union in Addis Ababa, allowing airlines from both nations to operate within each other’s airspace.
Tunisia, located in North Africa along the Mediterranean coast, has a population of over 12 million people. Arabic is the official language, and the Tunisian dinar serves as the national currency.
Officials from both countries say continued diplomatic engagement is expected to further consolidate relations and expand cooperation in key sectors.

title_en: Burundi Confirms Death of Communications Minister Gabby Bugaga in Road AccidentApril 16, 2026 ; The Government of Burundi has confirmed the death of the Minister of Communications and Information, Gabby Bugaga, who died in a road accident in the early hours of April 16, 2026, in Bujumbura City.
excerpt_en: The announcement was made by government spokesperson Jérôme Niyonzima, who dismissed speculation surrounding the circumstances of the incident and described the death as an accident. According to official information, the minister’s body was discovered at around 2:00 a.m. inside
body_en:
The announcement was made by government spokesperson Jérôme Niyonzima, who dismissed speculation surrounding the circumstances of the incident and described the death as an accident.
According to official information, the minister’s body was discovered at around 2:00 a.m. inside his vehicle, a Toyota Hilux, parked in a palm grove in the Kivoga area near a roadside in Bujumbura.
Authorities noted that the minister was traveling alone at the time of the incident and was not accompanied by security personnel, a situation considered unusual for a senior government official in Burundi.
“The Republic of Burundi is deeply saddened to inform the public and the international community of the sudden death of Minister Gabby Bugaga, who died in a road accident in the early hours of this morning, April 16, 2026,” Niyonzima said in an official statement.
President Évariste Ndayishimiye expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and to the nation, praising the late minister’s public service.
“May God receive him and reward him for the courage, diligence, and dedication he demonstrated in serving the country,” the president said.
Bugaga had previously built a career in journalism at the national broadcaster RTNB before serving in several public institutions, including the Senate and the National Independent Electoral Commission (CENI). He was appointed Minister of Communications and Information in August 2025.

title_en: United States Urges DRC to Dismantle FDLR, Warns of Possible SanctionsApril 16, 2026 ; The United States has called on the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to urgently dismantle the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), warning that continued inaction could lead to sanctions.
excerpt_en: The message was reiterated on April 15, 2026, by U.S. Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Tammy Bruce, during a United Nations Security Council session focused on peace and stability in the Great Lakes region. The discussion also featured remarks from Rwanda’s
body_en:
The message was reiterated on April 15, 2026, by U.S. Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Tammy Bruce, during a United Nations Security Council session focused on peace and stability in the Great Lakes region.
The discussion also featured remarks from Rwanda’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, Robert Kayinamura, who stated that the FDLR remains active in eastern DRC and continues to pose a regional security threat. He also linked the group to its historical origins tied to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, calling for its complete dismantlement.
US position on peace commitments
The U.S. delegation emphasized that the DRC must fulfill its commitments under the peace agreement signed with Rwanda in June 2025, which included provisions for dismantling the armed group. Washington noted that implementation has been delayed despite the agreement.
U.S. officials argued that the continued presence of the FDLR contributes to mistrust between parties and fuels instability in eastern Congo.
“The DRC government must honor its commitments and quickly eliminate the FDLR, at least in the areas it controls. Eliminating these long-standing security concerns is essential to ending the cycle of mistrust that has caused war for many years,” Tammy Bruce said.
Ongoing dispute over presence of armed group
The DRC government has previously argued that FDLR elements are not primarily located in areas under its direct control, stating that some are in territories affected by ongoing conflict involving other armed actors in the east.
However, U.S. officials countered that FDLR presence has also been reported in government-controlled areas, reinforcing the need for immediate action.
Warning of possible sanctions
The United States also warned that it is prepared to use available diplomatic and economic measures if parties are seen to be obstructing peace efforts, including the possibility of targeted sanctions.
The statement reflects growing international pressure on actors in the region to accelerate implementation of existing peace commitments as instability persists in eastern DRC.

title: DRC Government Maintains Selective Dialogue Approach Amid Calls for Inclusive Talks
excerpt: Kinshasa April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reaffirmed its position that it will determine which Congolese actors will participate in ongoing peace negotiations, insisting on a selective approach to dialogue aimed at ending long-standing
title_en: DRC Government Maintains Selective Dialogue Approach Amid Calls for Inclusive Talks
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reaffirmed its position that it will determine which Congolese actors will participate in ongoing peace negotiations, insisting on a selective approach to dialogue aimed at ending long-standing
body_en:
Kinshasa April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reaffirmed its position that it will determine which Congolese actors will participate in ongoing peace negotiations, insisting on a selective approach to dialogue aimed at ending long-standing conflict in the country.
Authorities in Kinshasa say the talks are intended to achieve lasting peace, but maintain that participation will not be open to all groups. “The government will select those to talk to and those to leave,” officials have indicated, underscoring their control over the composition of the dialogue process.
This stance comes amid growing calls from religious leaders, civil society actors, and political figures urging President Félix Tshisekedi to initiate a broad-based national dialogue. Church representatives, including pastors from the Catholic and Anglican communities, have stressed that any meaningful peace process should include Congolese from all walks of life, including representatives of armed groups.
However, the government has rejected the inclusion of armed factions in the talks. Religious leaders argue that excluding such actors risks undermining efforts to reach a comprehensive and durable settlement to decades of instability.
At the international level, Angolan President João Lourenço, in his capacity as African Union (AU) chair, also called on President Tshisekedi to integrate representatives of the AFC/M23 movement into the dialogue framework. Kinshasa has declined this recommendation.
On April 16, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya clarified that President Tshisekedi had agreed to engage in discussions with Congolese actors “separated from Kagame,” emphasizing that the government’s priority remains the recovery of territories currently under the control of armed forces.
Muyaya further accused the AFC/M23 and their affiliates of committing crimes against civilians, stating that they would be held accountable. He added that the government seeks to ensure justice and prevent what it describes as a culture of impunity.

title: AFC/M23 Renews Demand for Reopening of Banks in Goma and Bukavu Amid Ongoing Negotiations
excerpt: Goma April 19, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has reiterated its call for the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo to reopen banks in areas under its control, including Goma and Bukavu, and to lift legal and financial sanctions imposed on its senior members. The appeal wa
title_en: AFC/M23 Renews Demand for Reopening of Banks in Goma and Bukavu Amid Ongoing Negotiations
excerpt_en: Goma April 19, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has reiterated its call for the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo to reopen banks in areas under its control, including Goma and Bukavu, and to lift legal and financial sanctions imposed on its senior members. The appeal wa
body_en:
Goma April 19, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has reiterated its call for the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo to reopen banks in areas under its control, including Goma and Bukavu, and to lift legal and financial sanctions imposed on its senior members.
The appeal was restated during ongoing peace talks held in Switzerland from April 13, 2026, where representatives of the coalition and the Congolese government discussed a range of confidence-building measures aimed at reducing tensions in eastern DRC.
Since AFC/M23 took control of Goma in January 2025, the government in Kinshasa has closed all banking institutions in the city, a move intended to weaken the group’s administrative and financial capacity. However, the closure has also had broader economic consequences, affecting civilians and businesses unable to access their deposits or conduct routine transactions.
The coalition argues that restoring banking services in Goma, Bukavu, and other areas under its control is essential for normal economic activity and civilian livelihoods. It has repeatedly urged the government to allow financial institutions to resume operations without restrictions.
AFC/M23 has also called for the lifting of judicial measures against its senior officials, including death sentences and asset seizures imposed by the Congolese authorities.
In parallel, the government delegation has called on AFC/M23 to reopen Goma Airport, a request the coalition has firmly rejected. title: Heineken Confirms Exit From DRC After Four Decades, Citing Security and Operational Risks
excerpt: April 10, 2026 - Dutch brewing company Heineken N.V. has announced its complete withdrawal from the Democratic Republic of the Congo after nearly 40 years of operations, following the sale of its shares in Bralima. In a statement released on April 10, the company confirmed that i
title_en: Heineken Confirms Exit From DRC After Four Decades, Citing Security and Operational Risks
excerpt_en: April 10, 2026 - Dutch brewing company Heineken N.V. has announced its complete withdrawal from the Democratic Republic of the Congo after nearly 40 years of operations, following the sale of its shares in Bralima. In a statement released on April 10, the company confirmed that i
body_en:
April 10, 2026 - Dutch brewing company Heineken N.V. has announced its complete withdrawal from the Democratic Republic of the Congo after nearly 40 years of operations, following the sale of its shares in Bralima.
In a statement released on April 10, the company confirmed that its stake in Bralima had been sold to ELNA Holdings Ltd, marking the end of its long-standing majority ownership that began in 1986.
Bralima, originally founded in 1923 by Belgian investors, has long been one of the leading beverage producers in the country, supplying major urban centers including Kinshasa, Goma, Bukavu, Kisangani, and Lubumbashi.
Heineken said the decision follows a period of heightened insecurity in parts of eastern DRC, where operations had already been temporarily suspended due to clashes between government forces and the AFC/M23 armed coalition. The company had previously transferred management of its eastern operations to a Mauritius-based entity to protect staff and ensure continuity of supply.
The brewer indicated that while it will fully exit the country’s market structure, operations in more stable regions of the DRC had continued until the final divestment process. It added that a return to eastern provinces could remain possible if security conditions improve in the future.
The departure of Heineken marks a significant shift in the DRC’s business landscape, reflecting growing concerns among multinational companies operating in conflict-affected areas.

title: Oman and Rwanda Sign Aviation Cooperation MoU to Boost Air Transport and Infrastructure
excerpt: April 12, 2026 - The Oman Airports Authority has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Rwanda’s Aviation Travel and Logistics (ATL) group to strengthen cooperation in aviation development and related infrastructure projects. The agreement, announced on April 11, 2026, e
title_en: Oman and Rwanda Sign Aviation Cooperation MoU to Boost Air Transport and Infrastructure
excerpt_en: April 12, 2026 - The Oman Airports Authority has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Rwanda’s Aviation Travel and Logistics (ATL) group to strengthen cooperation in aviation development and related infrastructure projects. The agreement, announced on April 11, 2026, e
body_en:
April 12, 2026 - The Oman Airports Authority has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Rwanda’s Aviation Travel and Logistics (ATL) group to strengthen cooperation in aviation development and related infrastructure projects.
The agreement, announced on April 11, 2026, establishes a framework for collaboration between the two parties in areas including airport land development, air transport infrastructure, workforce training, and broader aviation services.
ATL, a Rwandan state-linked aviation and logistics holding company established in 2015, brings together several entities including RwandAir, Airports Company Rwanda Ltd, Akagera Aviation, Rwanda Tours & Events, and Rwanda Links Logistics.
Under the MoU, both sides are expected to explore investment opportunities and technical cooperation aimed at expanding airport capacity and improving operational efficiency.
The partnership comes amid growing aviation ties between the two countries. Oman Air has confirmed plans to launch direct flights to Kigali in June 2026, a move expected to strengthen tourism, trade, and business connectivity between East Africa and the Gulf region.
Officials from both countries say the agreement reflects a shared interest in positioning their aviation sectors as regional hubs, with a focus on infrastructure modernization and skills development.

title: Guinean Students to Be Sent to Rwanda for Science and Technology Training
excerpt: Kigali April 12, 2026 - The Guinean government has announced that students and researchers will be sent to Rwanda to pursue studies in science and technology as part of a new bilateral cooperation initiative aimed at strengthening human capital in key technical fields. The Minist
title_en: Guinean Students to Be Sent to Rwanda for Science and Technology Training
excerpt_en: Kigali April 12, 2026 - The Guinean government has announced that students and researchers will be sent to Rwanda to pursue studies in science and technology as part of a new bilateral cooperation initiative aimed at strengthening human capital in key technical fields. The Minist
body_en:
Kigali April 12, 2026 - The Guinean government has announced that students and researchers will be sent to Rwanda to pursue studies in science and technology as part of a new bilateral cooperation initiative aimed at strengthening human capital in key technical fields.
The Minister of Education and Research of Guinea, Dr. Diaka Sidibé, confirmed the initiative following a working visit to Rwanda on Friday, April 10, 2026, during which discussions were held with senior officials of Rwandan higher education institutions.
During the visit, Dr. Sidibé met with the Chancellor of the University of Rwanda, Assoc. Prof. Didas Kayihura Muganga, as well as the Dean of the Faculty of Science, Prof. Ignace Gatare. The talks focused on expanding educational cooperation between the two countries, in line with existing bilateral agreements aimed at promoting academic exchange and capacity building.
According to the minister, Guinea has expressed readiness to send volunteers and students to the Science and Technology Pilot Center at the University of Rwanda. He emphasized that the initiative forms part of the broader Simandou Academy program, which seeks to strengthen the skills of Guinean students, teachers, and researchers in alignment with the national development vision of President Mamadi Doumbouya.
“During my working visit to Kigali, I was received at the National University of Rwanda, specifically at the College of Science and Technology, accompanied by the Ambassador of Guinea to Rwanda, Soumaïla Savané,” Dr. Sidibé stated. He added that the program is designed to provide targeted training in strategic fields essential to national development.
Rwandan academic authorities reportedly expressed their readiness to host Guinean students, researchers, and postgraduate candidates once the formal cooperation framework is finalized.
The first cohort of Guinean participants is expected to arrive at the beginning of the next academic year. They will pursue studies in disciplines including science, technology, mining, data analysis, engineering, and related fields.
The cooperation between Rwanda and Guinea forms part of a broader partnership covering sectors such as technology, agriculture, investment, services, tourism, energy, and trade.

title: Lawmakers Move to Oust Security Minister Over Rising Insecurity
excerpt: Kinshasa April 14, 2026 - A group of deputies in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has initiated proceedings aimed at the dismissal of the Minister of Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, citing what they describe as a continued deterioration of public safety across the count
title_en: Lawmakers Move to Oust Security Minister Over Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 14, 2026 - A group of deputies in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has initiated proceedings aimed at the dismissal of the Minister of Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, citing what they describe as a continued deterioration of public safety across the count
body_en:
Kinshasa April 14, 2026 - A group of deputies in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has initiated proceedings aimed at the dismissal of the Minister of Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, citing what they describe as a continued deterioration of public safety across the country.
The initiative, led by Laddy Yangotikala, a Member of Parliament from Kisangani and a member of the ruling coalition Union Sacrée, accuses the minister of failing to contain rising crime levels, particularly in Kinshasa and other major urban centers.
Speaking before his parliamentary colleagues, Yangotikala said insecurity had become widespread and persistent, with armed robberies occurring even in broad daylight.
“Whether you live in Kinshasa or elsewhere, armed robberies are being committed in broad daylight. Do we know whether investigations are being conducted? Do we know whether those arrested are being prosecuted? Day after day, Congolese citizens continue to live in insecurity. Can we remain silent simply because we are members of the Union Sacrée? No,” he stated.
The lawmaker expressed a loss of confidence in Minister Shabani and called for his resignation within 48 hours following April 13, 2026, urging him to submit his resignation to President Félix Tshisekedi.
According to parliamentary sources, the motion is expected to be formally debated in the National Assembly, where lawmakers will decide whether to support the initiative calling for the minister’s removal or allow him to remain in office.
Yangotikala has continued to mobilize support among his colleagues and confirmed that he has already secured more than 50 signatures backing the proposal, signaling growing momentum behind the push within the legislature.
